author: Unknown
title: Iran has executed at least 28 women since start of 2026
content:
At least 28 women have been executed in Iran since the beginning of 2026. The Women’s Committee of the National Council of Resistance of Iran (WCNCRI) published a report on the execution of women in the country.




The report said the most recently recorded execution was that of Mahrokh Mirzaei on 26 September. It stated that Mirzaei had killed her husband in self-defence after being subjected to violence during their marriage: “Mahrokh Mirzaei experienced constant disputes and tensions with her husband throughout their four-year marriage. Over time, these circumstances affected her mental and psychological health, leading to serious problems. She was arrested four years ago on charges of killing her husband and was sentenced to death. With the execution of Mahrokh Mirzaei, the number of women executed in Iranian prisons since the beginning of 2026 has reached at least 28.”




The report also stated that at least 356 women had been executed by the regime since 2007. It said: “Most of the women executed by the Iranian regime were themselves victims of domestic violence and discriminatory family laws. A significant number had acted in self-defence. Since Masoud Pezeshkian took office, the clerical regime has executed 4,110 prisoners, including 116 women.”

title: Protest in Hamburg against police raid on Kurdish Community Center in Hanover
content:
A protest was held in Hamburg against the police raid on the Democratic Kurdish Community Center (DKTM) in Hanover. Kurds and people from left-wing and antifascist groups gathered outside the autonomous center Rote Flora in the Sternschanze district and expressed solidarity with those affected by the raid.




The protest was directed against the police operation last weekend, during which a Kurdish commemoration event in Hanover was prevented and the community center was subsequently stormed by a large police contingent. Numerous people present were detained for hours.




















At the rally, Fatma Doğan, co-chair of the Hamburg DKTM, criticized the police operation as “unlawful and unacceptable.” She said it was unacceptable for such a raid to take place at a time when the PKK has ended its armed struggle and a peaceful solution to the Kurdistan question is being discussed.




Doğan recalled the heavy sacrifices made over decades of the Kurdish freedom struggle. She said that attempts to criminalize the commemoration of the martyrs could not prevent Kurdish society from preserving their memory. “Until the last drop of our blood, we will follow the path of our martyrs,” she said.




At the same time, Doğan stated that police pressure and criminalization could not prevent the Kurdish population’s struggle for freedom and expressed solidarity with those affected in H

title: Long-term political prisoner denied permission to attend his father’s funeral
content:
Political prisoner Aydın Altığ, who has been imprisoned in Turkey for 30 years, has been denied permission to attend the funeral of his late father. The prison administration justified the refusal by stating that Altığ is subject to a “strict prison regime.”




Mahmut Altığ, the prisoner’s father, died on September 29. His son subsequently applied for permission to attend the funeral. Altığ is currently being held in a high-security prison in Kırşehir, central Anatolia.




Aydın Altığ was arrested at the age of 17 in the southern Turkish province of Mersin and, according to the Human Rights Association (İHD), was severely tortured. A State Security Court (DGM) in Adana subsequently sentenced the Kurdish man to life imprisonment on charges of “separatism.” During his many years in prison, he was repeatedly transferred and held successively in prisons in Erzurum, Amed (Diyarbakır), Çankırı, Çanakkale, Adana, and Kırşehir.




On February 3 of this year, Altığ completed 30 years of his prison sentence. However, his scheduled release was postponed for six months by the prison’s Administrative and Observation Board. The decision was justified on the grounds that he had shown no remorse for the offense of which he was convicted. When the prison board reviewed his release again on August 3, his imprisonment was extended for another six months. Altığ therefore remains in prison beyon

title: 10-week ‘Women, Justice and Memory Vigil’ against femicides to be launched in Amed
content:
The Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) Network for Combating Violence announced that it will launch a “Women, Justice and Memory Vigil” against femicides and suspicious deaths of women.




According to a press statement issued at the Rosa Women’s Association, the vigil will begin outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse at 12:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, and will continue at the same location every Tuesday for 10 weeks.




Speaking on behalf of the women, İrem İlhan, a member of the Amed Bar Association’s Women’s Rights Center, said that in some cases, women’s deaths are classified as “suicide,” “accident,” or “suspicious death” and are not effectively investigated.




İlhan stressed that femicides should not be treated as isolated incidents, and factors such as domestic violence, threats, stalking, access to firearms, failure to enforce protection orders, ineffective investigations, and impunity must be assessed together.




Call for effective and comprehensive investigations




The network is calling for comprehensive investigations, particularly in cases where the cause of death remains unclear, including thorough examination of crime scenes, forensic and digital evidence, as well as any history of violence experienced by the women.

author: Unknown
title: Soldiers attack Martyr Binevş Cemetery on Mount Gabar
content:
The Martyr Binevş Cemetery, located near the village of Basret on Mount Gabar, was damaged. It was stated that numerous gravestones bearing names had been broken.




Images reportedly showing the cemetery show numerous gravestones smashed into pieces. The cemetery was constructed between 2010 and 2014. It was reported that many PKK guerrillas who were killed in the conflicts in the region were buried there.




The cemetery had previously been attacked in 2015 and was damaged at the time by bombardments carried out both from the air and from the ground.




Relatives of those buried at the cemetery reportedly reacted to the attack after learning that the cemetery had once again been damaged.

title: Kurdish publishing is a cultural struggle, not a commercial one
content:
Diyarbakır (Amed) is welcoming autumn with a book fair. The municipality is providing free transport throughout the fair, and I take one of the buses to the venue. The fair is being held in Üçkuyular, close to the Research Hospital, and there is also a large car park. Families from across the city are visiting the fair with their children. Even so, attendance is lower than last year. I think this may be because it is a weekday, and more people are likely to attend over the weekend. Publishers are also complaining about the low turnout, particularly as stand rental fees are quite high, meaning that some may even make a loss over the nine-day fair. Temperatures in the city are also above seasonal averages, while the floor of the fairground is covered with red carpets.




The struggle for Kurdish is important




Just inside the entrance, on the left, I see Aram Publishing House. I ask Salih Keleş about the state of Kurdish-language publishing from the perspective of a publisher that produces books in Kurdish. Keleş said publishing in Kurdish was itself a field of struggle for the publishing house: “Every year, although not at the level we would like, we see growing interest in Kurdish books. title: Meral Danış Beştaş: Process advancing but key gaps remain
content:
Parliament will open its doors today for the new legislative year. As political attention turns to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Peoples’ Democratic Congress (HDK) Co-Spokesperson, Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP and commission member Meral Danış Beştaş spoke to ANF about the course of the process, the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) ruling on the “right to hope” and the role Parliament should assume.




Meral Danış Beştaş responded to Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş’s statement that “the process is running smoothly”, saying that while it was valuable that the process was continuing, this did not mean it was progressing without problems.




Beştaş said that as of 1 October, the process would be approaching its second year and recalled that nearly two years had also passed since Abdullah Öcalan’s call of 27 February.




Beştaş said of the current stage of the process and Parliament’s responsibilities: “The process is moving forward, there is no problem in that respect, but what matters is how it is moving forward. The fact that the process itself is continuing does not mean there are no problems. The commission’s report has still not been implemented. We are all asking questions such as: ‘Will the framework law be implemented?’, ‘When will it be implemented?’ and ‘How will the transitions take place?’”

title: Abdullah Öcalan’s books published in English and Swedish
content:
Abdullah Öcalan’s book “The Civilizational Crisis in the Middle East and the Democratic Civilization Solution: : Manifesto of the Democratic Civilization, Volume IV” has been published in English by PM Press.




The Sociology of Freedom in Swedish




Öcalan’s work, "Manifesto of Democratic Civilization, Volume 3: The Sociology of Freedom" will be published in Swedish ("Manifest för en demokratisk civilisation, volym 3: Frihetens sociologi") this week. The book was translated into Swedish through a collaboration between Federativ Förlag and Heval Förlag, the publishing house of the Rojava Committees.




A launch of the book will be held on Sunday, 4 October in Stockholm. Participants will include the book’s translator, Tomas Petterson; political writer Gabriel Kuhn; and a member of the Academy of Democratic Modernity.




The launch will take place from 12:00 to 16:00 at the Katasalen venue in ABF-huset, Stockholm (Sveavägen 41).

title: Three Kurdish citizens sentenced to death in Tehran
content:
The Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) has published a report on the death sentences handed down to three Kurdish citizens from Rojhilatê Kurdistan.




The report states that three Kurdish citizens registered as residents of Kermanshah, Xesrew Mihemedîniya, Mesûd Toşmalanî, and Sîrwant Şehîdî (22), were arrested during protests in the capital, Tehran.




The 23rd Branch of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced the three citizens to death on charges of “war against God” and “assembly and collusion against national security.”




All three citizens are reportedly being held at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. The report also states that a woman tried in the same case was sentenced to five years in prison, and that her proceedings were still at the investigation stage.

title: Semir Aslanyürek: Cinema and art must stand for peace
content:
Turkey has been moving towards a new period since the Call for Peace and Democratic Society was issued on 27 February 2025. Discussions that began with statements by Devlet Bahçeli in October 2024 opened the way for a new process with the historic call on 27 February.




As the Peace and Democratic Society Process entered its third year, different sections of society in Turkey shared their views and criticisms of the process with the public. Art, one of the fields most affected by disinformation during 50 years of conflict, also became part of these discussions.




A look at the history of Turkey’s film and television industry shows that different sections of society, particularly Kurds, were represented through certain stereotypes for many years. Kurds and other marginalised groups were often portrayed as “helpless”, “ignorant”, “coarse” or prone to violence.




Director Semir Aslanyürek, who said that “productions that legitimise violence and caricature the ‘other’ are not art”, spoke to ANF about his cinema and the new period unfolding in Turkey.




Aslanyürek, who studied cinema at the USSR State Institute of Cinematography in Moscow, said of his time there: “When you ask, ‘What did the Soviets contribute to your art?’, you are of course referring to the USSR State Institute of Cinematography (VGIK) in Moscow. title: Remains of 25 Shengal people killed by ISIS finally laid to rest
content:
The remains of 25 people killed on 3 August 2014, and exhumed from mass graves in Koço since 2019, were handed over to their families. On Tuesday, the 25 remains had been collected from the Baghdad Institute of Forensic Medicine and sent to Mosul.




The remains of those killed set off from Mosul toward Shengal on Thursday. Thousands of people gathered at the Martyrs’ Monument in the village of Solê to receive them. The ceremony began with a minute of silence attended by political, civil and military representatives, the families of the martyrs, and the people of Shengal.




Following religious and traditional rituals, the martyrdom certificates of those killed in the massacre were read aloud and handed over to their families. After the bodies were returned to their families, most of whom were from Koço, they were buried in cemeteries.




The process of opening mass graves containing people killed by ISIS during the 3 August 2014 massacre officially began in the village of Koço on 15 March 2019. A total of 96 mass graves and dozens of individual graves have been identified across Shengal.




A total of 321 bodies exhumed from mass graves have been sent to Shengal. Families are waiting for more than 500 bodies currently in Baghdad to also be sent to Shengal.

title: Police detain Mersin Metropolitan Municipality mayor and 58 others
content:
A total of 59 people have been detained as part of an investigation launched into allegations of “corruption” involving Mersin Metropolitan Municipality and the municipalities of Yenişehir and Mezitli. As part of the investigation, police raided the homes of 59 people, including Mersin Metropolitan Municipality mayor Vahap Seçer, Yenişehir Mayor Abdullah Özyiğit, and Mezitli Mayor Ahmet Serkan Tuncer, and took them into custody.




According to the allegations, the investigation is examining 13 tenders and 63 direct procurement transactions. It is claimed that the investigation identified public losses amounting to 330 million and 945 thousand Turkish lira.

title: Iran bombs KDP-I camp
content:
The Iranian state carried out a drone attack on the Azadî Camp of the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDP-I), located in the Koye area of Erbil (Hewlêr), in South Kurdistan.




The KDP-I camp was bombed using “Hadid”-type drones. It was reported that there were no fatalities or injuries in the attack.

title: Protests for Kurdish-language education continue in Rojava
content:
The protests against restrictions on Kurdish-language education in Rojava, which have been continuing for weeks, are ongoing. In Girkê Legê and Rimêlan, students boycotted classes. In Qamişlo, Til Temir, and Dirbêsiyê, students, teachers, and education workers also protested for the right to mother-tongue education.




The protests are directed against a decision by the Education Ministry of the Islamist transitional government in Damascus to limit Kurdish in schools to three hours of instruction per week. Protesters are demanding the continuation of Kurdish-language education and constitutional recognition of Kurdish in Syria.






















Trilingual statement in Qamişlo




In Qamişlo, students and staff from the Şehîd Şervan, Canşêr, Dilxwaz, Heqî, and Omîd schools gathered in front of Canşêr School. A joint statement was read out in Kurdish, Arabic, and English. Student Mêrva Emo read the Kurdish version, teacher Wasil Esaed the Arabic version, and teacher Rojîn Mihemed Mûsa the English version.




In the statement, the students referred to the decades-long repression of the Kurdish population and the achievements of the Rojava Revolution. They described the current decisions as a continuation of a policy aimed at erasing Kurdish history and identity. They said that reducing Kurdish-language instruction was a first step in this direction.

title: Body of HPG guerrilla Mevlüt Elver returned to his family after nine years
content:
Nine years after his death, the body of guerrilla fighter Mevlüt Elver (Azad Tolhildan) was returned to his family and laid to rest in Van. Elver, a member of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG), lost his life in 2017 during a clash with Turkish military units in a rural area of Van province.




His body was buried in 2018 in the cemetery for the nameless in Seyrantepe, in the Tuşba district. That same year, the family provided a DNA sample in order to identify and bury their son. Although the sample matched Elver’s DNA, his body was not handed over to his relatives.




Eight years later, the family submitted another application. Following another confirmed DNA match, they were finally able to receive Elver’s body.




The reburial at Seyrantepe Cemetery took place with the participation of numerous people and was organized at the initiative of MEBYA-DER, the Association of Families of the Martyrs. Elver was laid to rest in the family grave at Xaçort Cemetery. Participants accompanied the burial with chants of “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal).

title: Revenge Teams kill a “collaborator responsible for the killing of four guerrillas” in Rojhilat
content:
The Revenge Teams of the Martyrs of Kurdistan issued a statement regarding an action directed against a collaborator named Heyder Mûradî.




The Revenge Teams of the Martyrs of Kurdistan said that Mûradî collaborated with Iranian intelligence forces and the Sine Shahramfer Command Center and was responsible for the killing of four guerrillas in 2018.




“Through his treacherous actions, he openly acted against the values of the people. Although we had previously given him the necessary warning, he did not cease his counter activities. This collaborator, through his betrayal and cooperation with the intelligence forces and the Sine Shahramfer Command Center in particular, was responsible for the deaths of four of our guerrillas and people’s heroes—Tolhildan Sine, Argeş Karzan, Rojhat Şer, and Dilovan Fedayî—on September 7, 2018,” the statement said.




The Revenge Teams of the Martyrs of Kurdistan stated: “We reiterate once again that we will hold accountable those who have had a hand in shedding the blood of the Kurdish people, Kurdistan’s leading figures, and revolutionaries, especially those who continue to side with intelligence agencies, engage in collaboration and espionage, and oppress our people. We will always pursue them in order to punish them.”

title: Economic crisis in Turkey: Money barely covers basic necessities at the market
content:
The stalls at a weekly market in Istanbul’s Esenyurt district are filled with tomatoes, peppers, aubergines, and fruit. Yet many people can afford less and less of what is on offer. Instead of buying several kilograms of vegetables, shoppers purchase individual items, compare prices between the market and supermarkets, and carefully calculate their spending even on basic foodstuffs. “Who can still buy everything they need here? No one,” says a man who supports his family on the minimum wage. “There is plenty at the market, but we can buy very little of it. Of our income, 20,000 lira already goes toward rent. There is hardly anything you can do with what remains.”




Official figures reflect part of this development. According to the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜİK), annual inflation stood at 31.51 percent in August, while consumer prices rose by 1.84 percent compared with the previous month. Calculations based on TÜİK data indicate that inflation eroded 6,196 lira of the minimum wage’s purchasing power in the first eight months of the year alone. There was no mid-year increase in the minimum wage.




Food is bought individually




At the market in Esenyurt, a kilogram of tomatoes costs between 40 and 100 lira, depending on quality. Cucumbers are sold for around 70 lira per kilogram, peppers for 150 lira, and aubergines and courgettes for about 60 lira. Fruit prices range

title: Kurdish political prisoners denied medical care in Urmia
content:
Prison authorities are denying two Kurdish political prisoners, Hossein Osmani and Bahram Majidi-Far, access to adequate medical care at Urmia (Orumiyeh) Central Prison despite serious health problems.




The two men are held in the prison’s Ershad ward, which houses political prisoners and prisoners of conscience.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Osmani, 65, from Mahabad, is suffering from serious vision problems caused by a cataract in his left eye, and that prison officials have refused to transfer him to a medical facility outside the prison.




Osmani is serving the 13th year of a 30-year prison sentence.




Majidi-Far, from Urmia, has experienced severely low blood pressure in recent months.




Doctors at the prison infirmary have recommended that he be transferred to a medical facility outside the prison for examination by a cardiologist, but prison authorities have refused to approve the transfer.




Hossein Osmani’s case




Osmani was arrested on 23 February 2014 after being summoned to the Ministry of Intelligence’s office in Mahabad and was taken to the ministry’s detention facility in Urmia.




He spent 13 months in solitary confinement, during which he was denied family visits and allowed only two brief telephone calls with his family.

title: Kataib Hezbollah suspends military activities in Iraq
content:
Kataib Hezbollah, one of the Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, announced that it has suspended its military activities in the country following the complete withdrawal of US forces from Iraq.




Kataib Hezbollah leader Ahmed al-Hamidawi instructed the group’s fighters to halt military activities in Iraq. However, the statement said that operations targeting “enemy aircraft” violating Iraqi airspace would continue.




The decision came after the United States withdrew its remaining troops from Iraq. With US Central Command (CENTCOM) completing the evacuation of personnel and equipment from Erbil Air Base, Washington’s military mission in Iraq under Operation Inherent Resolve officially came to an end.




A new period following the US withdrawal




The United States and Iraq agreed in 2024 to end the mission of the International Coalition in Iraq. The US-led coalition was deployed to the country in 2014 after ISIS seized large areas of Iraqi territory.




The Pentagon says that despite the end of the military mission, training and intelligence support for Iraq will continue. The Coalition’s command structure is expected to continue operating from outside Iraq.




The US withdrawal is also viewed as the beginning of a new phase in the Iraqi government’s efforts to bring the weapons of Iran-aligned armed groups in the country under state control.

title: Dr Bogos Yalim: No democratisation without confronting the past
content:
Dr Bogos Yalim, who has lived in Belgium for many years and is known for his work within the Armenian community, spoke about the historical experiences of Armenians and developments in Turkey. Yalim said the Armenian community approached developments in Turkey with caution because of the collective memory shaped by the 1915 Genocide, while stressing their support for the Kurdish people’s struggle for rights and freedoms.




Yalim said the historical memory of the 1915 Genocide played a decisive role in how the Armenian community viewed developments in Turkey, adding that its cautious approach to the peace process stemmed primarily from a historical distrust of state policies.




Gains for the Kurdish people would make us happy




Yalim said that despite historical problems between the Armenian and Kurdish communities, Armenians supported Kurdish demands for rights and freedoms. He stressed that they respected the Kurdish people’s right to determine their own future and said the Kurdish people securing their rights would be a positive development for Armenians.




Yalim said, “If the Kurdish people gain certain rights there, that would make us happy. Nothing more than that,” adding that the concerns arising from the Armenian community’s historical experiences did not mean opposition to Kurdish demands for rights and freedoms.

title: Ayyıldız: Economic crisis and social decay deepen social problems
content:
The deepening economic crisis, lack of employment opportunities and problems with public services in Kurdish cities are having an increasingly visible impact on social life. Migration driven by a lack of investment, problems with the quality of education and unemployment are exacerbating social problems affecting broad sections of society, particularly women and young people.




Insufficient investment in the region and limited employment opportunities are driving young people in particular to migrate to other cities, while unemployment and economic deprivation are also taking a toll on social life.




Social worker Berfin Ayyıldız spoke to ANF about the issue.




Economic crisis deepens the social cycle




Berfin Ayyıldız said there were many factors affecting the social fabric, with economic problems among the most significant.




Ayyıldız said economic difficulties did not affect only individuals or families, but had consequences for society as a whole. 




She said: “Economic problems do not affect only an individual or a family. They affect society as a whole. A family facing economic hardship may be forced to migrate. They may have to take insecure jobs outside the home, on the streets or in their neighbourhood, or someone may turn to illegal means to earn money. This can then trigger other problems, such as violence, addiction or involvement in crime.”

title: Psychologist Kaya: Peace cannot be achieved through a declaration alone
content:
Academic Orhan Kaya, discussing the historical dimensions of collective trauma, the Kurdish people's resistance, and conflict resolution processes, said that approaches focusing exclusively on trauma are incomplete. He also commented on expectations and disappointments surrounding the current process, hopes of return among the diaspora, distrust between communities, and the conditions necessary for peace to be felt throughout society. Kaya said that the atmosphere of distrust must be eliminated for peace to be experienced and that fundamental steps are needed to achieve this.




The Kurdish people did not just experience traumatic processes, they resisted




Kaya added that the history of collective trauma runs very deep and has been discussed in psychology for many years. He described trauma as unexpected and sudden events that affect human life in its entirety. Noting that people in Turkey, particularly the Kurdish population, have been exposed to traumatic experiences for decades, Kaya said that focusing solely on trauma would be an incomplete approach.







 







Kaya argued that the history of resistance must also be examined alongside trauma. He said: “When traumatic processes have continued for such a long time, discussing only trauma would be an incomplete approach. title: DFG Media Report: A free and pluralistic media is necessary for socialization of peace
content:
A report published by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) examined the language used in coverage of the process, headlines, news sources, and the actors given visibility.




The report covers the period 27 February 2025 to 1 October 2026. It underlined that media outlets close to the government predominantly framed the process through concepts such as “security,” “terrorism,” “dissolution,” and “liquidation,” while opposition media placed greater emphasis on the policies of the political government, previous peace-process experiences, and the political objectives of the current process.




The DFG noted that reporting unverified claims in some media outlets affected public discussions about the process. It also stated that publications within the Free Press tended to address developments more through concepts such as “peace,” “negotiation,” “democratic solution,” and “a new political era.”




Who is speaking and who is not visible 




The report also drew attention to the diversity of sources used by media organizations. The DFG stated that statements by state institutions, government representatives, and political party officials dominated coverage of the process, while the views of Kurdish political actors, civil society organizations, academics, journalists, and different segments of society received more limited coverage. title: Eren: Concrete steps needed for democratisation and clear status
content:
The “1001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, launched to contribute to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, was announced to the public on 12 September. The campaign calls for support for non-violence and disarmament, constitutional guarantees for equal citizenship, the strengthening of the democratic rule of law and the creation of conditions for free and equal negotiations. It also seeks to broaden social participation in the process and enable different sections of society to become active participants.




Journalist Faruk Eren, a relative of a disappeared person and one of the campaign’s signatories, spoke to ANF about the campaign’s aims, the importance of democratisation amid the ongoing period without conflict, the concrete steps needed for the process to move forward on a sound footing, and the need to confront the truth in order to achieve lasting peace. Eren also discussed the prevailing language in the media and peace journalism.







 







Eren explained why he had signed the campaign, saying first that he was generally reluctant to support signature campaigns. He drew attention to the relationship between journalism and activism, saying that the state of democracy in Turkey had also changed the role of journalists.

title: DEM Party calls for respect for the will of the people of Mersin
content:
DEM Party Co-Chairs Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhans said: “We do not accept the operations targeting 59 people, including Mersin Metropolitan Municipality mayor Vahap Seçer, Yenişehir mayor Abdullah Özyiğit, and Mezitli mayor Ahmet Serkan Tuncer.”




The Co-Chairs added that the will of the people expressed at the ballot box is continually being suppressed through judicial processes, arguing that “the will of the people has effectively been rendered inoperative.”




The DEM Party Co-Chairs continued: “We know this method very well. We encountered the same approach when our municipalities were seized and handed over to trustees. The people were granted the right to vote, but the person they elected was not granted the right to govern. If the right to vote and stand for election is violated in one place, the consequences do not remain confined there.”




The statement said: “If the will of the people is valid only when the election result is liked, then this is not democracy. Whoever the people of Mersin elected should govern Mersin. The will of the people must be respected, and the judiciary must be removed from the sphere of political reckoning.”

title: Iraqi Islamic Resistance Movement: We will not surrender our weapons
content:
Jafar Husseini, spokesperson for the Iraqi Islamic Resistance Movement, issued a statement on bringing weapons under state control and the withdrawal of the International Coalition against ISIS from Iraq.




Husseini said that their movement is not bound by any agreement or decision made by the government or political parties, adding: “Our weapons are still in the hands of our fighters.”




The statement said that the movement has been holding talks with the Coordination Framework Committee for more than 40 days regarding the reorganization of weapons, and called for the withdrawal of US and NATO forces, as well as all foreign military forces, from Iraq.




Stating that no response has yet been received from the Iraqi government regarding the talks, the statement said: “We will fight any enemy that targets Iraq and its people. Our door is open to any dialogue that will safeguard Iraq’s sovereignty and freedom.”




The statement came on the day the International Coalition announced its withdrawal from Iraq. The process of bringing weapons under state control was reportedly postponed until June 2027.

title: Sarıtaş: Building peace and a democratic society requires struggle
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Siirt Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş spoke to ANF about the parliamentary dimension of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the steps taken so far and the role parliament should play in the coming period. She discussed public support for the process, the responsibilities of political actors and the steps needed to achieve lasting peace.




Sarıtaş stressed that society was directly involved in shaping the process and said the state needed to accelerate its efforts and take concrete steps towards a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.




The people are not on the sidelines but at the heart of this process




Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş discussed public support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that this support was also a reflection of how the process had emerged.




Sarıtaş said opinion polls and meetings with the public had shown widespread support for the process from the outset. She noted that the Kurdish political movement's role in the process, particularly the initiatives undertaken by Abdullah Öcalan, had received strong public support.

title: Remains of 25 Yazidis killed in Shengal Genocide to be returned to their families
content:
The remains of 25 people killed during the genocide against the Yazidis will be handed over today to their families, bringing the number of Yazidi victims whose identities have been established and returned to their families since 2021 to 321.




16 of the victims were from Koço, four from Herdan, two from Tilbenat, and three from the villages of Solax, Werdiyê, and Borik.




The return of the remains has once again brought attention to efforts to establish the fate of those who went missing or were abducted during the Yazidi genocide. Calls continue for the opening of mass graves, the acceleration of identification procedures and DNA analyses, and efforts to determine the fate of missing and abducted people.

author: Unknown
title: Öcalan: The YBŞ must become part of the Iraqi army and remain in Shengal
content:
The Shengal People’s Council provided information on the latest developments in the region during an assembly. Representatives of Yazidi civil society organizations, the local population, and Yazidi security forces took part in the meeting on Wednesday. A message from Abdullah Öcalan was read out during the assembly.




In the message, the Kurdish leader focuses in particular on the future of the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the protection of Yazidi society. He advocates integrating the YBŞ into the Iraqi army while allowing it to remain in Shengal as a local force. “The YBŞ must remain in Shengal,” Öcalan states, describing the Yazidis’ own self-defense forces as necessary.




Öcalan also addresses the talks between the YBŞ and the Iraqi government. According to the information available to him, an agreement has already been drafted but has not yet been signed by the Iraqi prime minister. Reports indicate that the agreement is being blocked by Turkey. Öcalan calls on Ankara not to obstruct it and emphasizes that the Yazidis are not demanding an autonomous region, but local democracy.




Abdullah Öcalan's message to the Yazidi community reads as follows:




“Do Yazidi women have a strong stance in the face of ISIS attacks? This needs to be understood. Yazidi culture alone is also not sufficient for freedom. I say this, and I have also told the state the same thing, an

author: Unknown
title: Conference in London: The path for democratic politics must be opened to achieve lasting peace
content:
On the second day of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference in London, the future of the Kurdish question was discussed by individuals with direct experience of the struggle and resolution processes. İmralı Secretariat member Veysi Aktaş spoke about the 1999 disarmament experience, while Çetin Arkaş recounted his 33.5 years in prison and the period he spent on İmralı. Legal guarantees for disarmament, opening up space for democratic politics, and the role of women in the peace process emerged as key themes of the panel.




The first session of the second day, titled “Post-Conflict Kurdish Democratic Politics,” featured İmralı Secretariat members Veysi Aktaş and Çetin Arkaş, Nesrin Akgül representing the Kurdish Women’s Movement, and Yüksel Genç, a member of the First Peace Group. Moderated by journalist Tuğçe Tatari, the session addressed the transition from armed struggle to democratic politics, experiences from previous processes, legal guarantees, conditions on İmralı, and the role of women in the new period.




Speaking at the opening of the second day, politician Serpil Kemalbay said that the Kurdish political movement had begun to open the way for a new and different form of struggle. Emphasizing that peace does not simply mean the silencing of weapons, she stressed that coexistence must be built on political will and strong legal guarantees.

author: Unknown
title: Removed co-mayors of the DEM Party demand an end to trustee rule
content:
The removed co-mayors of ten DEM Party-run municipalities have called for an end to trustee rule and for their reinstatement to the offices to which they were elected. At a meeting in Mardin on Wednesday, they assessed the consequences of the trustee policy and linked their demand to the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




Following the meeting, Devrim Demir, the removed co-mayor of Mardin Metropolitan Municipality, said that the discussions had focused on the consequences of trustee rule in the ten affected municipalities. “The picture that has emerged clearly shows that trustee rule means plunder and the usurpation of political will.” Demir also criticized the fact that government austerity measures apparently do not apply in the same way to municipalities under trustee rule. “All the avenues that were closed to us to prevent us from providing municipal services are open to the trustees. This policy must be ended as soon as possible.”




With regard to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Demir said that the steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement had so far not been met with corresponding steps by the state. The removed mayors called on the government to seize the current historic opportunity through decisive measures. “The conditions must be created for Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan to live and work freely. The usurpation of political will must end immediat

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish nurse tortured after arrest by Iranian intelligence
content:
Iranian Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested Kurdish nurse Foad Ghaderi on 21 September as he travelled from Sanandaj to Javanrud.




During several days of interrogation at the ministry’s detention facility in Javanrud, he was subjected to severe physical and psychological torture in an attempt to force him to confess. He was then transferred to Dizel Abad Prison in Kermanshah.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Ghaderi, from the village of Sarrud-e Olya in Javanrud, worked as a nurse at a private medical centre in Sanandaj. Agents arrested him at the Naleh Shekineh mountain pass on the road between Kamyaran and Ravansar and took him to the Javanrud detention facility.




After his arrest, Ministry of Intelligence agents raided his family home and took away some of his personal belongings.




Since his arrest, he has been denied access to a lawyer and visits from his family. The charges against him remain unknown.

author: Unknown
title: Conference in London: Integration is possible through rights and freedoms
content:
The second day of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference, organized by the Centre for Kurdish Affairs in London, continued with discussions on the political future of the Kurdish question in its different parts.




The session, titled “The Kurdish Question Across Borders,” was moderated by journalist Fréderike Geerdink. Ilham Ehmed participated via video message, while Dr. Abdulkerîm Omer, Dr. Shilan Fuad Huseyîn, and Dr. Hêmin Seyîdî contributed their assessments.







 







Ehmed said integration must be based on freedom and rights




Ilham Ehmed discussed the process underway in Syria and the position of the Kurds in the country’s future. She said that an agreement providing for a ceasefire had been reached on January 29, adding that the aim was to end the war and establish a process that would enable Kurds to participate in the Syrian state and its institutions.




Ehmed said that, within this framework, the integration of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) into the army, the Internal Security Forces into the Ministry of Interior, and the institutions of the Autonomous Administration into state institutions were on the agenda. She noted that some steps had been taken, but that serious problems remained, particularly in the field of education.




Ehmed said that the teaching of Kurdish for three hours a week in government schools had been accepted, but that

author: Unknown
title: Conference in London: Democratic transformation essential for peace
content:
On the second and final day of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference, held in London, the panel titled “Inclusive Peace: Women, Minorities, Human Rights and Justice Systems” took place.




The panel was moderated by Dr. Nisan Alıcı and featured politician Gültan Kışanak, DEM Party parliamentary group deputy chair and Qers MP Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, Dr. Güneş Daşlı, a research fellow at Loughborough University’s CARA, journalist and writer Ali Duran Topuz, and lawyer and writer Gürkan Çakıroğlu. Topuz and Çakıroğlu joined the panel online.




The panel addressed women’s role in the peace process, a democratic solution to the Kurdish question, social reconciliation, legal guarantees, truth and justice, and the role of the media.




Kışanak: Women must be founding agents of peace




Politician Gültan Kışanak emphasized that speaking only with the government would not be enough to resolve the Kurdish question and that broader social reconciliation also needed to be achieved.




Drawing attention to how state and government policies have deepened social polarization, Kışanak said that Kurdish demands and the Kurdish struggle had been stigmatized through narratives such as “a foreign powers’ plot” and “a threat to national survival.”

author: Unknown
title: Mazloum Abdi issues message on Kurdish-language education
content:
Syrian Presidential Adviser Mazloum Abdi delivered a video message through ANHA on Kurdish-language education, the situation of schools, Rojava University and Kobanê University.




The message was as follows:




“Dear people, the Kurdish language is our identity. Protecting and developing Kurdish has always been a fundamental objective of the struggle we have waged to this day. Learning and receiving an education in one’s mother tongue is a natural right of all peoples, and education in Kurdish is likewise a fundamental and natural right of the Kurdish people. Over the past 14 years, during the Rojava Revolution, tremendous efforts have been made to provide Kurdish-language education and establish an education system despite the conditions of war. Although it has had shortcomings and weaknesses, it was something new and represented a historic step in the history of Rojava.




I would like to take this opportunity to salute all the families who sent their children to Kurdish-language schools despite the war, difficulties and obstacles. I also congratulate all the teachers and staff who have contributed to the teaching and study of the Kurdish language over the past 14 years.




It has been one year and eight months since the fall of the Baath regime. Our efforts to make Kurdish an official part of Syria’s education system are continuing. Numerous meetings, initiatives and di

author: Unknown
title: Mother of NATO prisoner: We are now victims of the judiciary too
content:
Twenty-nine-year-old earthquake survivor Halil Yakut was among those imprisoned in what was described as a witch-hunt against opposition groups ahead of the NATO Summit on 7–8 July 2026. Yakut, whose family home in Antakya was destroyed in the Maraş-centred earthquakes, was detained on 23 June 2026 in Muğla, hundreds of kilometres from Ankara, on the assumption that he was planning to stage a protest, and was subsequently imprisoned. An indictment prepared months later included anti-NATO articles published in Halk Okulu magazine and social media posts by Halkın Sesi TV concerning NATO bases as evidence relating to the alleged preparations for a protest ahead of the summit. It also referred to previous cases in which Yakut had been tried, including cases in which he had been acquitted. The indictment was submitted to the Istanbul 14th High Criminal Court, which ruled that it lacked jurisdiction over the case. Halil Yakut’s mother, Gülten Yakut, spoke to ANF and said: “We are earthquake survivors, but the injustice inflicted on my son has now made us victims of the judicial system as well.”




Gülten Yakut, whose family home in Antakya was destroyed in the Maraş-centred earthquakes, said she had not even had time to recover from the devastation because of what she described as the systematic use of hostile law against her son. She said Halil had repeatedly been imprisoned becaus

title: Against male violence and male domination
content:
An extremely interesting march will take place in Amed today, 30 September. Perhaps it would be more accurate to call it a march without precedent, or one of very few of its kind. Men will march against male violence. Through this march, they will protest the dominant male violence directed against women. Until now, women have organized marches and rallies to protest male violence against women. Some men who had educated themselves on the basis of women's freedom would occasionally participate in these demonstrations and marches. Now, however, men themselves are organizing and carrying out a march to protest male violence against women. And beginning in Amed, which is known as the “capital of democracy.” In this way, the spirits of the many Gülistan Doku, Rojin Kabaiş and little Narin Güran, who were murdered by dominant masculinity, may find at least some consolation.




Undoubtedly, the fact that such a historically significant action is taking place in Amed also carries great meaning. This action demonstrates the level of development and strength attained by the Kurdish Freedom Revolution. It reveals that the essence of this revolution is, in fact, a Women's Freedom Revolution. Once again, it proclaims to the entire country and the world that Amed is a pioneering city of such a revolution. author: Unknown
title: Öcalan must be able to carry out his work as Coordinator for Peace and Political Transition
content:
As a well-known saying goes, there can be no proper treatment without a correct diagnosis. Whatever anyone may say, the main issue on Turkey’s agenda today is the Peace and Democratic Society process, which began with Abdullah Öcalan’s call for the dissolution of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). The President of Turkey and the Speaker of Parliament have said that the process is important and progressing well. Yet recent developments raise doubts about how accurately the state understands the process. If there is a problem and a process aimed at resolving it, it can only be addressed with the parties directly concerned. The leadership of the Kurdish Freedom Movement, one of the principal parties to the issue, says that the process is not progressing well. Doubts inevitably grow when one side says things are not going well while the other insists that they are.




On the day the so-called framework law was passed, Justice and Development Party (AKP) Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Abdullah Güler said that Abdullah Öcalan’s status would change and that he would subsequently meet with many different groups. Two months have passed, yet there has been no tangible outcome from those remarks. title: Yılmaz: Visually impaired people face barriers to sport
content:
Sport is one of the key areas that strengthens individuals’ participation in physical and social life, yet barriers preventing visually impaired people from accessing sport persist. Inaccessible sports facilities, limited opportunities for different sports and training, transport difficulties and economic constraints make it harder for visually impaired people to participate in sporting activities regularly and independently.




The lack of accessibility at sports facilities, particularly in urban areas, makes it difficult for visually impaired people to reach them independently and participate regularly in sporting activities.




Abdülmecit Yılmaz, President of the Amed Visually Impaired Sports Club and the Amed Federation of People with Disabilities, spoke to ANF about the difficulties visually impaired people face in accessing sport.




The biggest barriers are the lack of facilities and infrastructure




Yılmaz said people with disabilities were unable to participate freely in sport in the city and that the most fundamental problem was the lack of facilities where they could train and compete.

author: Unknown
title: Iraqi Prime Minister: International Coalition’s mission has officially ended
content:
A ceremony was held today in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, to mark Sovereignty Day and the end of the International Coalition’s mission against ISIS. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi attended the ceremony alongside commanders of the coalition forces and the Iraqi military.




Speaking at the ceremony, Ali al-Zaidi said: “We officially announce the end of the International Coalition forces’ mission in Iraq. Today, Iraq is reaping the fruits of the sacrifices and heroism demonstrated over many years. Our security forces, with all their components, have established security and operational control across all regions of Iraq.”




Stating that the fight “against terrorism” would continue, the Prime Minister added: “The end of the International Coalition’s mission does not mean that our war against terrorism is over. On the contrary, it marks the transition to a stage in which Iraq assumes full responsibility for its own defense, security, and stability.”

author: Unknown
title: Cebar Yaver: KDP-PUK dispute leaves the door open to threats
content:
In an exclusive interview with Fırat News Agency (ANF), military and security expert Cebar Yaver assessed the security situation in Iraq and the Kurdistan Region, the end of the mission of the International Coalition forces, and the process of unifying the Peshmerga forces of the KDP (Kurdistan Democratic Party) and PUK (Patriotic Union of Kurdistan).




‘Coalition forces were established to protect US interests’ 




Yaver noted that the end of the mission of the anti-ISIS International Coalition forces in Iraq was an expected development, noting that the force had been deployed for a specific purpose.




Yaver said: “This coalition was established at a time when ISIS had gained control in Iraq and Syria, occupied a quarter of Iraqi territory, and become a serious threat to Baghdad, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan. Taking its own interests into account, the United States formed this coalition of more than 70 countries.”




Regarding the withdrawal process, Yaver said that two years ago a joint military committee comprising representatives from Iraq, the Kurdistan Region, and the United States assessed the ISIS threat and concluded that the organization’s military and financial capabilities had diminished and that it had lost territory.




The agreement stipulated that the departure would take place in two phases; withdrawal from central and southern Iraq by the end of September 2

title: Muqtada al-Sadr announces dissolution of his armed structures
content:
Iraqi Shiite leader Muqtada al-Sadr announced that the armed structures affiliated with him have been dissolved and that one of them has been transformed into a civilian foundation.




According to Sadr’s statement, Saraya al-Salam (Peace Brigades) has been dissolved, while the Imam Mahdi Army, which had previously been among Sadr’s armed formations, will be transformed into a civilian organization under the name “Ansar al-Imam al-Mahdi Foundation.”




Sadr also announced the dissolution of the armed group Liwa al-Yawm al-Mawud (Promised Day Brigade).




In his statement, Sadr emphasized Iraq’s sovereignty and independence, saying that weapons in the country should be brought under state control.




Sadr’s move came on the same day that the US-led International Coalition ended its military mission in Iraq and US forces completed their withdrawal from the country.




The Iraqi government had previously called on armed groups in the country to place their weapons under state control and identified September 30 as an important milestone. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government had stated that weapons held outside state control would face legal consequences. However, the government was later reported to have treated this date as the beginning of a process of regulation and integration rather than a deadline for the complete surrender of weapons.

content:

Awdanan said: “Recognizing the political status of the Kurds and drafting a constitution based on the democratic self-government of the Kurdish nation are fundamental conditions for Iran’s democratic and decentralized political future.”

title: Conference in London discusses international experiences of peace and political settlement
content:
The Centre for Kurdish Affairs (CKA) convenes the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference in London on 29–30 September 2026, bringing together Kurdish political and civic figures, parliamentarians, policymakers, academics, peace-process practitioners, journalists, researchers and representatives of civil society.




The conference provides a structured and non-partisan forum for examining the prospects for peace, democratic participation and political settlement in relation to the Kurdish question, with particular attention to the evolving process in Turkey and its wider regional and international implications.




The conference is taking place at a significant stage in the current political process. In August 2026, the Turkish Parliament adopted the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion, establishing a legal framework for certain procedures connected with the disarmament, dissolution and reintegration process, subject to the conditions set out in the legislation. The law was approved by Parliament on 10 August and published in the Official Gazette on 18 August 2026.

title: Conference in London addresses issues of power-sharing and constitutional arrangements
content:
The Centre for Kurdish Affairs (CKA) has organized a Peace and Democratic Integration Conference in London on 29 and 30 September 2026, bringing together Kurdish political and civic figures, parliamentarians, policymakers, academics, peace-process practitioners, journalists, researchers and representatives of civil society.




Today, the conference’s second panel was titled “Peace, Power-Sharing, and Constitutional Arrangements: Lessons from the United Kingdom.” The panel explored the role of constitutionalism in conflict resolution, drawing on the UK’s experience of power-sharing, devolution and differentiated forms of governance. It will examine how constitutional arrangements can provide credible guarantees, distribute political authority and accommodate distinct political and territorial claims within a stable democratic framework. The discussion will consider what these experiences can offer to the Kurdish question, particularly how constitutional reform can provide durable channels for recognition, political participation and meaningful local authority while strengthening confidence in the wider political settlement. 




Speakers were Prof. Michael Gunter, Dr. Matthew Whiting, Prof. Michael Keating, Geraint Thomas, while Matt Broomfield was the moderator.

title: MAF-DAD: Reasonable grounds to suspect war crimes in North and East Syria
content:
The Association for Democracy and International Law (MAF-DAD) has published its report, International Crimes Committed by and on Behalf of the Government of the Syrian Arab Republic, examining developments in North and East Syria in January and February 2026.




MAF-DAD’s independent Fact-Finding Mission investigated violations in North and East Syria following attacks on the Sheikh Maqsoud (Şêxmeqsûd) and Ashrafiah (Eşrefiyê) neighbourhoods of Aleppo in early January 2026. Members of the mission conducted field investigations in the region between 21 February and 17 March 2026.




The report said 32 detailed qualitative interviews were conducted as part of the fieldwork, involving a total of 62 people. Those interviewed included 25 direct victims, one victim’s family and six representatives of institutions and organisations involved in documenting violations or assisting victims.




MAF-DAD said the report was based on a comparative assessment of statements from victims and witnesses, direct field observations, medical records, reports by institutions and civil society organisations, evidence collected by the Rojava Information Center (RIC) and open-source material. The report applied the standard of “reasonable grounds to believe” that a violation had occurred.

author: Unknown
title: Life of Kurdish political prisoner at risk in Tehran
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Network has published a report about the health of Mutelîb Ehmedyan, a Kurdish political prisoner from Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan).




Ehmedyan has been imprisoned for 16 years, and is reportedly suffering from several illnesses, including stomach cancer.




His health condition is said to be so serious that he is no longer fit to remain in prison. For this reason, Ehmedyan requested a postponement of the enforcement of his prison sentence. However, following an objection by the Tehran Prosecutor General’s Office, the political prisoner has continued to be held in the harsh conditions of Evin Prison.




According to the report, due to the negligence and indifference of the authorities, the Kurdish man was previously denied permission to receive treatment outside the prison. As a result, the cancer spread throughout his body. After his condition deteriorated, doctors reportedly had to remove his gallbladder, liver and part of his intestines in several operations. The report also states that prison authorities frequently withhold or prevent the delivery of medication obtained from outside the prison.




Ehmedyan was arrested by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on September 13, 2010. He was held in solitary confinement for eight months and subjected to severe physical torture. He was sentenced to 30 years in prison on charges of “rebellion.”

title: Öcalan: The true objective of this transformation is to build a democratic society
content:
Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan has addressed the international “Peace and Democratic Integration Conference” in London with a detailed message. The two-day conference, which begins today, focuses on international experiences from peace processes and their significance for a democratic and political solution to the Kurdistan question. In his message, Öcalan refers back to his Call for Peace and a Democratic Society of February 27, 2025, stating that the political perspective opened at that time must now be developed further in practice.




At the heart of Öcalan’s message is the concept of democratic integration. He understands this not as assimilation or the abandonment of social autonomy, but as the voluntary participation of a democratically organized society in a democratic republic on the basis of collective rights. Lasting peace, he argues, requires far more than an end to armed conflict: legal guarantees, the democratization of the republic, the free development of language and culture, strengthened local self-government, and social organization.




The message from Öcalan reads as follows:

title: DEM Party calls for parliamentary inquiry into the ‘Fund Crisis’
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Central Executive Board called for a comprehensive investigation and public scrutiny into developments it described as the “Fund Crisis” in a statement.




The statement said the developments could not be regarded merely as a technical financial problem, arguing that persistently high inflation, unemployment, the rising cost of living and poverty in Turkey had driven people to seek alternative ways to invest their savings and make ends meet. It added that financial markets had been turned into an arena for speculation and manipulation by certain groups.




The DEM Party said the issue could not be considered resolved simply through the resignation of a former minister or by holding certain fund managers responsible. It called for an investigation into why the relevant public institutions, particularly the Capital Markets Board (SPK) and the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BDDK), had failed to intervene in a timely manner.




The party called for every stage of the process to be examined and made public, from the establishment of the funds and their investment decisions to their relationships with companies, regulatory oversight and liquidation decisions.

author: Unknown
title: MP Çandar: The process is a long road with ups and downs
content:
DEM Party MP Cengiz Çandar has described the Peace and Democratic Society Process as a long-term political path whose outcome remains open. Speaking at an event at the Democratic Kurdish Community Center in Geneva, the politician discussed the next steps, the role of Abdullah Öcalan, and the future of Rojava.




Çandar particularly rejected accusations that the Kurdish Freedom Movement had abandoned its goals by ending the armed struggle. “There can be no talk of betrayal or deviation. For the first time, they have ended an uprising through their own decision and moved it into a new phase.” However, he said, this marks only the beginning of the political phase of the process. “Nothing is finished yet,” Çandar said. Öcalan himself, he added, speaks of “the first step on a thousand-kilometer journey.”






















Öcalan remains crucial




According to Çandar, the process cannot be implemented without either Öcalan or Turkey’s political leadership. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, he said, is crucial to state decision-making because of the presidential system. At the same time, he noted, Öcalan continues to wield the influence necessary over the Kurdish Freedom Movement. As an example, Çandar cited the practical implementation of disarmament and the possible return of members of the movement from the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. title: Demonstration in Strasbourg calls for ‘Right to Hope’ for Öcalan, urges the CoE to "act now"
content:
DEM Party Amed MP, Co-Spokesperson of the Foreign Relations Commission and member of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe Bedran Öztürk, together with Faik Yağız, Mazlum Dinç, Sevilay Çeleng, and parliamentarians supportive of the Kurds, have been holding talks at the Council of Europe for the past two days.




Due to the ongoing sessions of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, numerous elected Kurdish politicians and parliamentarians gathered in front of the Council of Europe, joined by French supporters of the Kurds and internationalists.




















The elected representatives assembled at the site of the ongoing Freedom Vigil in front of the Council of Europe, which is demanding the ‘Right to Hope’ for Abdullah Öcalan, and issued a statement.




Zübeyir Aydar, speaking on behalf of the KNK (Kurdistan National Congress), and Hekim Sefkan, speaking on behalf of Tev-Çand (Kurdish Movement for Culture and Art), delivered statements in Kurdish, while Zübeyde Zümrüt and Ayşe Acar Başaran spoke in Turkish on behalf of the KCDK-E (Congress of Democratic Societies of Kurdistan in Europe).




















In addition, Tiny Kox, Chair of the Left Group at the Council of Europe, and Emmanuel Fernandes, an MP from La France Insoumise, each delivered a speech calling for Öcalan’s freedom.

author: Unknown
title: Iran strikes Azadî Camp
content:
The Iranian state bombed Azadî Camp in the Koye district of Hewlêr (Erbil) with drones. Families of Peshmerga fighters affiliated with the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDP-I) live in the camp.




No casualties were reported in the attack, but material damage was caused.

title: Gülbeyaz: Lasting peace requires the state to embrace diversity
content:
Abdurrahman Gülbeyaz said trust cannot be rebuilt through political rhetoric alone and that democracy requires the state to adapt to society’s diversity, rather than the other way around.




Professor Abdurrahman Gülbeyaz of Nagasaki University spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, examining it not merely in terms of ending the conflict and removing weapons from the equation, but also as a process of rebuilding society's political, social and cultural relationships.




Gülbeyaz discussed the conditions necessary for a democratic society, the social and political foundations of lasting peace, the need to redefine relations between the state and society, and the resolution of the Kurdish question. He emphasised the importance of building a shared life while preserving differences.




Democracy means the state adapting to society




Is it enough to understand the concept of a democratic society solely in terms of political rights? What are its social and cultural requirements?




I would like to begin with a minor objection to the premise of this question. The moment we reduce a democratic society to a catalogue of political rights, we risk inadvertently turning society once again into an object on the state's table of legal and administrative classifications. Political rights are, of course, indispensable. Without freedom of expression and association,

author: Unknown
title: Court orders release of comedian Deniz Göktaş after sentences of 19 months and 5 days
content:
The first hearing in the trial of detained comedian Deniz Göktaş, who faced allegations of “insulting the president,” “inciting the public to hatred and hostility,” and “praising crime and criminals,” was held at the Istanbul 14th Criminal Court of First Instance.




In his defense, Göktaş said the charges against him were based on four sentences he had used in his show Dead Sea. He stated that he had delivered these lines hundreds of times in different cities across Turkey and that audience reactions to the performances had consisted solely of laughter and applause.




Göktaş argued that criminalizing political humor and criticism could lead to self-censorship. He rejected the charges and requested acquittal.




‘I have been in a cell for 88 days’




Göktaş also drew attention to the length of his detention, telling the panel of judges: “I’ve been in a cell for 88 days. Of course, I’m going to speak.”




In his defense, Göktaş said that describing the president as a “shy dictator” was a political characterization and stated that he would continue expressing his criticism through humor.




He also referred to complaints filed against him through CIMER, Turkey’s presidential communications center. Göktaş said that a total of 185 complaints had been included in the case file and that they were the result of an organized campaign.

author: Unknown
title: Shengal Mountain is the guarantee of life
content:
Shengal Mountain is not merely a place of refuge, but the only guarantee of survival for Yazidis. As the withdrawal of the International Coalition approaches and the risk of a potential security vacuum grows, attempts at disarmament and threats against those defending the mountain are fuelling fears of a repeat of the 2014 scenario. This comes despite the fact that the people of Shengal have received no meaningful support from the state beyond empty promises. For Yazidis, the defence forces on Shengal Mountain are not merely an armed force. They are the last stronghold of their existence and their only guarantee after they were abandoned by all forces and states during one of the darkest periods in their history. On the map, Shengal Mountain is not simply a military zone. It is the only path to survival, a mother who embraced her children when everyone else left them to die.




No one remained when all regular and irregular forces withdrew from Shengal. At that moment, tens of thousands of Yazidis had no option other than the mountain, which protected them from abduction and death. The people of the mountain armed themselves with the limited means available to them and fought to stop the attacks by ISIS mercenaries. For this reason, any suggestion that the mountain should be taken out of the hands of its people amounts to depriving the victims of their last refuge. Today, we a

author: Unknown
title: Süleyman Çarnewa: Art’s role in peace is as vital as politics
content:
Koma Amed, one of the signatories of the “1,001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Speaking on behalf of the group, Süleyman Çarnewa stressed the importance of art and artists on the path to peace. 




Leaving behind the crowds of Beyoğlu and walking for a while through its narrow side streets, we came across the familiar sign. The moment we stepped into the institution that has nurtured countless artists since 1991, we were greeted warmly with broad smiles.







 







Koma Amed, which made a major impact in the 1990s, is continuing rehearsals at the Mesopotamia Cultural Centre ahead of its concert tomorrow, 30 September, at the Harbiye Open-Air Theatre.




Last year, the group was enthusiastically welcomed in Diyarbakır (Amed) after 30 years, but the same enthusiasm in Istanbul was cut short when the Governor’s Office banned its concert. The group also announced that it had cancelled its Ankara concert because of attacks on Rojava. Koma Amed eventually ended its 30-year absence from the Istanbul stage by lighting the Newroz fire in Yenikapı.




Koma Amed was also among the first signatories of the “1,001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, launched on 12 September.




We signed the campaign because we need peace

title: Monitoring and Evaluation Committee on the Peace Process convenes again
content:
The Monitoring and Evaluation Committee, established as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, convened in Ankara on Monday for its second meeting. The meeting at the Presidential Complex was chaired by Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz.




Participants included Justice Minister Akın Gürlek, Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Interior Minister Mustafa Çiftçi, Defense Minister Yaşar Güler, intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalın, Secretary-General of the Presidency Hakkı Susmaz, and Secretary-General of the National Security Council Okay Memiş. The discussions reportedly focused on the current state of the process and the work of the four subcommittees.




Four subcommittees accompany the process




The Monitoring and Evaluation Committee first convened on August 24. During the approximately three-and-a-half-hour meeting, four subcommittees were established to address different aspects of the process. These are the Subcommittee on Justice and Legal Affairs, the Subcommittee on Monitoring and Assessment, the Subcommittee on Social Integration, and the Subcommittee on Disarmament and Strategic Coordination.




Speaking on Sunday ahead of today’s meeting, Yılmaz said that the committee’s task is to monitor the process. He stated that the four subcommittees are dealing with legal issues, social integration, developments on the ground, and disarmament and strategic coordination

author: Unknown
title: Lawyer Çakas: Release of ill prisoners must not be political bargaining
content:
The release of seriously ill prisoners suffering from severe health problems continues to be obstructed on various grounds. The health of prisoners who remain behind bars despite having completed their sentences or meeting the conditions for release is deteriorating by the day.




Prisoners' families and human rights organisations have condemned the failure to implement release decisions, calling for the removal of obstacles to the release of ill prisoners and protection of their right to life.




Lawyer Yusuf Çakas, a member of the Amed (Diyarbakır) Prison Commission of the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD), spoke to ANF about the prison sentence enforcement system, decisions by the Forensic Medicine Institute, and the legal and practical obstacles faced by ill prisoners.




Prison conditions are designed to make prisoners ill




Çakas said that any discussion of ill prisoners must begin with a proper understanding of what it means to be ill and the conditions inside prisons.




Çakas also said: “An ill prisoner is someone whose health has deteriorated to the point where they can no longer sustain their life under prison conditions. Being ill means not being healthy. In international literature, illness is essentially understood as the absence of health. If a person is not healthy, they are ill.




What is a prison? A prison is the institutionalisation of conditions

title: Varto resistance against geothermal power plant project to continue on 8 October, day of ispection
content:
The vigil launched against a geothermal power plant (JES) project planned by the US-based IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim A.Ş. in Xwarik village, in the Varto district of Muş, is continuing on its 148th day. On Sunday, Tülay Hatimoğulları, co-chair of the DEM Party, and Sümeyye Boz, DEM Party MP for Muş, visited the vigil organised by the Varto Ecology Platform Youth Council to show their solidarity.




Speaking during the visit, Sümeyye Boz said that the people’s main concern was the struggle, adding that the resistance of Varto residents defending their land and water would continue on 8 October.




We will continue to make your voice heard




DEM Party Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları underlined that the struggle being waged in Varto had also been raised in parliament and in Ankara. Pointing out that the geothermal power plant project would cause environmental destruction, Hatimoğulları said that cancelling the company’s licence was important. She criticised the licensing processes for mining, geothermal power plant (JES), hydroelectric power plant (HES) and wind power plant (RES) projects in Turkey, which she said were being pursued under the name of “renewable energy”.

title: Kocaağa: Debt brake and social cuts deepened Germany’s crisis
content:
Muhlis Kocaağa, a member of Bremen's state parliament for Die Linke (The Left), discussed the reasons behind the rise of the far right in Germany, particularly in the eastern states, and Die Linke's role in opposing this trend.




Kocaağa said shrinking state budgets, the debt brake (Schuldenbremse) and cuts to social services had disrupted social stability. He also highlighted shortcomings in infrastructure and public services related to migration policies.




He said Germany was facing global geopolitical crises, rising energy costs, challenges arising from industrial transformation and a deepening housing crisis. Kocaağa stressed the urgent need to develop public and social policies to address these problems.




There has recently been a significant rise in the far right in Germany, particularly in eastern and North-Eastern Germany. How do you interpret this situation? Do you think the state is, in a sense, paving the way for it?




I assume you are referring to the state elections and the political situation in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, one of Germany's coastal states. There are two main reasons for this situation. My view differs somewhat from that of other politicians, and I have expressed it in political discussions as well.

title: Ronahî Culture and Arts Commune established in Zurich
content:
The Ronahî Culture and Arts Commune was established in Zurich on Sunday, following work carried out by TEV-ÇAND.




At the event for the official declaration of the commune, Fahriye Iliş. Serhat Hülakü, a member of TEV-ÇAND, then took the floor and highlighted the importance of organising cultural and artistic activities according to a communal approach.







 







Hülakü spoke about the role of cultural and artistic activities in building Kurdish national unity, adding that work in the fields of culture and art constitutes an important area of resistance and achievement against assimilation policies pursued across the four parts of Kurdistan. Hülakü also expressed his enthusiasm about the establishment of the Ronahî Culture and Arts Centre.




Representatives from the four parts of Kurdistan also spoke at the event, emphasising the importance of carrying out cultural and artistic activities with an awareness of national unity.




Activities to be carried out in four areas




Mehmet Akdoğan, another TEV-ÇAND member, said that following three months of work, cultural and artistic activities had been reorganised from the perspective of a communal system. He announced that the organisation had been established under the name “Navenda Çanda Ronahî” (Ronahî Culture Centre).
