title: Second phase of mine clearance launched in Rojava
content:
Mine clearance and removal of war remnants operations continue in the countryside of Serêkaniyê, Til Temir, and Zirgan, as part of efforts to secure roads, villages, and agricultural land ahead of the return of displaced people to their areas.




The Mine Action Office in Heseke provided ANHA with an overview of its work map and the latest updates regarding mine clearance and war-remnant removal operations in the region.




According to the office, mine clearance operations on and around the main road in Serêkaniyê are nearing completion and the second phase has been launched, with clearance operations now beginning in villages.




The office explained that mine clearance operations are currently targeting villages located along the line extending from Til Temir and Zirgan towards the city of Serêkaniyê, in addition to villages located along the M4 highway towards the southern countryside of the city.




The office stated: “The clearance of the main road connecting the cities of Dirbêsiyê and Serêkaniyê, which passes through al-Asadiyah village and extends to the Turkish military base located in Bab al-Faraj village along the main road, has been completed. The clearance operations covered the road and both sides of it to a distance of 25 metres."

title: Women in Amed call for a united struggle against femicide
content:
Following the femicide of Ayfer Çakmak, women in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) called for a united struggle against patriarchal violence. At the initiative of the DEM Party Women’s Council, numerous women gathered at a busy intersection in the Bağlar district. Ayfer Çakmak, 32, was killed by her husband, O.Ç., on September 25 in the 5 Nisan neighborhood of Bağlar. While the 37-year-old perpetrator was arrested after the killing, the investigation into the femicide is ongoing.




Participants in the rally included DEM Party Women’s Council spokesperson, Halide Türkoğlu, representatives of political parties and women’s organizations, and Amed Co-Mayor Serra Bucak. Ruçem Vefa Elyakut, co-chair of the DBP’s Amed provincial organization, pointed out that women are often killed by men in their immediate surroundings. “Enough is enough. We will not remain silent in the face of these killings,” Elyakut said.




‘Violence against women is a structural problem’




Serra Bucak rejected treating femicides as isolated incidents unrelated to one another. Violence against women is a structural problem and must be addressed accordingly, she said. Bucak particularly criticized shortcomings in the justice system and in the implementation of Law No. 6284 on the protection of women from violence. title: The Turkification of Kurdish place names and the restoration of names in the peace process
content:
Across Kurdistan, dozens of cities, hundreds of districts, and thousands of villages, neighborhoods, highland pastures, and waterways were known for centuries by names rooted in the languages of the peoples who lived there. Beginning with the establishment of the Republic, administrative renaming policies erased a large proportion of these names from official maps. Today, at a time when the peace process is once again being discussed, restoring these names will be a concrete test of the seriousness of the process.




Beginning in the 1940s, and particularly through assimilation policies carried out by the “Specialized Board for Name Changes,” established in 1957, the names of more than ten thousand settlements were changed, according to official records. Names of Kurdish, Armenian, Syriac, Laz, and Zaza origin constituted the overwhelming majority of those targeted. Across the geography stretching from Diyarbakır to Hakkari, and from Mardin to Muş, changing the name of a village was not merely a matter of replacing a sign. It was also an attempt to erase from official records the memory, sense of belonging, and connection to the land embodied in that name.




The renaming of settlements was not merely an administrative measure; it was also part of a strategy to render a people’s presence in their own geography invisible. The name of a mountain, a stream, or a village was amon

title: Peshmerga Ministry voices concern over the withdrawal of U.S. forces
content:
The Kurdistan Regional Government’s Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs issued a statement regarding the withdrawal of United States (US) forces from Iraq and the Kurdistan Region.




Under the agreement reached between the Iraqi federal government and the US and International Coalition forces, the withdrawal of American forces from all of Iraq and the Kurdistan Region is expected to be completed by September 30.




Highlighting the sensitivity of the current period, the statement on Monday said that the continuing instability in Iraq and the broader Middle East could have consequences beyond individual states, calling for vigilance and sound political decision-making.




According to the statement, more than 1,000 drones and ballistic missiles have targeted the Kurdistan Region during the conflict, with some striking civilian areas and causing deaths, injuries and material damage.




“The United States leaving the Kurdistan Region behind in such a complex regional situation, without providing any defense system, is a cause for concern,” the statement said, stressing that the Iraqi federal government is primarily responsible for protecting the Kurdistan Region’s airspace.




The ministry also stressed the “Peshmerga forces remain prepared for new security developments and capable of responding to threats.”

title: Third group of IDPs from Serêkaniyê to return home
content:
Zehra Semio, a member of the Serêkaniyê Forcibly Displaced Persons Committee, announced that the third group of people forcibly displaced from the Serêkaniyê countryside will return to their homes on Sunday.




Semio said that the third group, consisting of more than 500 families who are currently living in schools and residential centers in Hesekê, will return to their areas between the towns of Menacîr and Til Helef, west of Serêkaniyê. She added that the number of returning families may change.




The second group, consisting of around 700 families—nearly 7,000 people—who had been living in Serêkaniyê Camp, returned on September 8 to their homes in 55 villages in the countryside of Serêkaniyê, Zirgan, and Til Temir.




Background




Serêkaniyê is located in the Jazira (Cizire) Canton on the border with North Kurdistan, opposite the Ceylanpınar district of Urfa. Due to its water resources, fertile lands, and position along important trade routes, the city has been considered a strategically significant center for centuries. Its population consisted of Kurds, Arabs, Armenians, Syriacs, Circassians, and Chechens, making Serêkaniyê one of the most diverse places in the region.

title: Bakırhan: We will discuss our demands in the second phase
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) held its third Ordinary Provincial Congress at the ÇandAmed Congress Centre in Amed (Diyarbakır). DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan attended the congress alongside numerous representatives of political parties and civil society organisations.




A poster of Abdullah Öcalan was displayed in the congress hall, while participants chanted slogans including “Bijî Serok Apo” (Long live Abdullah Öcalan), “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs never die), “Bijî berxwedana zindanan” (Long live the resistance in prisons), “Bijî berxwedana ciwanan” (Long live the resistance of the youth) and “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom).




A moment of silence was observed in memory of those martyred in the Kurdish freedom struggle, followed by a video presentation highlighting the work, demonstrations and activities carried out in Amed.




DEM Party Amed Provincial Co-Chair Gülşen Özer also addressed the congress and reaffirmed their determination to continue the struggle.




We will discuss our demands in the second phase




DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan addressed the congress, paying tribute to those who had contributed to bringing the ongoing process to its current stage and sending greetings to prisoners and those living in exile.

title: Ipek: Looking only at the final link in child worker deaths is wrong - Part Two
content:
Deniz Ipek, a Class A occupational safety expert working with the İSİG Assembly, spoke to ANF about child labour in Turkey and the reasons behind the rising number of worker deaths.




Part one of this interview can be read 

here

. 




Child labour is rising in small and informal workplaces




Ipek said child labour is now used in sectors such as industry, construction and textiles, increasing the risk of death and serious injury among children.  Ipek continued: “We cannot explain the increase in child worker deaths solely by a lack of safety measures in workplaces. We need to look at the fact that more children are entering production, working longer hours and performing more dangerous jobs. In the past, child labour was mainly associated with agriculture, small businesses and informal workshops, but today it extends across a wide range of sectors, including industry, construction, logistics, motorcycle delivery, metalwork, textiles and services. MESEM has also made the presence of children in businesses widespread through the education system rather than exceptional. As the number of working children and their exposure to hazards increase, so does the risk of death and serious injury.

author: Unknown
title: Police raid memorial for martyrs in Hannover
content:
German police raided a hall in Hannover where a memorial event for the Martyrs of Kurdistan’s Freedom Movement was due to take place.




Police entered the hall and prevented the event, citing the grounds that “memorial events for PKK members are not permitted in this hall.” Following this, Kurds moved to the Hannover Democratic Kurdish Community Centre (DKTM), where they sought to hold the memorial event. However, hundreds of German police officers surrounded the DKTM.







 







Xoşnav Ata, co-chair of the Association of Martyrs’ Families (KOMAW), said that a large number of people had been surrounded by police in the area around the association.




Ata said: “Around 200 of us are currently being held hostage, and we are being subjected to ill-treatment. We want our people in Hannover, and everyone else, to hear our voices. We call on everyone to rush to the association.”

title: PJAK member Ehwen Çiyako calls for joint struggle
content:
Ehwen Çiyako, a member of the Assembly of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), spoke at the conference “The Human Rights Crisis in Iran: Toward a Collaborative Joint Initiative,” held in Oslo, the capital of Norway. Çiyako stated that executions, torture and arbitrary arrests in Iran are indicators of systematic human rights violations.




Speaking at the conference, held on September 25–26, 2026, Çiyako gave an assessment of the human rights situation in Iran.




“Kurdistan and Baluchistan are facing serious violations”




Çiyako said that executions, torture and arbitrary arrests could not be treated as isolated incidents, saying they were evidence of a systematic structure. “Security and economic pressures are not at the same level throughout the region. However, areas such as Kurdistan and Baluchistan face serious discrimination and violations in multiple respects, intertwined with political, ethnic, national, linguistic and religious differences,” Çiyako said.




Emphasizing the importance of developing cooperation between different political and civil society forces on the basis of human rights, Çiyako said: “We may have different views on political thought and forms of governance for the future, but we must unite around the right to life, freedom, human dignity, justice and political participation.”

title: Tülay Hatimoğulları: As Kurds, as Alevis, and as women, we demand democratic governance
content:
DEM Party Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları attended the 2nd Ordinary Provincial Congress of the party’s Erzurum Provincial Organization.




‘Every congress is a political breakthrough’




Speaking at the congress, Tülay Hatimoğulları said that the gathering also represented a political breakthrough: “At a time when politics in Turkey is being restructured, and at a time when we are building the Peace and Democratic Society Process, every congress we hold is also a political breakthrough.”




Drawing attention to the ongoing economic crisis and growing impoverishment, Hatimoğulları said that the country was facing extreme poverty as a result of the government’s policies.




‘Turkey has become a hub for major fraud’




“The corruption spree enabled by the government is responsible for the swindle of the century,” Hatimoğulları said. Recalling major fraud scandals of the 1980s and 1990s, she also drew attention to the latest alleged schemes involving Tera and Pusula Holding.




Hatimoğulları said: “Unfortunately, they have turned the country into a hub for major fraud. The stock market scandal was obvious to everyone. The Capital Markets Board knew about it. The state knew, the government knew. Everyone knew, but they turned a blind eye to it.”

author: Unknown
title: Excavation work at mass grave in Shengal Cemetery completed
content:
The Martyrs Institution announced that excavation work at the mass grave in Şerfedîn Cemetery, located in the Sinûnê subdistrict of Shengal, which began six days ago, has been completed.




On the final day of the excavation, specialist technical and forensic teams affiliated with the Directorate for the Excavation and Preservation of Monuments and Mass Graves carefully carried out the recovery of the remains. The work was conducted in accordance with international technical and forensic standards, rules and protocols, with due regard for the dignity of those who lost their lives.




Following their recovery, the remains were handed over to the Forensic Medicine Department of the Iraqi Ministry of Health after the completion of the official and legal documentation process. The final stage of the examination of the remains will be completed at the Ministry of Health’s Forensic Medicine Department.




DNA samples collected from families who lost loved ones will be compared and matched with biological data obtained from the remains. Once their identities have been established, the remains will be handed over to their families so that they can hold farewell ceremonies in accordance with their traditions and beliefs.

title: Evin Women’s Cooperative: A space for solidarity and production in Van
content:
Women in cities across Kurdistan are participating in social and economic life through cooperatives in response to policies rooted in a male-dominated mentality that seek to exclude women from public life.




NûJINHA published a feature about women taking part in production through cooperatives in many cities. Among the cooperatives are the Ortak Yaşam Women’s Cooperative in Mazıdağ (Şemrex), Mardin (Mêrdîn), and the Varto Hafızası Women’s Initiative Production and Business Cooperative in Varto (Gimgim), Muş (Mûş). In Van (Wan), women at the Evin Women’s Cooperative, established in 2015, aim to make women’s labour visible and develop collective production.




Şehriban Adsaz, a fashion design graduate who has worked at the cooperative as an instructor and producer for the past three years, spoke to NûJINHA about the work they carried out.




From seven women to 20




Şehriban Adsaz said the cooperative began its work with seven women and that the number later grew to 20. Adsaz said it was very important to her to bring out the potential women already possess and continued: “Our cooperative is not merely a business model; it is a platform for solidarity where women support one another, produce together and make decisions together. title: Kurdish entrepreneurs discuss economy and political process in Switzerland
content:
Kurdish entrepreneurs from Switzerland, Germany, and France gathered in Egerkingen, Switzerland, for a meeting on economic prospects, new technologies, and the role of the diaspora. The conference, organized by the Swiss Democratic Employers’ Association (SDAV), focused primarily on artificial intelligence and its economic applications. However, the discussion also expanded to include the economic development of Kurdistan and the peace and democratic society process.




Participants in the event in the canton of Solothurn included DEM Party parliamentary group deputy chair Sezai Temelli; economist and former HDP MP Erol Katırcıoğlu; Hasan Siral, chair of the Association of Kurdish Entrepreneurs in Germany (AKEE); and AKEE board member Leylan Uca. Abdullah Ülmez, deputy chair of the Association of Kurdish Businesspeople in France (UEFK), and other board members also traveled from France to attend the meeting.




Artificial intelligence and the economy of tomorrow




Opening the event, SDAV board member Eyyüp Kavak said the association was closely following developments in Kurdistan and supported the ongoing political process. At the same time, he said they wanted to explore how Kurdish entrepreneurs could make use of artificial intelligence and technological developments.

title: Heyva Sor a Kurdistanê-Italia celebrates 11th anniversary in Livorno
content:
Kurdish Red Crescent Heyva Sor a Kurdistanê-Italia celebrated its 11th anniversary on Saturday evening with a well-attended event at the historic Fortezza Vecchia in Livorno. Representatives of Kurdish and Italian organizations reflected on the solidarity work carried out over the past years. The event continued with Kurdish cuisine, music, and Kurdish traditional dance Govend.




Following an opening by moderator Melenia Carnavale, speakers included Ali Can Yıldız, chair of the Italian section of the Kurdish Red Crescent, and its secretary, Barbara Mancini. The event was also attended by Abdulkarim Omar, who is responsible for Rojava’s foreign relations; representatives of Heyva Sor a Kurdistanê in Germany and the Kurdistan Information Office; as well as representatives of Un Ponte Per and the Waldensian Church.




Other participants included Dr. Sherwan Bery of Heyva Sor a Kurd in Rojava, Giulia Torrini of the Italian Health Committee for Rojava, and Comas Nebot of the Barcelona city administration.






















Eleven years of cross-border solidarity




The speeches reflected on the work of Heyva Sor a Kurdistanê-Italia since its establishment. Particular emphasis was placed on the ties that have developed between Kurdish and Italian society, as well as the various aid and solidarity projects carried out over the years.

title: Great turned out on first day of Amed’s 10th Book Fair
content:
The 10th Amed Book Fair, organized by TÜYAP Fair Organization Group in cooperation with the Publishers Association of Turkey and with the support of the Amed Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DTSO), opened on Saturday at the Mesopotamia International Fair and Congress Center. The fair will run until 4 October, and its opening day attracted considerable interest. Hundreds of people attended the opening, alongside representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.




125 publishers and civil society organizations present at the fair




The opening speech was delivered by Ilhan Ersözlü, General Manager of TÜYAP Fairs Organization Inc. and President of the Turkish Fair Organizers Association. Ersözlü said that the previous nine book fairs had attracted more than 1.5 million visitors in total, with approximately 1,300 exhibitors participating. He noted that 125 publishing houses and civil society organizations are taking part in this year’s 10th fair.




The presence of the publishers participating here is extremely valuable to us all




Nazlı Berivan Ak, Secretary General of the Publishers Association of Turkey, addressed the audience. “We are representatives of a tradition that stretches from dengbêjs [Kurdish traditional singers and storytellers], folk poets and writers to the present day. The greatest significance of this fair today lies in the fact that y

author: Unknown
title: Ill prisoners Mehmet Elçe and Abdülhalik Oral must be released, says the IHD
content:
The Prison Commission of the Istanbul branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) held its 757th “F Sitting” protest outside the association’s building in Beyoğlu, Istanbul, to draw attention to the health conditions of sick prisoners. The protest highlighted the situation of Mehmet Elçe (62), a sick prisoner with a 93% disability who is being held at Elazığ R-Type Closed Prison.




Numerous relatives of sick prisoners and human rights defenders attended the protest. A banner reading “Release Sick Prisoner Mehmet Elçe” was displayed, and participants chanted slogans including “Release sick prisoners” and “Treatment is a right; it cannot be denied.”




The Initiative for the Freedom of Sick Prisoners gathered on Sakarya Street in Ankara for its 629th weekly protest. This week’s action drew attention to the situation of sick prisoner Abdülhalik Oral, who is being held at Kırıkkale Hacılar F-Type Closed Prison.

author: Unknown
title: Saygı: Receiving support in one’s mother tongue is vital in combating violence against women
content:
In Turkey, femicides and cases of violence against women are increasing day by day, contrary to the rhetoric of those in power.




In Kurdistan, women are subjected to attacks not only by family members and people close to them, but also by state security forces, such as police officers and soldiers, as part of special warfare policies. These attacks, which result in the killing of women, have continued for many years as part of policies targeting the struggle of Kurdish women.




203 women killed in the first eight months of 2026




The fact that perpetrators of violence against women receive light sentences or no punishment at all, both in Turkey and Kurdistan, is increasingly paving the way for further violence. According to 2026 data from the We Will Stop Femicide Platform, 203 women were killed in the first eight months of 2026, while the deaths of 215 women were recorded as “suspicious.”




In Kurdistan, cases of violence against and the killing of women targeted by special warfare practices are also increasing day by day. According to data from the Amed Branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD), 38 women were killed in the first six months of 2026.




Attacks against women are carried out particularly by men described as those closest to them. In Kurdistan, however, women are also subjected to attacks by state security forces, including police officers and soldie

author: Unknown
title: Ipek: Looking only at the final link in child worker deaths is wrong - Part One
content:
In Turkey, where cheap labour is widely used, the number of child workers has begun to rise, particularly as the economic crisis has deepened. According to data from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜIK), the number of working children stood at 720,000 as of 2019.




The number of child workers began to increase further with the introduction of Vocational Education Centres (MESEM). The lack of inspections at workplaces affiliated with MESEM has also led to an increase in child worker deaths. According to data from the Workers’ Health and Work Safety Assembly (İSİG), 62 children lost their lives in work-related deaths in the first eight months of 2026.




Deniz Ipek, a Class A occupational safety expert working with the ISIG Observatory, spoke to ANF about child labour in Turkey and the reasons behind the rising number of worker deaths.




I believe the real figure should be counted in the millions




Ipek said the exact number of child workers in Turkey as of 2026 is unknown and that although some figures provide a reference point, the full scale cannot be determined. Ipek continued: “We do not know exactly how many child workers are working in Turkey today. TÜIK’s most recent special Child Labour Force Survey covering the entire 5–17 age group was conducted in 2019, and the number of children engaged in economic activity was reported as 720,000. author: Unknown
title: Karasu: Rıza Altun’s struggle will always guide us
content:
Rıza Altun, one of the leading cadres of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, and those who lost their lives in the Freedom Movement’s struggle were commemorated at an event held in Paris.




In a video message to the commemoration, KCK (Kurdistan Communities Union) Executive Council member Mustafa Karasu spoke about Rıza Altun’s activities from the early years of his involvement in the struggle until his death. Karasu said that Altun assumed responsibilities in various areas of the Freedom Movement, from organizing work in Ankara’s Tuzluçayır neighborhood to Antep, from resistance in prison to his activities in Kurdistan and diplomatic work, highlighting his qualities as an organizer and activist.




Karasu also saluted commemorations for the martyrs that have been held in many cities across Kurdistan over the past month after the announcement of their deaths. He said that the public’s participation in and support for these commemorations had given them great morale.




















The message sent by KCK Executive Council member Mustafa Karasu to the commemoration in the French capital is as follows:




“I greet all our people who have gathered to commemorate Comrade Rıza. This is the seventh anniversary of Comrade Rıza’s death. Comrades Baz and Garzan, together with Comrade Rıza, lost their lives in an airstrike on September 25, 2019.




As we remember these comrades, co

author: Unknown
title: Peshmerga Ministry: International Coalition’s financial assistance has ended
content:
The Secretary-General of the Ministry of Peshmerga in the Kurdistan Region, Lieutenant General Bakhtiar Mohammed Sadiq, confirmed on Saturday that the Global Coalition has halted financial assistance to the Peshmerga forces.




Bakhtiar told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the period specified for financial assistance provided by the Global Coalition to the Peshmerga forces had ended in accordance with the prior agreement concluded between the two sides, noting that the financial assistance for August and September 2026 was the final payment under the agreement.




He continued that “the memorandum of understanding was in effect from September 21, 2022, to September 21, 2026, for a period of four years. The memorandum has expired, and thus the transfer of financial amounts by the Global Coalition has also ended.”




He pointed out that “the Ministry of Peshmerga had announced that the financial assistance provided by the Global Coalition for August and September 2026 was distributed last Thursday, September 24, and this was the final payment according to the agreement.”




Bakhtiar confirmed that “we requested the federal government to compensate for this assistance by adjusting the salaries of the Peshmerga forces in line with the Iraqi forces.”

author: Unknown
title: People in Diyadin demonstrate against gold mining: “Killing nature means killing life”
content:
Under the slogan “We Protect Our Land,” large numbers of people demonstrated in the district of Diyadin in Ağro province against gold mining using cyanide. The environmental rally was organized by the DEM Party and the Mesopotamia Ecology Movement. The demonstrators marched from the post office on İnönü Street to the central bus terminal. Chants included “Bê ax jiyan nabe” [There is no life without land] and “Kurdistan nabe goristan” [Kurdistan will not become a graveyard.] Banners and placards carried messages including “Kurdistan is not your mining zone,” “Killing nature means killing life,” and “Hands off my air, my water, my land, and my forests.”







Participants in the rally included DBP and DEM Party co-chairs Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar and Tuncer Bakırhan, as well as representatives of various environmental groups. The protest was directed against a gold mining project near the village of Mollakara. Environmental organizations and municipalities in the region have warned in particular about the potential impact of cyanide use on the Murat River and its watershed.




‘We are fighting for every place that is being plundered’




Alev Yılmaz of the Varto Ecology Platform recalled the resistance against energy and resource extraction projects in Varto, which has been ongoing for more than 140 days. She stressed that the protest there was not limited to their own region: “We a

author: Unknown
title: Saturday Mothers demand justice for Ibrahim and Edip Çelik
content:
At their 1,122nd vigil in Istanbul’s Galatasaray Square, the Saturday Mothers commemorated Ibrahim and Edip Çelik. The father and son were abducted and forcibly disappeared by the radical Islamist Hezbollah on July 10, 1994, in the northern Kurdish province of Batman. There has been no sign of them since.




Relatives of the disappeared and numerous human rights activists took part in the vigil. They carried photographs of people who disappeared or were killed in state custody, as well as red carnations. The statement on the case was read by lawyer Jiyan Kaya of the Istanbul branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD).




IHD points to links with the state apparatus




Kaya recalled that the Hezbollah death squads abducted and forcibly disappeared numerous people during the 1990s. She also pointed to the role of state structures, saying there was established evidence that Hezbollah could rely on protection and support from parts of the security and administrative bureaucracy in carrying out these crimes and that its activities were tolerated by the state. As a result, there was no effective state intervention against these crimes.




What happened on July 10, 1994?




On the evening of July 10, 1994, four masked and armed men knocked on the door of the Çelik family home. Under the pretext that they wanted him to show them a location, they took 50-year-old Ibrahim Çelik wi

author: Unknown
title: Iraq announces new plan to bring weapons under state control
content:
Iraq is preparing a new plan to bring weapons outside state control under the authority of the state. According to Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, negotiations with armed groups over surrendering their weapons are continuing. “This issue is an internal matter for Iraq. We are presenting a new plan for this dossier. Negotiations and talks with the relevant parties over the handover of weapons are ongoing,” Hussein said on Friday.




The foreign minister linked the initiative to the approaching end of the mission of the US-led International Coalition. Its withdrawal from Iraq is scheduled to be completed by September 30. Hussein said the date should not be seen as the beginning of a security vacuum, but rather as a transition into a new phase.




Talks on US sanctions against Iranian airlines




Hussein also commented on US sanctions against Iranian airlines. He said Baghdad was in contact with Washington on the issue and had officially informed the Iranian side of the decision concerning the entry of Iranian aircraft into Iraqi airports. The talks follow measures against the international operations of Iranian airlines announced by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on September 22.




“Iraqi economy is the first victim”




Referring to the war and regional tensions, Hussein also warned of the economic consequences for his country. “The Iraqi economy is the first victim of

author: Unknown
title: Balance of power is shifting in Iraq
content:
The 12-year mission of the international coalition against ISIS in Iraq will officially end on 30 September. The date will also mark the end of the US military presence in the country that began with the 2003 invasion. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has described the deadline as “fixed and final”, while Baghdad is also accelerating plans to bring weapons under exclusive state control. The question of what awaits Iraq once the withdrawal is complete is critical both for the country’s internal balance of power and the reshaping of regional dynamics.




What lies behind the withdrawal decision?




An agreement reached between Baghdad and Washington in 2024 provided for the phased conclusion of the international coalition’s mission against ISIS. Bases in central Iraq were evacuated in the first phase, while hundreds of troops and air defence systems remained around Erbil (Hewlêr) in Southern Kurdistan (Başur).




Ali al-Zaidi, who became prime minister in May 2026, travelled to Washington in July and met US President Donald Trump at the White House. Trump said during the meeting that the US military presence in Iraq was no longer necessary and indicated that the relationship would increasingly focus on companies and investment.




Talks between the Baghdad government and US Central Command (CENTCOM) subsequently clarified the timetable for the coalition forces’ withdrawal fr

author: Unknown
title: Mithat Sancar concludes talks in Switzerland
content:
İmralı Delegation member Mithat Sancar traveled to Switzerland at the invitation of the “Peace and Solidarity Platform,” which brings together political parties, trade unions, and civil society organizations, to hold a series of meetings. Sancar participated in events organized by the platform and also held separate meetings at the Federal Parliament with delegations from the Socialist Party (SP) and the Green Party (Grüne).




Sancar took part in a roundtable meeting with the leadership of the Swiss Democracy Platform. Finally, he attended a panel organized by the Peace and Solidarity Platform on the latest developments in Turkey and the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




The panel was moderated by Rebekka Wyler, General Secretary of VPOD (Swiss Public Service Union), with İmralı Delegation member Mithat Sancar and Meral Çiçek, representative of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe, participating as speakers.




Mithat Sancar gave a comprehensive presentation on the Peace and Democratic Society Process.






















‘There is a need for a climate of trust’




Sancar emphasized that some progress had been made in the ongoing talks between the Turkish state and Abdullah Öcalan, and that certain reciprocal steps had been taken. He stressed that the issue of trust, however, remained a key matter that needed to be addressed.

author: Unknown
title: Tunç: Process must not be left at the mercy of the state
content:
Writer Aziz Tunç assessed the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that despite setbacks, disruptions and obstacles, the process was continuing. He said the main problem was that resolving the Kurdish question had not been placed at its centre.




Tunç said past experiences offered important lessons regarding the state and argued that approaching the process solely in terms of disarmament would not produce a lasting solution. He emphasised the need for all sections of society to become more actively involved in the process and said: “This process is too important and valuable to be left at the mercy of the state.”




Tunç said the process was moving forward, but not as it should, pointing to significant obstacles at every stage. He recalled that the atmosphere when the process first began had created an expectation that the issue would be resolved within a few months. Nearly two years later, however, he said the process was still moving “at idle speed”, repeatedly encountering obstacles and difficulties.




Tunç identified a fundamental mismatch between the process itself and the way it was being conducted. He said the Kurdish question was not being sufficiently discussed within a process presented as seeking to resolve it. He said, “Of course, a process discussing the resolution of the Kurdish question cannot move forward without discussing the

author: Unknown
title: MEP Lucano calls for Öcalan’s freedom
content:
The process that began following Abdullah Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and a Democratic Society is being closely followed not only in Turkey and Kurdistan but also across Europe. The progress of the process, the legal and political steps that need to be taken, and Öcalan’s status are among the key issues in international discussions.




One of the figures closely following these discussions is Domenico “Mimmo” Lucano, an Italian MEP. Lucano’s relationship with the Kurds dates back nearly 30 years, before he became mayor of Riace. In 1998, a boat carrying Kurdish refugees arrived in Riace, a small coastal town in Calabria. This became a turning point not only for the town but also for Lucano’s political life. The solidarity that began with the settlement of Kurdish refugees and the opening of vacant houses to them laid some of the foundations for the migrant reception experience that would later become internationally known as the “Riace model.”







 







Years later, after being elected to the European Parliament, Lucano described his bond with the Kurds in these words: “I became mayor thanks to the Kurds.” Referring also to Öcalan’s arrival in Italy in 1998, Lucano argues that Öcalan must be able to participate freely in the Peace and Democratic Society Process currently underway.

author: Unknown
title: Memorial for Rıza Altun and Freedom Martyrs to be held in London
content:
A memorial for Rıza Altun, one of the founding members of the PKK, and the Kurdistan Freedom Martyrs will be held in London tomorrow, Sunday.




The commemoration will be held at the Haringey Kurdish Community Centre under the slogan “Şehîd Heqîqet e”. The families of the martyrs, as well as families of those whose deaths have recently been announced and whose relatives live in the UK will attend the memorial. Following the event, the families will receive condolences.




A special stage is being prepared for the commemoration, featuring photographs of Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas whose deaths have been announced recently. Artists will perform songs in memory of the martyrs, and video presentations will also be screened.




Altun's to be highlighted




A video presentation about the life and struggle of Rıza Altun will be shown at the commemoration. A member of the founding generation of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, Altun took on responsibilities in various fields throughout his five decades of activism, from Amed Prison to political and diplomatic work in Europe.




Rıza Altun’s death on 25 September 2019, was announced in May 2025, following the PKK’s 12th Congress.




Martyr Fîraz Dağ to be commemorated




Journalist and filmmaker Fîraz Dağ (Mehmet Aksoy) will also be commemorated on the ninth anniversary of his death.

author: Unknown
title: KJAR: Whereabouts of Zehra Pirdehqan and Parvin Raseq Qezelbash unknown for months
content:
The Community of Free Women of Eastern Kurdistan (KJAR) holds the Islamic Republic of Iran responsible for the fate of two of its members, from whom there has been no sign of life for nearly three months. Zehra Pirdehqan (Dicle Makû) and Parvin Raseq Qezelbash (Adar Makû) were in Urmia carrying out civil society work and organizing women when they disappeared within days of each other in early July.




Zehra Pirdehqan is 32 years old and comes from Qere Êynî (Chaldiran), while Parvin Raseq Qezelbash, also 32, is from Maku. According to KJAR, the organization’s inquiries found that both women had been detained by Iranian regime forces and taken to an unknown location.




No news for nearly three months




“For nearly three months, we have received no information whatsoever about the fate or condition of our two comrades,” KJAR said on Saturday. The security authorities have refused to provide the families with any clear information about where the two women are being held or their current condition.




According to KJAR, the families are also being subjected to pressure aimed at preventing them from pursuing legal and civil society channels to determine the women’s whereabouts. This has further heightened concerns for their safety.

author: Unknown
title: Mother seeks answers for 29 years
content:
Almost every household in Kurdistan carries memories shaped by the loss of loved ones, massacres, detentions and arrests. Some witnessed the killing of a loved one, some the disappearance of a sibling, some the arrest and torture of their mother, and others the death of their child. Even as the years pass, these stories are remembered anew every day in the lives of those left behind.




At a time when peace is once again on the agenda, the people of Kurdistan are demanding that the pain of the past be confronted and that similar losses never happen again. Yet for thousands of families, the past still means a search that has never reached a conclusion.




One of these families is that of Dilber Eren, a relative of the disappeared who has been trying for 29 years to learn the fate of her son and daughter-in-law. Dilber Eren has been searching for traces of her relatives ever since her son Orhan Eren and daughter-in-law Zozan Eren disappeared and were never heard from again.




Dilber Eren’s search is not limited to her struggle to learn the fate of her missing loved ones. For 29 years, she has held on to the hope that her son might one day return, repeatedly going to his home to check whether he has come back.




Her story is also part of the pain experienced by thousands of families in Kurdistan who have spent years seeking truth and justice for their missing loved ones.

author: Unknown
title: Others tried to decide her life, but Beyan Ferec chose her own path
content:
1 January 2000 marked a turning point in Beyan Ferec’s life. That day, her husband, Bekir Abdülkerim Abdullah, left home to go to his shop in Halabja. Beyan recalled that before leaving, Bekir mentioned an elderly and impoverished man whose television had broken down. He said he would give the man a new television because he did not want him to enter the new year without one.




Around ten minutes later, the sound of an explosion from the shop changed Beyan Ferec’s life. Beyan recalled going to the shop with her mother-in-law and others who were at home, only to find the building completely destroyed. According to her account, an explosive device planted inside a television in the shop detonated, and Bekir was martyred at the scene. Beyan had only recently turned 27.




Forced into marriage at 16




Beyan was born in 1974 in the Necîbek neighbourhood of Sulaymaniyah. She said her family had been kept under surveillance because of their political activities during the Baath regime, preventing her from continuing her education as a child.




Beyan attended school until the sixth grade and said her father had forced her to marry at the age of 16. She married her cousin Bekir in 1990, and they had four children, two daughters and two sons.




The family lived for a time in Darbandikhan. Beyan said they later returned to Sulaymaniyah because of war and displacement along the Sh

author: Unknown
title: Psychologists: Tests not in mother tongue label children
content:
The second session of the congress organised by the Mesopotamia Psychologists Association (DER-MEZ) in Amed (Diyarbakır) under the slogan “Human psychology should be understood through language and identity” focused on “Testing and therapy in psychological practice” and “The role of the mother tongue in the construction and denial of identity”.




As reported by Mezopotamya Agency (MA), psychologist Emel Izgi Demir said psychometric tests took shape in response to the needs of the Industrial Revolution and the capitalist system in the 19th century. She said these tools were fundamentally designed to control, classify and filter populations and fit people into predetermined categories. Demir also pointed to the historical influence of eugenic approaches on psychological testing. Demir said, “Although efforts are now being made to develop these tests into more dynamic tools that focus on the process, the underlying risk of categorisation and labelling remains.”




‘How is children’s intelligence measured?’




Demir said Kurdish therapists faced serious difficulties in clinical practice and that children’s intelligence and developmental levels were assessed using imposed measurement tools that disregarded their mother tongue. She said strict standardisation was required in training on how to administer the tests: “Practitioners are expected not to change even a single sentence

author: Unknown
title: HPG announces the death of German internationalist Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte
content:
The People’s Defence Forces (HPG) announced the death of guerrilla fighter Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte. The internationalist, who was known within the Kurdish freedom movement as Baran Nûjiyan Salîma, was born in Germany to a German mother and a Portuguese father. According to the HPG, he joined the guerrilla ranks in 2019 and was active in areas including Gare, Metîna and Qandil. He lost his life in Qandil on August 6, 2025.




The ID information of the fallen internationalist guerrilla fighter is as follows:



















Nom de Guerre: Baran Nûjiyan Salîma




First-Last Name: Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte




Birthplace: Germany




Mother's-Father's Name: Angela – Romeu




Date and Place of Death: 6 August 2025 – Qandil

















The obituary published by the HPG Press Centre reads as follows:




“Our comrade Baran Nûjiyan was born in Germany into an internationalist family, to a Portuguese father and a German mother. Although he grew up in a family environment where different cultures came together, from a very young age he began to fundamentally question the structure of capitalist modernity, which turns human beings into objects, strips them of their spirit and alienates them from their own essence.




With great seriousness, our comrade devoted himself to his education and successfully completed his university studies. Afterwards, he worked in various

author: Unknown
title: Serêkaniyê Forcibly Displaced Persons Committee calls for safe return
content:
The Serêkaniyê Forcibly Displaced Persons Committee called for the continued return of forcibly displaced people and for the return process to be placed on a safe, orderly, and legal footing.




In a written statement on Friday, the committee said that the return of forcibly displaced people to their land and homes is a legitimate right and called for this right to be guaranteed.




The statement noted that the people of Serêkaniyê have been living in displacement camps for years and facing humanitarian, social, and economic hardships, stressing that the return process must continue. It pointed out that measures beginning with the closure of schools in the Serêkaniyê camp have deprived thousands of students living in the camp of access to education.




The committee called on the official, security, and administrative authorities in Damascus, as well as the Hesekê Governorate and the administration of the Serêkaniyê region, to take action.




Calling for the safe and orderly continuation of return convoys, the committee said that the list for the next group of returnees should be prepared in order to clarify the process and prevent delays.




The statement called for obstacles to safe return to be identified and urgently removed, and for concrete measures to be taken to protect the lives and property of those returning.

author: Unknown
title: Rıza Altun commemorated in Dersim
content:
Kurdish revolutionary Rıza Altun, who died on September 25, 2019, was commemorated in Dersim (Turkish: Tunceli). The commemoration, held at the premises of the DEM Party, was organized by the Platform of Democratic Institutions.




The event began with the lighting of a candle and a minute of silence. This was followed by a film about Altun’s life and political struggle.







“Commemoration means carrying forward their ideals”




Solcan Gedik, who was released last March after 32 years of political imprisonment, recalled Altun’s decades-long involvement in the Kurdish Freedom Movement. She said that through this resistance, the Kurdish people had become known around the world, and that Rıza Altun was among those who had made great efforts and sacrifices toward this end.




“To commemorate those who have fallen means to understand them and their struggle. It means loving what they loved and striving to carry forward the ideals they left unfinished,” Gedik said. For her, commemoration therefore does not mean mourning: “We do not mourn. Our aim is to bring their philosophy to life and make their dreams a reality. Only if we can represent them can we truly commemorate them.”

author: Unknown
title: Two more Kurds arrested in Iran
content:
Iranian forces have arrested two Kurdish citizens, Shahin Mostafazadeh and 18-year-old Pezhman Amani, in Mahabad and Saqqez in recent days, taking them to undisclosed locations.




According to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), Shahin Mostafazadeh was arrested on a street in his home city of Mahabad, on 23 September. Security forces then raided and searched his family home.




Pezhman Amani was arrested on the same day at his family home in Saqqez, Kurdistan Province, where agents confiscated personal belongings, including mobile phones belonging to family members.




Both arrests were carried out without warrants, and neither detainee has since been allowed access to a lawyer or visits from family members.




Any charges against them and their whereabouts remain unknown.

author: Unknown
title: Barınç: Martyr Dîlan’s heart belonged to her struggle and her land
content:
The Coordination of the Kurdistan Women’s Liberation Party (PAJK) announced recently that Dîlan Şirnex (Rabia Barınç) joined the caravan of martyrs on 17 September 2026 after suffering from cancer.




Her brother Selim and her friends Rahime Arzu and Leyla Arzu İlhan spoke to ANF about martyr Dîlan’s life, her struggle and her devotion to her people and her land.




Selim Barınç said they grew up in a patriotic family from Şırnak (Şirnex) and described his sister, martyr Dîlan, in the following words: “We were four brothers and four sisters, and comrade Dîlan was the eldest of us. She truly was a very determined person, from her childhood until her martyrdom. Once she said something, no one could make her change her mind. Comrade Dîlan had tremendous willpower and conviction. She loved her land, she loved Abdullah Öcalan, and she loved her struggle. I believe that we and her comrades will certainly carry her goals through to success.




Comrade Dîlan was the eldest of us. I used to say that if we ever lost our mother and father, comrade Dîlan would be both a mother and a father to us. But comrade Dîlan attained martyrdom.




Wherever comrade Dîlan went, she always left a mark with her natural manner, simplicity, humility and sense of humour. She was also very compassionate. She was a strong-willed and loving person. As long as we are alive, comrade Dîlan will continue to li

author: Unknown
title: Iraq's Najaf Airport suspends flights to Iran
content:
The management of Najaf International Airport announced in a statement that all flights to Iran have been suspended in accordance with official directives.




According to the statement, all flights between Iran and Najaf International Airport are suspended indefinitely as of 2:00 p.m. today, based on official instructions.




The airport management informed all airlines and relevant parties of the decision to halt flights and requested compliance with the directives.




Iran’s leading airlines were forced to cancel their international flights on Wednesday after Washington announced that it would make no concessions to companies supporting them.




If they fail to comply with the U.S. sanctions, those companies will also face the risk of being blacklisted and consequently excluded from the dollar-denominated financial system.




The same happened on September 8 to companies in Turkey, Malaysia, the United Arab Emirates, and Kazakhstan that had cooperated with Mahan Air.




U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday, “We are putting the Iranians under unprecedented pressure.”




According to Bessent, “More than 80 to 90 percent of international flights departing from Iran have been suspended.”

author: Unknown
title: Tons of felled trees transported out of Besta by trucks
content:
New footage has emerged of the logging that has been continuing for years in the Besta region in the countryside of Şırnak province. The footage published by the Mezopotamya Agency shows trees reportedly cut down in February and left in the area to dry being loaded onto trucks and transported out of the region.




The footage shows how the trees are loaded by village guards brought from Hosyan village in Şırnak’s Pervari district and transported through military checkpoints. The trucks, which are covered with tarpaulins, reportedly have Ankara license plates beginning with 06, while tons of additional timber are said to remain in the area awaiting transport.




Logging has continued for nearly seven years in central Şırnak and its districts, as well as in the Cudi and Gabar mountains and the Besta region, causing serious ecological destruction in the area.




There is no definitive information about where the felled trees are being taken. According to local sources, some of the timber is being transported to surrounding cities for use as fuel in bread ovens or taken to other areas to be used as firewood during the winter.

author: Unknown
title: SÜDEF President Türker: We support the peace process
content:
Evgil Türker, President of the Federation of Syriac Associations (SÜDEF), spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




Türker said the process, which gained momentum with the Call for Peace and Democratic Society, offers hope for minorities and particularly for Syriacs. He said the vast majority of Syriacs were forced to migrate because of intense conflict, unresolved killings and various state policies targeting those it did not consider its own, recalling that the more peaceful environment created during previous processes enabled Syriacs to return to Turkey.




Türker said, “Sayfo has now become an identity for Syriacs,” and stressing that although the Syriac community withdrew into itself because of the traumas it experienced and has largely remained distant from politics, it is following the process and has serious expectations.




What does this process, which aims to move the historical Kurdish-Turkish relationship from a ground of war and conflict to one of democratic society and peace, mean for other minorities in the country?




The process of moving away from war and conflict towards democratic society and peace means many things for minorities, particularly Syriacs. As is well known, Syriacs were forced to migrate because of the conflict in the region in the mid-1980s and particularly in the early 1990s.

title: Kaya family gets their daughter’s remains after 27 years
content:
The identities of Süheyla Kaya and Zehra Kısaoğlu, whose remains were among those exhumed from Garzan Cemetery in the countryside of Tatvan, Bitlis, in 2017 and taken to Kilyos Cemetery in Istanbul, were established through DNA testing.




Following years of applications and DNA procedures, the families of Süheyla Kaya and Zehra Kısaoğlu confirmed the identities of their daughters through a DNA match conducted at the Council of Forensic Medicine on September 21. The families took the remains they received from Kilyos Cemetery back to their hometowns.




Süheyla Kaya was buried in Karlıova, while Zehra Kısaoğlu was buried in Bingöl in ceremonies held for each. Following the burials, condolence gatherings were held in the villages of Kargapazarı and Çira Cor, where the families live.




27 years looking for their daughter's remains




Süheyla Kaya’s mother, Fakite Kaya, described the years-long struggle to find her daughter’s remains. Speaking to Mezopotamya Agency (MA), Fakite Kaya said that after learning of allegations concerning a mass grave in Garzan, they applied to the relevant authorities and provided DNA samples. She said they were informed years later that her daughter’s remains had been found.




“Our hearts are deeply broken, and all those mothers’ hearts are broken too. Having to go through so much hardship just to find even the bones of a child is extremely pai

author: Unknown
title: Conference in London will address Kurdish question and peace processes
content:
London will host a conference focusing on a democratic and political solution to the Kurdish question and international peace processes.




Organized by the Centre for Kurdish Affairs at Hamilton House on September 29–30, the “Peace and Democratic Integration Conference” will bring together Kurdish politicians, academics, journalists, civil society representatives, and experts who have been involved in peace processes in different countries.




Former British Foreign Secretary and Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy, along with Labour MPs Catherine West and Bambos Charalambous, have expressed their support for the aims of the conference, which the organizers said are: "To establish London as a strategic forum for inclusive and informed dialogue on peace, democratic transition, and the Kurdish question; to draw on the United Kingdom’s experience of managing political conflict, competing national claims, and constitutional change through democratic consent, negotiation, devolution, and power-sharing; To ensure that political, regional, cultural, and gender diversity is meaningfully represented throughout the process; To translate comparative learning into credible, practical, and forward-looking policy options.




Peace experiences from around the world to be discussed

author: Unknown
title: He walked, and a people followed in his footsteps
content:
It all began in Tuzluçayır, a shantytown in Ankara. It was a stronghold of leftist organizations. In those years, the police could not enter the neighborhood. It was therefore known as “Little Moscow.”




After Comrade Rıza met Kemal Pir, the Apoists began coming and going. The Altun family’s house was no longer large enough to accommodate everyone who came. The Apoists demolished the house with their own hands and rebuilt it as a larger home. Before long, this house became the Apoists’ headquarters in Ankara. Who didn’t pass through its doors? From Abdullah Öcalan to Kemal Pir, from Sakine Cansız to Ali Haydar Kaytan, it was a regular gathering place for all the cadres of the early period. It served as a center for education and accommodation.




As Tuzluçayır became the headquarters of the Apoists, the neighborhood’s young people also began joining them, following Comrade Rıza and the first group. With the participation of Tuzluçayır’s youth, followed by the support of their families, the Apoist group grew considerably. Comrade Rıza would later joke about those days:




“We didn’t join the Apoists; the Apoists joined us. Our group was much bigger than theirs.”




Indeed, a march was held in Ankara in the mid-1970s. For the first time, the Apoists took part in a demonstration under their own banners. Comrade Rıza and his friends gathered everyone they could from the neighb

author: Unknown
title: Deviren: Living together with differences lays the ground for social peace
content:
Debates surrounding the Democratic Society and Peace Process are bringing changes and transformations within society on the agenda alongside political developments. The weakening of a culture of solidarity, individualization, the problems facing young people and concerns about the future are among the key issues shaping social life. Writer Mehmed Deviren spoke to ANF about the impact of these transformations on how people live together and on social values.




Social bonds are weakening




Deviren said that the changes society has undergone in recent years cannot be adequately explained solely by shifts in economic or political conditions, adding that the way people relate to one another, to society and to the future has also changed.




Deviren said: “In the past, relationships built around family, neighbourhood, neighbours, common struggle and solidarity had a more prominent place at the heart of social life. Today, however, people can grow distant from one another even while living in the same city, on the same street or even in the same house. There is also a weakening of people’s willingness to solve common problems together. Faced with unemployment, difficulties making ends meet, education, housing and uncertainty about the future, people often focus on how to secure their own lives before seeking a common solution.”

title: CDK-F: We gather to keep the legacy of Rıza Altun and martyrs alive
content:
The Democratic Kurdish Council in France (CDK-F) called on the Kurdish people, their friends and representatives of institutions to attend a commemoration in the Île-de-France region today, 25 September, to mark the anniversary of the martyrdom of Rıza Altun, one of the founding cadres of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). The event will also commemorate the martyrs of Kurdistan’s freedom struggle whose martyrdoms have recently been announced.




CDK-F continued its statement as follows: 




“This gathering is being held to keep alive the memory of those who dedicated their lives to the Kurdish people’s freedom struggle, to remember the legacy of struggle they left behind and to preserve them in our collective memory. The commemoration will also be an important gathering where our people can share their common pain, memory and sense of solidarity.




The Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom throughout history has reached the present day through great sacrifices and at a heavy cost. Keeping alive the memory of those who were martyred in this struggle, not forgetting our past and passing on our respect for their lives to future generations is a shared responsibility for all of us.




Our responsibility today is to commemorate the martyrs not only on particular anniversaries, but by remembering the values they defended, their struggle and the historical legacy they left behi

author: Unknown
title: No news from Ilham Alizadeh 18 days after arrest by Iran
content:
IranWire, an Iran-based news outlet, reported that forces from the Mahabad Intelligence Department detained Ilham (Suheyla) Alizadeh at her mother’s home and transferred her to the Urmia Intelligence Department the same day.




Her family and relatives have reportedly spent the past two weeks contacting judicial and intelligence authorities in Mahabad and Urmia in an effort to obtain information, but have received no answers about the reason for Alizadeh’s detention, any possible charges against her or the status of her case.




The family reportedly waited outside the Urmia Intelligence Department for three days and three nights, but authorities provided no information about Alizadeh’s situation.




No charges against Alizadeh have been announced, and it is also unknown whether she has been allowed access to a lawyer, to make a phone call or to communicate with her family.

title: KCK commemorates Rıza Altun and the victims of the Diyarbakır Prison massacre
content:
The Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) commemorated Rıza Altun and his comrades, who lost their lives in an airstrike in 2019, as well as ten political prisoners who were killed in the E-Type Prison in Diyarbakır (Amed) on September 24, 1996, on the anniversaries of their deaths.




In a statement, the Co-Presidency of the KCK Executive Council paid tribute to Altun’s role within the Kurdish freedom movement and recalled his political journey from Ankara and North Kurdistan, through Turkey’s prisons, to the movement’s diplomatic work.




The KCK statement on Thursday reads as follows:




“On September 24, 1996, ten of our comrades were brutally killed with nail-studded wooden planks in the E-Type Prison in Diyarbakır. On September 25, 2019, our comrade Rıza Altun, one of the leading cadres of our party, was killed together with our comrades Baz and Garzan in an airstrike. On the anniversaries of their deaths, we commemorate our comrades with respect, love, and gratitude, and renew our promise to fulfill their aspirations.




Our comrade Rıza Altun joined our group together with numerous friends from the Tuzluçayır neighborhood when the Apoist movement first began among university students in Ankara. They significantly strengthened our group. Rıza Altun was among the leading revolutionaries of the period when Tuzluçayır was known as ‘Little Moscow.’ At the time, the neighborh

author: Unknown
title: Varto Municipality’s participatory budgeting initiative ranks second in international vote
content:
The Participatory Budgeting initiative implemented by the Municipality of Varto, a district of Muş province, ranked second in an international evaluation aimed at strengthening local democracy.




188 municipalities applied for the OIDP 25th Anniversary Award




According to a statement issued by the DEM Party Press Office, 188 municipalities applied for the International Observatory on Participatory Democracy (OIDP) 25th Anniversary Award, which evaluates the work of local governments around the world in the field of participatory democracy. Following the evaluation process, 40 initiatives reached the final.




Varto Municipality’s Participatory Budgeting initiative was among the finalists and ranked second in the public vote.




According to the municipality’s statement, all seven neighborhoods in Varto were reached as part of the Participatory Budgeting initiative.




During meetings and participatory processes held in the neighborhoods, residents directly identified their needs and priorities. The aim was for a portion of the municipal budget to be allocated in line with the priorities identified by the public.




The municipality stated that the initiative aims to increase residents’ direct participation in local government decision-making.






















Varto experience presented in Kraków




Varto Municipality Co-Mayors Gülbahar Kaya and Gıyasettin Aydemir

title: Protests in Qamişlo and Girkê Legê for mother-tongue education
content:
In Qamişlo and Girkê Legê, students, parents, and teachers have once again protested against restrictions on mother-tongue education. They are calling for the planned limitation of Kurdish-language instruction to three hours per week to be withdrawn and for the right of Kurdish children to continue their schooling in their mother tongue to be guaranteed.




In Qamişlo, educators and students came together for a joint protest. In a statement read by teacher Leyla Qewas, they called for the relevant regulations issued by the Syrian Ministry of Education to be amended. “Kurdish is not merely a school subject, but an inseparable part of the identity and culture of the Kurdish people,” the statement said. Participants concluded the protest with the slogans “Bê ziman jiyan nabe” (No Life Without language] and “Zimanê me nasnameya me ye” (Our language is our identity.)




Protest tent outside school in Rimêlan




The protests are also continuing in Girkê Legê. In Rimêlan, students and their families have set up a protest tent outside the Şehîd Axîn School, reaffirming their demand to continue receiving education in Kurdish. In a statement read by teacher Rozîna Osman at the end of the protest, the Syrian Ministry of Education was called upon to continue Kurdish-language education and respect the Kurdish population’s right to education in their mother tongue.

content:
Abdullah Öcalan defines the current period as a period of “strategic struggle.” The fundamental political orientation of this period of strategic struggle is to free the Kurds entirely from the grip of genocide and to completely break that grip. In this respect, the more the Kurds proceed from the reality that they are confronted with a system of destruction, the more they can develop policies appropriate to the period of strategic struggle.




The reality of the genocidal grip demonstrates that being a Free Kurd is not easy. Yet it is also a fact that it is not impossible. The initiative developed by Öcalan has created an opportunity for the Kurds to completely break the grip of genocide and secure a free existence. In fact, this opportunity is not new. Over the half-century-long process of building the Free Kurd, such opportunities have emerged, on average, once every ten years. However, we were unable to make use of them.




Every initiative developed by Öcalan with its strategic and critical character has presented a major opportunity. Yet every opportunity also carries risks. Indeed, every initiative has been undertaken by accepting those risks. Doing nothing and continuing the familiar routine entails no risk, but neither does it create opportunity. Routine is risk-free, but it creates no opportunities either.

title: Kurdish child’s forced confession raises fears of possible death sentence
content:
Media outlets affiliated with the security agencies of the Islamic Republic of Iran have published a video of forced confessions by Arjin Jındi, a 16-year-old Kurdish child detained over the killing of an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) member, raising concerns that IRGC Intelligence is building a fabricated case against him to pave the way for a death sentence.




The video, released on 23 September, concerns the killing of IRGC member Eslam Kak-Darvishi.




Jondi remains denied access to a lawyer and family visits, 12 days after his arrest.




An informed source in Piranshahr told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) that, in recent days, a convoy of IRGC forces accompanied by several judicial officials from Piranshahr had taken Jondi to the village of Kuper and forced him to re-enact the killing as part of a staged reconstruction orchestrated by the security forces.




The source said Jondi’s hands were covered with cloth when he was taken to the reconstruction. It is unclear whether this was intended to conceal signs of torture or was done for another reason.




The forced reconstruction and publication of his confessions, while he remains denied access to a lawyer and family visits, have heightened concerns about his condition and efforts to prepare the ground for a death sentence.

title: Kurdish language and culture institutions: Mother-tongue education is a fundamental human right
content:
Kurdish language and culture institutions in Europe have spoken out against restrictions on mother-tongue education in Rojava. In a joint statement, they called for the right to education in Kurdish to be constitutionally guaranteed and for Kurdish to be granted equal status with Arabic in Syria.




The institutions issued the statement in response to the debate over the future of the Kurdish-language education system in Rojava. They said that restricting Kurdish to individual classes or treating it as a foreign language was unacceptable. The signatories described the population’s protests against such efforts by the transitional government in Damascus as a legitimate and democratic struggle for a fundamental right.




“No political or ideological preference”




“Mother-tongue education is not a political or ideological preference, but a fundamental human right. Every child has the right to be educated in their own language and to freely develop their language, culture, and identity,” the statement said. The institutions recalled that for decades, Kurds in Syria were systematically prevented from freely using their language in education as well as in institutional and public life. They said that the policies associated with this had not only restricted the right of subsequent generations to mother-tongue education, but had also hindered the free development and preservation

author: Unknown
title: Greater unity, stronger struggle
content:
In its statement of 21 September, the Asrın Law Office said that circles profiting from war and opposing the Peace and Democratic Society Process have intensified their attacks on the Kurdish Freedom Movement, particularly Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan, and through them on the Kurdish people. These attacks have even reached the level of insults.




Such attacks are coming not only from fascist-nationalist circles hostile to the Kurds, but also from social-nationalist circles that call themselves leftist. In unison, they oppose the Peace and Democratic Society Process by claiming that it “will not succeed.” In other words, they want a return to the period before the Call for Peace and Democratic Society of 27 February 2025. They oppose peace and want war. If we call them “war profiteers and bloodsuckers,” that is already what they have knowingly and willingly been doing for decades. title: ERC and EH Bildu call for support to the peace process in Turkey
content:
Esquerra Republicana re-submitted to the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Congress in Madrid a non-legislative proposal in support of the Kurds in Turkey and the peace process initiated there. 




The proposal was originally submitted last year, but, as it was not discussed, ER presented it again. Francesc-Marc Alvaro said that “the proposal did not prosper due to the opposing vote from the PP and PSOE, who do not want to upset Erdoğan.”




Jon Iñarritu, deputy from EH Bildu, said: “First of all, we would like to thank the Republican Group for bringing forward this motion. Until now, particularly over the past few decades, we have spoken about the Kurds as the largest stateless nation in the world, in terms of the repression and denial they face in all the states where they live, whether in Iran, Iraq, Syria, and especially Turkey.”




Iñarritu added: “Where the Kurdish population is largest, there is now a sense of hope. There is hope because a peace process has been opened and, as Mr. Mark Álvaro rightly pointed out, last August the Turkish Grand National Assembly approved the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration. This is a step toward strengthening the peace process and seeking a political solution to the conflict in Turkey.

author: Unknown
title: Kılıç: Mother-tongue education is a fundamental right
content:
Civil society organisations and political groups continue their efforts to secure recognition of Kurdish and other languages as languages of instruction, establish the right to mother-tongue education at every level from preschool to university, and place that right under legal protection. Advocates say mother tongues should not be confined to elective courses and are calling for a multilingual education model and official status for different languages.




Serhat Kılıç, Co-Chair of the Education and Science Workers’ Union (Eğitim Sen) Amed (Diyarbakır) Branch No. 2, spoke to ANF about the demand for mother-tongue education.







 







Children should begin education in the language through which they understand life




Kılıç stressed the importance of children beginning their education in a language that reflects their own lived experiences. He said: “The demand for mother-tongue education means that a child should begin their education in the language through which they first understand and experience life. Only then can education achieve its intended goals. Children who encounter an education system in a language other than their mother tongue begin life at a disadvantage in many respects. Without mother-tongue education, we can see disadvantages in achieving expected learning outcomes, developing self-confidence, fulfilling their potential and many other areas.”
