title: FEDA and DAKB to hold memorial for Rıza Altun in Paris
content:
In a written statement, the Democratic Alevi Federation (FEDA) and the Democratic Alevi Women’s Union (DAKB) commemorated all martyrs “with respect and gratitude” in the person of Rıza Altun, one of the founding leaders of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), who fell as a martyr on 25 September 2019.




The statement said: “To commemorate Rıza Altun, one of the noble representatives of those who, in their pursuit of rights and truth, said, ‘I would sacrifice my life for this path; let my body bear witness to it,’ means keeping alive his struggle, the memory of resistance and the invaluable legacy he left behind.”




The two Alevi organisations added: “As we keep Rıza Altun’s memory alive, we also strengthen our hope for peace, freedom and a democratic future. We believe that lasting peace can only be achieved by confronting the truth and by peoples building a life of equality and freedom.”




The statement announced that a commemoration would be held in Paris on 25 September “to commemorate Rıza Altun and be a voice for peace, freedom and truth”.




The details of the commemoration are as follows:




Venue: Espace Venise – Sarcelles, Paris




Time: 18:00




Address: 30 Route de Groslay, 95200 Sarcelles




The statement concluded: “We invite all our people, friends and comrades to join this meaningful commemoration.”

author: Unknown
title: Trees cut down in Amediye are being transported to Turkey
content:
It was reported that trees were cut down over a large area in the village of Kêste, in the Berwara Bala area of Amediye district in Duhok province, and transported to Turkey on trucks and lorries under the supervision of the Turkish army.




The footage obtained by Rojnews of the tree-cutting shows once again the extent of the destruction taking place in the region’s natural areas.




Environmental activists and advocates stated that the situation cannot be regarded simply as deforestation, noting that irreversible damage is being inflicted on the region’s natural resources.




It was also reported that local residents have been unable to return to their homes, villages, and gardens because of the situation.




It was stated that the Turkish state’s military activities in Başûrê Kurdistan (Iraqi Kurdistan) are continuing at a time when the Peace and Democratic Society process, which aims to find a democratic and peaceful solution to the Kurdish issue, is ongoing.

author: Unknown
title: Kavak: Nature and living spaces destroyed in the name of energy
content:
Kurdistan is facing ecological destruction caused by mining operations and Geothermal Power Plant (GPP) and Hydroelectric Power Plant (HPP) projects. Through licences granted in the name of energy and mining investments, mountains, forests, water resources and agricultural land are being opened up for use by companies, while natural habitats are steadily shrinking.




In areas where mining, GPP and HPP projects have fragmented living spaces, the livelihoods of people who depend on agriculture and livestock farming are also under threat. Projects that continue despite objections from local communities have prompted criticism that natural resources are being opened up to capital investment.




Nevroz Kavak, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Chamber of Environmental Engineers, spoke to ANF about the ecological destruction in the region and the impact of energy and mining projects.




Environmental destruction has reached an alarming level




Nevroz Kavak stated that environmental destruction across the region has increased to an alarming level in recent times. Kavak said: “Frankly, environmental destruction has been steadily increasing across a large part of the region recently. When we began discussing these issues, as people who approach them not only from an ecological perspective but also from a technical and scientific standpoint, we were able to look at the

author: Unknown
title: Release of Irfan Yılmaz, 96 percent disabled, blocked over ‘slogan’
content:
Irfan Yılmaz, who has cerebral palsy and is 96 percent disabled, continues to be arbitrarily denied a suspension of his sentence by the Administrative and Observation Board of Marmara No. 2 Prison, even though the 11th Specialization Board of the Council of Forensic Medicine issued a report stating that he “cannot remain in prison.” Yılmaz, who cannot meet his basic needs on his own and uses a wheelchair, was previously denied a suspension of his sentence by the board on the grounds that he had “refused to move to an independent ward.” It has now emerged that the board has once again blocked his request, this time on the grounds that he had “chanted a slogan.” Hasan Toğan, Yılmaz’s legal guardian, spoke to ANF and reacted to the decision, saying: “No matter how you look at it, this is a violation. What is being applied to Irfan is not merely hostile law, but a law of revenge.”




Even the chairs there are unsuitable for Irfan, let alone the prison




Hasan Toğan, Yılmaz’s legal guardian, visited him on Tuesday, 15 September, and said Yılmaz’s health had deteriorated further because of the poor and difficult conditions in prison. Toğan said the prison’s architecture is not suitable for wheelchair access and that guards have to carry Yılmaz to every visit. author: Unknown
title: Basque autonomy developed despite obstacles, an interview with MEP Pernando Barrena
content:
Compared with other regions, the Basque Country is the Spanish state’s most politically active autonomous region when it comes to what is sometimes described as a policy of “unnamed federalism.” In response to the systematic repression and exclusion imposed by dictator Francisco Franco Spain, including measures ranging from the banning of the Basque language to other forms of persecution, the Basque people resorted not only to armed struggle but also to numerous forms of political struggle. In the past, they were prevented from engaging in politics, their politicians were arrested, their candidacies were restricted, and their parties were shut down.




One of the figures who has been a witness, defendant, and victim of this process and its developments is Pernando Barrena, who serves as a Member of the European Parliament with The Left group on behalf of EH Bildu, the Basque Country’s left-wing pro-independence coalition. After beginning his political career as a municipal councilor at the age of 19, Barrena went on to serve as a regional parliamentarian and party spokesperson. His candidacy was blocked twice, he was arrested three times, and official records document that he was tortured. All of these experiences further strengthened Barrena’s struggle for the rights of the Basque people.




Barrena spoke to Devris Çimen of 

Yeni Özgür Politika

title: UN experts demand end to killings of kolbars
content:
Four independent UN experts urged the authorities of the Islamic Republic of Iran to end the unlawful use of lethal force against Kurdish kolbars and Baloch sukhtbars (fuel carriers), calling for independent investigations into every death caused by security forces.




In a statement issued today, 23 September, they highlighted reports of killings at close range and without warning, including of kolbars carrying no goods.




The statement, published by the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) said: "Iranian authorities must end the use of lethal force against Kurdish border couriers and Baloch fuel carriers, UN experts* said today, calling the measures unlawful and calling for independent investigations into every death caused by security forces.




The Kurdish border couriers known as kolbars and Baloch fuel carriers known as sukhtbars, are among the most economically marginalised people in Iran, carrying goods and fuel across border areas with few other means of supporting their families,” the experts said. “They must not pay for that poverty with their lives."




The statement underlined that "at least 12 kolbars have reportedly been shot dead by Iran’s border forces or Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps since the start of 2026. In the last two months, the experts received reports of seven kolbars killed by direct gunfire from Iranian border guards,

author: Unknown
title: Freedom for Öcalan Vigil enters Its 743rd week
content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, which was launched on 25 June 2012, in Strasbourg, has entered its 743rd week.




The vigil, which continues in Strasbourg, where institutions such as the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights are located, was taken over by Seyit Manoş, Mirza Çağlayan, and Emre Can, who came from the canton of Basel in Switzerland.




We want Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom 




Speaking on behalf of the group, Seyit Manoş stated that the Kurdish people have been maintaining a vigil in front of European institutions for more than 14 years with the demand for Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom.




Manoş said they want Abdullah Öcalan to be granted physical freedom as soon as possible and for his status to be recognized.




Condolences to the families of the martyrs




Manoş conveyed, on behalf of the group, his condolences to the families of the Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas following the reported deaths.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish kolbar killed at the Iranian border
content:
A Kurdish kolbar in the Sêlas Bawcanî district of Kermanshah province died as a result of an armed attack by Iranian border forces.




Twenty-eight-year-old Mihemed Sıddîq Ewelî was shot at close range without warning in the Şêx Salih border area in the early hours of Wednesday. Ewelî, who was the father of two young children, was from the village of Encîrbus in Sêlas Bawcanî.




According to statistics compiled by Kolbarnews, 26 kolbars were killed and 31 were injured in 2025 in the border areas and intercity roads of West Azerbaijan, Kurdistan, and Kermanshah provinces. The causes included direct gunfire by regime forces, avalanches and hypothermia, landmine explosions, falls from mountains and elevated areas, and other incidents.




According to the records, of the 57 kolbars killed or injured in 2025, 44 were affected by direct gunfire from regime forces. Two of the kolbars were children under the age of 18. One of them was killed by direct gunfire from Iraqi border guards (Haras al-Hudud).




Although the number of kolbars killed and injured in 2025 decreased by 69% compared with 2024, the proportion of deaths among the total casualties increased from 28% to 46%. This change indicates a significant increase in the proportion of deaths among total casualties and reflects that violence became increasingly lethal in 2025.

author: Unknown
title: Work-related deaths: Some 8 children lose their lives every month
content:
The Health and Safety Labour Observatory (ISIG) has released its “Child Labour Deaths Report,” covering the period from September 2025 to August 2026.




According to the report, 95 children lost their lives in work-related deaths. The report added that 14 of the children who lost their lives were refugees.




The report also included the causes of the children’s deaths, noting that 18 percent were due to crushing and collapses, 17 percent to traffic accidents, and 16 percent to drowning and poisoning cases.

author: Unknown
title: Grave of HPG guerrilla Kahraman Gezici found after 21 years
content:
Kurdish families whose children lost their lives in the conflict in North Kurdistan continue searching for their graves even years later. Due to the destruction of cemeteries, the failure to return bodies to families, or the burial locations remaining unknown, some families are only able to locate the graves of their children many years later.




The family of fallen HPG guerrilla Kahraman Gezici, located his grave after recognizing it in footage of a cemetery aired on the program Motorewan, broadcast on Nûçe TV.







The Şehîd Binevş Cemetery, where HPG and YJA-Star guerrillas are buried, is located in the village of Basret, near Mount Gabar in the countryside of Şırnak province.




The cemetery was damaged in an airstrike in 2015 and remained closed to visitors for many years after the area was declared a “military security zone.” After footage of the cemetery was aired in a program on Nûçe TV, the Gezici family, who live in Van, identified the grave of their son, HPG guerrilla Kahraman Gezici (Kendal Tatvan), whom they had been searching for 21 years.







The HPG guerrilla's mother, Hayriye Gezici, and brother, Fedai Gezici, traveled from Van to Gabar region to visit Kahraman Gezici’s grave.

title: From the free press to the free mountains: Egîd Amed
content:
In the mountains




lies the life we lead,




hidden within the time we live through.




When our lives come to an end,




it will become clear




how meaningful they have been.




Thus wrote Egîd Amed in one of his poems.




The history of the Kurdish people is a history of oppression, but also of resistance and great sacrifice. Many steps were taken and many words spoken under conditions of resistance. The history of the Kurdish freedom movement has likewise been shaped by these experiences.




In Kurdistan, despite all the repression, children grew up chanting “Bijî Serok Apo” [Long Live Leader Abdullah Öcalan]. For them, “Bijî Serok Apo” was not merely a slogan heard at demonstrations. It was part of their everyday lives and the political reality in which they grew up.




Egîd Amed was one of those children. In the words of Musa Anter, he was among the “little generals of Kurdistan.” He grew up surrounded by resistance, shaped by the convictions and struggle of those who came before him.




His own path began on the streets of Amed (Diyarbakır) and later took him to Istanbul, where he worked for Özgür Halk (Free Folk) magazine, an important publication in the free press tradition. title: Pervin Buldan: More concrete and practical steps will be taken in the coming period
content:
Pervin Buldan has announced concrete developments in the Peace and Democratic Society Process in the coming days. During a visit to the Peace Mothers’ Council in Van, the DEM Party MP, who is part of her party’s Imrali Delegation, said that the process would enter a new phase.




“In the coming days, we will probably enter a phase and a process in which more concrete and practical steps are taken. There will be important developments. With these developments, peace will also become more tangible,” Buldan said. At the same time, she emphasized that further progress would require social engagement and a collective struggle.




Buldan most recently visited Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on the prison island of Imrali on September 13, together with her parliamentary group colleague Mithat Sancar and lawyer Özgür Faik Erol. Following the visit, Öcalan stated that after the adoption of the framework law, the focus should be on initiating reciprocal practical steps and ensuring that the established bodies actively carry out their work.




A large number of people attended the meeting held at the DEM Party offices in Van. Gülşen Kurt, co-chair of the party’s provincial organization, highlighted the role of women and particularly the Peace Mothers: “Women are at the forefront of this struggle; the Peace Mothers are at the forefront. Mothers have paid the highest price.”

title: Geothermal project in Varto: Site inspection scheduled for October 8
content:
In the legal proceedings against the planned geothermal project by the US company IGNIS H2 Energy in Xwarik near Varto district of Muş, a site inspection involving experts is scheduled to take place in October. The Administrative Court in Bingöl had already ordered the inspection in July. Two months later, a date has finally been set. The site inspection is scheduled to begin at 10 a.m. on October 8 in the project area. Experts will examine the project’s potential impacts on the environment and local habitats. A report will then be prepared for the court.




Residents of Xwarik and surrounding villages have been opposing the project for months and are continuing the protest camp they launched in early May. Most recently, residents from various villages in the region have taken turns participating in the protest. On April 9, they filed a lawsuit with the Bingöl Administrative Court challenging the decision not to require a comprehensive environmental impact assessment for the project. At the same time, they requested a stay of execution pending the court’s ruling.




In July, the court decided that a site inspection and an expert assessment should first be carried out. The examination will cover, among other things, the project’s potential effects on agricultural land, forests, groundwater, biodiversity, flora, and fauna. title: DEM Party Women’s Assembly: We will not give up our rights
content:
The Women’s Assembly of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) issued a written statement regarding femicides, the verdict in the Aleyna Çakır (Sema Esen) case, and operations carried out under the name “My Family Is Safe.”




The statement drew attention to the killing of 10 women over the past five days, stating that these events are a reason to strengthen women’s struggle.




Femicides are the result of policies of impunity




The statement said that femicides are the result of a male-dominated system and policies of impunity, adding, “If women are not safe in their homes, on the streets, or in their workplaces, no segment of society is safe.”




The statement said that the male-dominated judiciary, which fails to protect women’s lives, does not implement protective measures, and rewards perpetrators through policies of impunity, bears responsibility for femicides. It also stated that policies that protect not women themselves but the family within which women are killed pave the way for further killings.




The statement said that isolating women who want to escape environments of violence, failing to operate mechanisms designed to protect women, and targeting women’s struggle for freedom and equality all contribute to femicides.




Aleyna Çakır case is an indicator of the system of impunity

title: DEM Party: Preventing violence in schools is possible through building a culture of peace
content:
In a written statement, the DEM Party’s Children’s Commission and Education Policies Commission said: “We are deeply saddened by the armed attack at a high school in Turgutlu district of Manisa. We extend our wishes for a speedy recovery to the children who were injured and their families, as well as to children, parents, education workers, and society as a whole. The incident must be urgently and transparently investigated in all its dimensions, and effective judicial and administrative proceedings must be initiated against all individuals and institutions whose negligence contributed to it.




Recalling recent incidents of violence in schools in Maraş and Urfa, the commissions stated: “It is clear that the culture of violence and conflict reproduced every day in the adult world, representations of violence normalized through the mainstream media, deepening structural crises—particularly the economic crisis—sexism, and all forms of inequality permeating social life are also reflected in children’s living environments. Therefore, approaches that intervene not in the source of the problem but only in its visible consequences, producing short-term measures and security-oriented reflexes after each incident, not only fail to eliminate the violence itself but also render invisible the conditions that reproduce it.”

title: Kurdish writer Suzan Samancı detained upon entering Turkey, placed under a travel ban
content:
Kurdish writer Suzan Samancı was detained on Tuesday at Istanbul Airport while entering Turkey. The author, who has been living in Switzerland for 18 years, is under investigation on allegations of “propaganda for a terrorist organization.” Following her statement, she was released under judicial supervision and placed under a travel ban.




Her detention was made public by lawyer and human rights activist Eren Keskin. “Kurdish writer Suzan Samancı, who has been living in Switzerland for 18 years, returned to Turkey today. She was detained at Istanbul Airport on allegations of ‘propaganda for an organization,’” Keskin stated.




After her questioning was completed, Samancı was first referred to the prosecutor’s office and then brought before a judge. Via videoconference, the 64-year-old writer was connected to the competent court in Amed (Diyarbakır). The court imposed a travel ban as a judicial control measure and ordered Samancı’s release.




From Turkish-language literature to writing in Kurdish




Suzan Samancı is from Amed and has been part of the Kurdish literary scene for decades. She began her literary career with poetry before turning primarily to short stories and novels. She also wrote for newspapers including Demokrasi, Gündem, and Özgür Politika. She is a member of the writers’ association PEN.

title: Pasture bans: Rural decline and a new wave of forced migration
content:
Security-driven policies pursued for decades in Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) are gradually dismantling livestock farming, the main source of livelihood for the rural population. Restrictions on access to pastures on military grounds, the designation of grazing areas as “special security zones” and measures preventing villagers from taking their animals into the mountains and highland pastures are effectively bringing an end to a way of life that has sustained the people of Kurdistan for thousands of years. This is not accidental, but the result of a deliberate, systematic and political choice.




Small and large livestock farming, the backbone of the rural economy in Kurdistan, has come under an increasingly restrictive regime in recent years. Villagers can no longer freely take their animals to highland pastures. Even where access is permitted, they face narrow corridors imposed on security grounds, constant identity checks and arbitrary entry bans. These restrictions have gone far beyond a question of access. They amount to a deliberate severing of the ties between local people, their land and their economic autonomy.

title: Suspected death in Eskişehir prison
content:
According to information provided by Çiçek’s family, Şiyar Çiçek, who was being held in Eskişehir Prison, died under suspicious circumstances. Çiçek had been in prison since 2014, and had been held in Eskişehir Prison for approximately two years. He was allegedly kept in a cell for the past 10 days.




According to a report published by Ajansa Welat, Çiçek’s family said that his health was good and that he only had diabetes. Çiçek’s father, Menduh Çiçek, said that his son had died in prison, and added: “On Monday they called us and said ‘Your son is sick, we are taking him to the hospital.’ My son only had diabetes, he was in very good condition, but he died.”




We don't know what happened to my son




Çiçek's father said that he had seen his son’s body and found no signs of torture, but that they had suspicions about the cause of death. He added: “We think they poisoned my son or did something else to him.”




Çiçek said that his son had spoken to his mother by phone about a week before his death and told her that he had been placed in a cell. He continued: “My son had been in a cell for 10 days. If he had been in the ward, we could have found out what happened. But because he was in a cell, we don’t know what happened to him.”

title: Öztürk: Commission should not limit Öcalan’s role
content:
The Monitoring and Evaluation Board, established in line with the framework law adopted by Parliament as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, formed four subcommissions following its first meeting on 24 August. The inclusion of Abdullah Öcalan in one of these bodies, the “Disarmament and Strategic Coordination Subcommission,” has brought his role in advancing the process to the fore.




Öcalan’s involvement in the commission’s work is regarded as a critical step towards a democratic solution to the Kurdish question and the establishment of lasting peace.




Raziye Öztürk, a lawyer from the Asrın Law Office, spoke to ANF about the current stage of the process and Öcalan’s status.




Mr. Öcalan’s direct participation is valuable




Raziye Öztürk described the establishment of commissions within Parliament as an important threshold at the current stage and said the way should be opened for Mr. Öcalan to participate in the process directly and officially.




Öztürk said: “Undoubtedly, the establishment of commissions within Parliament and the institutional character this gives to the process can be regarded as an important threshold at the stage we have reached. At the same time, we consider every step that enables Mr. Öcalan to participate in the process directly and officially and to effectively fulfil his role to be valuable for advancing the process.

title: Alparslan: Ministry’s decision to separate Zazaki from Kurdish aims to create division
content:
The 2026–2027 academic year began on 14 September. One week before the start of the new school year, the Ministry of National Education (MEB) introduced a separate curriculum for Zazaki (Kirmanckî), which it had previously treated alongside Kurmancî as a dialect of Kurdish.




The new programme, prepared under the “Century of Turkey Education Model”, places Zazaki within the education system as a separate curriculum. It was also decided that Zazaki textbooks would be revised and that the field would be designated as a separate branch for teacher appointments.




As the first week of the new academic year came to an end, Istanbul Kurdish Institute Co-Chair Remziye Alparslan spoke to ANF about the impact of mother-tongue education on children’s development and the Ministry’s decision to treat Zazaki as a subject separate from Kurdish.




Alparslan said mother-tongue education is important not only for the individual development of children beginning their education, but also for preserving cultural identity. 




Alparslan said: “Education in the mother tongue is extremely important for children to begin school in the language that shapes their identity, culture and roots, without becoming alienated from themselves or disconnected from their families and roots, and with a sense of self-confidence. title: Mobilisation for the Kurdish language
content:
The demand for mother-tongue education has long been one of the central issues in discussions surrounding the Kurdish question and democratisation in Turkey. As the Peace and Democratic Society Process is being debated, the right to mother-tongue education and official status for Kurdish are seen not only as matters of education policy but also as fundamental conditions for social peace.




Heval Dilbahar, Co-Spokesperson of the Language, Culture and Arts Commission of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), said Kurdish-language education from preschool to university is possible and that, if the state demonstrates the necessary political will, existing shortcomings could be addressed within two to three years and Kurdish-language education introduced in schools.




In a report by Lütfi Pala of Mezopotamya Agency, Dilbahar said the republic was founded on a monist understanding: “A century ago, the Republic was established on a monist understanding. As a result, many languages, particularly Kurdish, were banned. The Kurdish language was subjected to severe pressure, coercion and restrictions. However, as a result of the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom, policies of denial, assimilation, prohibition and eradication were broken. In other words, it is no longer possible to deny or completely eradicate the Kurdish language through conventional methods.”

title: The red star of Istanbul: Egîd Tolhildan
content:
Throughout history, some cities have been remembered not only as geographical centres but also as symbolic places of resistance and social struggle. Stretching from Havana and Stalingrad to Chiapas and Kobanê, these cities have carved out a distinctive place in the history of peoples’ struggles.




Cities also hold a special place in the history of the Kurdish Freedom Movement in terms of resistance. Some have stood out for mass serhildans, or uprisings, while others have become known for the revolutionaries they nurtured and who took part in the struggle. Istanbul is one of the cities that embodies both.







 







Istanbul has witnessed decades of mass demonstrations and resistance throughout the history of the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Newroz uprisings, university protests, demonstrations against the international conspiracy, resistance in solidarity with Kobanê and Rojava, and actions carried out by the Patriotic Revolutionary Youth Movement (YDG-H), which was active between 2013 and 2016, marked important moments in this history.




Istanbul’s significance for the Kurdish Freedom Movement has not been limited to mass mobilisation. The city has also become associated with the many revolutionaries who joined the ranks of the movement. title: Duran Kalkan: Things need to change and transform; the Republic of Turkey needs to democratize
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, made important assessments on current affairs during a special program broadcast on Medya Haber TV.




Here are some excerpts from the interview.

It created great hope and excitement in many circles. This is what we call the “root law,” while those who drafted it define it as a framework law. In the previous program, we said that, at the very least, it had stopped the war and opened the way for politics. As you pointed out, 40 days have passed; there are no concrete steps. The only thing that has happened is that the body defined by the law as the Monitoring and Evaluation Board held a meeting. It announced that it had decided to establish four subcommittees. content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan spoke on current developments following her party’s first Central Executive Board (MYK) meeting after its 5th Ordinary Congress.




According to Doğan, the meeting addressed the party’s work for the new period, the new legislative term, the Peace and Democratic Society Process, as well as economic and social developments.






















‘We expect important developments’




Commenting on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Ayşegül Doğan said they viewed the framework law adopted by Parliament as the first step in the process.

“We expect important developments regarding disarmament in the coming days,” Ayşegül Doğan said.

Öcalan’s role

title: PJAK member remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after arrest by Iranian intelligence
content:
Sirwan Habibi, a member of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him in Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that Habibi’s family has repeatedly visited Ministry of Intelligence offices and courts in Kamyaran and Sanandaj in recent days, seeking information about his situation. However, the authorities have continued to deny any knowledge of his arrest.




Habibi, from Sanandaj, is known within PJAK by the organisational name Aram Sine. The continued lack of information about his fate, together with the absence of any judicial case registered in his name at the courts in either city, has heightened concerns about his condition and whereabouts.




KHRN has spoken to several residents of Kamyaran’s Besat neighbourhood who witnessed his arrest, obtaining further details about the circumstances.




According to witnesses, dozens of civilian vehicles with tinted windows used by the Ministry of Intelligence agents surrounded several streets in the neighbourhood on the evening of 8 September. At about 01:00 local time on 9 September, agents began pursuing Habibi as he rode a motorcycle.




Witnesses said one of the vehicles struck his motorcycle at high speed, causing it to overturn, before agents used violence to arrest him.

title: The enchanter of the Balkans
content:
At the beginning of the concert, when the lights in the hall were gently dimmed and the sound of a wind instrument rose from the back rows, everyone turned with curiosity toward the source of the sound. Some audience members stood up to see the musician. Just as they caught sight of him, another appeared from a different corner, and then another from the back. Positioned among the audience, the orchestra members began accompanying one another one by one as they walked toward the stage.




As they moved toward the stage playing trombone, trumpet, and saxophone, two women in traditional Bulgarian attire entered from behind and took their positions on the left. The younger, dark-haired man sat down behind a large bass drum. Once all nine were on stage, Goran Bregović arrived in white attire, with his signature disheveled hair. Sitting in the middle of the orchestra, he picked up his distinct electric guitar. As he took his seat, nearly the entire audience burst into applause and excitement. The few who remained seated looked bewildered and out of place, because this concert at the Kongresshaus in Zurich, Switzerland, was a gathering of former Yugoslavs and the "others."




Most of the Swiss audience members were bewildered because they had come simply to sit, listen, and leave. Yet here, the roles had reversed: the local had become the "other," while the "other" virtually turned

title: DFG pays tribute to journalist Seyit Evran
content:
The Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) issued a written statement marking the anniversary of the death of journalist Seyit Evran (Seyit Mahmut Evran).




Evran, who was 54, passed away on 22 September 2023, at a hospital in North and East Syria where he was receiving treatment. DFG said he had devoted his journalistic career to conveying to the world the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom and democracy, events in Kurdistan, and the realities of the peoples of the region.




DFG said that Evran did not view journalism merely as a profession, but as a means of making visible the realities experienced by peoples and bearing witness to history. The statement added that through the photographs he took, his reporting, and his analyses from conflict zones, he left behind an important journalistic and historical record.




The association said: “Keeping his memory alive, preserving the journalistic legacy he left behind, and continuing to defend the truth is a responsibility for us.”




Seyit Evran




Evran was born in 1969 in the Hênê (Hani) district of Amed. He witnessed the events that unfolded following the September 12 military coup. During his studies at Çukurova University, he met journalist Gurbetelli Ersöz, an encounter that became an important turning point in his journalistic career.

title: Iraq in talks with Ankara over withdrawal of Turkish troops
content:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has confirmed that talks are underway with Ankara over the withdrawal of the Turkish military from Iraq and the Kurdistan Region. “Our talks with the government in Ankara are continuing in order to reach an agreement on the withdrawal of Turkish troops from Iraqi territory,” al-Zaidi said in an interview with the New York Times.




In the interview, al-Zaidi also addressed the future of non-state armed groups in Iraq. He said their disarmament was not voluntary but mandatory. “Above all, in order to build a strong economy, weapons must be exclusively under the control of the state,” the prime minister said.




Disarmament to be completed by June 2027




Following the planned complete withdrawal of the remaining US troops on September 30, the Iraqi government intends to announce the terms of an agreement on disarmament. The process will then be implemented gradually and is expected to be completed by June 30, 2027. According to al-Zaidi, some of the groups concerned are calling for the deadline to be extended until the end of 2027.




As a first step, the plan provides for a 90-day period during which the armed groups will halt their attacks and the United States, in return, will refrain from retaliatory strikes. title: Lawyer Binbir: İGK decisions preventing releases from prison must be abolished
content:
The release of numerous political prisoners, including İzzethan Aykut, Hicran Binici, Mehmet Sait Yıldırım, Gülşen Adet, Nuriye Adet, Aydın Altığ, Mahsum Bilem, Levent Cin, Zübeyir İdem, Ömer Okul, Nidayi Tezer, Nurettin Ataman, Ahmed Abdi İbrahim and Tuncay Doğan, has been repeatedly postponed this year by the Administrative and Observation Boards.




The Administrative and Observation Boards, which have become an obstacle to the release process in prisons, are preventing the release of prisoners who have served 30 years in particular, citing various grounds. Their decisions have invoked reasons such as “not displaying good conduct,” “showing no remorse,” “failing to develop awareness of the offense,” “failing to distance oneself from organizational ideology,” and “the assessment that the individual will maintain ties with the organization.”




Lawyer Mehmet Zeki Binbir, a member of the Prison Commission of the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD), stated that the decisions issued by the Administrative and Observation Boards, which were established by legislation passed in 2020 and came into effect in 2021, are unlawful.

title: KNK welcomes the unification of KDP and PUK Peshmerga  in the Kurdistan Region
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a message welcoming the unification of the 80th Unit of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the 70th Unit of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) under the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs. The statement described the unification of the Peshmerga forces as an aspiration of the people of Kurdistan for decades and expressed hope that the move would mark the beginning of the unification of all administrative, security, economic and diplomatic institutions.




“We hope that this initiative will serve as a means of fostering unity and solidarity across Kurdistan on the basis of national and patriotic principles,” the KNK said.




The statement noted that a government has not been formed for two years following the elections held in the Kurdistan Region, describing the situation as dangerous and unacceptable and expressing hope that parliament would be formed as soon as possible.

title: Iraqi military delegation holds talks in Shengal
content:
A high-ranking Iraqi military delegation led by Chief of Staff Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah traveled to Shengal on Tuesday. The delegation is expected to meet with representatives of the Yazidi community and military forces present in the region to discuss the security situation and the restructuring of security arrangements.




According to the Iraqi Ministry of Defense, the visit is intended to assess the security situation in Shengal and review the operational readiness of the forces stationed there. Yarallah also heads the high-level security commission established by the government.




The delegation also includes members of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (Hashd al-Shaabi). According to multiple reports, meetings are planned with the military formations active in Shengal, including the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ). The talks will focus on the future security structure, the handover of weapons, and the integration of members of the units into state institutions.




The visit follows a decision by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi. Following a meeting with Yazidi organizations on September 11, he announced that the resistance units would hand over their weapons to the state. At the same time, he said that eligible members of the YBŞ and YJŞ could be integrated into Iraq’s official security institutions.

title: Bakırhan: No consensus without equal rights for Alevis
content:
DEM Party Co-Chairs Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan met with representatives of Alevi organizations in Ankara. The meeting focused on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, as well as the concerns, demands and proposals of the Alevi community.




Bakırhan said at the meeting on Tuesday that Turkey was going through a decisive period. He said the goal of the ongoing process could not be limited to ending violence and armed conflict. “This must be followed by a phase in which democracy, the rule of law and equal citizenship are realized.” The concerns of Alevis must also be taken into account, Bakırhan said. “For us, consensus can only be achieved on the basis of legal recognition, only within a legal framework in which Alevis feel that they are equal citizens.” The DEM Party, he added, will not support a process that does not ensure the equal participation of Alevis.




Peace is possible when all identities are free




Bakırhan said that genuine peace could only be achieved when Alevis were equal citizens, Cem houses (Alevi places of worship) were granted legal status, discrimination was ended, and all identities were free to exist. title: Sayyiğit: Öcalan must have conditions to work and communicate freely
content:
The Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with Abdullah Öcalan’s call on 27 February 2025, marks a new phase in efforts to achieve a democratic and peaceful solution to the Kurdish question. Providing Abdullah Öcalan, the chief negotiator in the process, with conditions in which he can work and communicate freely has emerged as one of the key issues for advancing the process towards lasting peace and a democratic society.




Gülcan Kaçmaz Sayyiğit, Co-Spokesperson of the Democratic Unity Initiative, spoke to ANF about the process.




Mr. Öcalan has launched peace initiatives many times




Sayyiğit said the Kurdish question had been left to the security bureaucracy for decades, creating a system in which the lack of a solution became entrenched. She argued that the status quo had ignored the genuine interlocutors in order to prolong its own existence.




Sayyiğit said: “Even when this mentality became open to a solution, it sought to pursue it through different actors. It tried to create interlocutors it considered acceptable in an attempt to secure the consent of the Kurdish people. Yet every attempt to manufacture artificial interlocutors failed. The state was looking for a solution in the wrong place, while Mr. Öcalan launched numerous initiatives for democratic peace from the 1990s onwards. title: Orhan: Kızıltepe JITEM case exemplifies impunity for known perpetrators
content:
Cases involving serious human rights violations, enforced disappearances and extrajudicial executions in Kurdistan during the 1990s have long been at the centre of debates over impunity. One of the latest developments to bring the issue back into focus was the detention of retired Gendarmerie Staff Colonel Hasan Atilla Uğur as part of a reopened investigation into the 2011 death of former National Intelligence Organisation (MIT) officer Kaşif Kozinoğlu in Silivri Prison.




Uğur’s name has been associated not only with the Kozinoğlu investigation but also with the Kızıltepe Gendarmerie Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism (JITEM) case, which concerned allegations of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial executions in the Kızıltepe district of Mardin during the 1990s.




Uğur was one of nine defendants in the Kızıltepe JITEM case, alongside Eşref Hatipoğlu, then Diyarbakır Provincial Gendarmerie Commander, Gendarmerie Commando Company Commander Ahmet Boncuk, Master Sergeant Ünal Alkan and village guards. The defendants were tried over allegations of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial executions in Kızıltepe during the 1990s.




The years-long trial ended in acquittals, while lawyers representing the victims and human rights organisations criticised the proceedings as an example of the policy of impunity.

title: Repression continues in Iran
content:
Forces from Iran’s Intelligence Department raided the homes of Baha’i citizens Nazanin Nikouseresht and her husband Pejman Zare, as well as Mina Zare, Mahshid Zare, Mahboubeh Zare and Parham Zare, in the Iranian city of Shiraz.




The simultaneous raids resulted in the confiscation of mobile phones, computers, books, images and materials related to the Baha’i faith, personal documents, passports, identity documents, a hard drive, gold and an amount of foreign currency.




Mina, Mahshid, Mahboubeh, Pejman and Parham Zare are reported to be siblings. Documents relating to Pejman Zare’s legal proceedings, along with a report prepared by the Forensic Medicine Organisation, were also reportedly confiscated.




Nazanin Nikouseresht, Mina, Mahshid, Mahboubeh and Parham Zare were summoned to the detention centre known as “Plaque 100”, which is affiliated with the Shiraz Intelligence Department.




Pejman Zare was detained by Shiraz Intelligence Department officers in March 2026 and informed of the charges against him following his detention. He was released on bail from Adelabad Central Prison in August 2026. Security forces reportedly also seized documents used in the legal proceedings concerning his previous detention during the latest raid.

title: Ask the Kurds
content:
We have written before about peace, arguing that silencing guns alone does not amount to peace. A conflict may end without truth, justice, memory, trust and social participation, but peace cannot take root in society. Much has already been said and written around this idea.




Today, we need to take the discussion one step further. The Kurdish question is no longer simply about ending the conflict; we are discussing a transformation that will determine the nature of the future political relationship. Regimes are being transformed, organisational structures are changing, paradigms are being redefined, and concepts such as “democratic integration”, “democratic society”, the “Democratic Republic” and the possibilities of a new form of coexistence are being discussed. None of this can be underestimated.




The establishment of a negotiating table, the possibility of ending the armed conflict and the opportunities this could create not only in Turkey but also in other parts of Kurdistan are of historic importance. We are therefore conscious of the context in which every critical word we say about the process is received. The issue is not to diminish the value of the negotiating table, but to discuss how a peace can be built that does justice to the weight of such a history.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish Women’s Platform: Kurdish must be constitutionally protected
content:
The European Kurdish Women’s National Unity Platform issued a statement on the right to mother-tongue education in Kurdish and the protection of the rights of the Kurdish people in Rojava and Syria.




The statement stressed that language is a fundamental human right and that mother-tongue education is essential to preserving identity and culture, saying: “As the European Kurdish Women’s National Unity Platform, we stress that the Kurdish people’s right to learn Kurdish and receive education in their mother tongue is a fundamental right that must be guaranteed constitutionally and legally.




We also strongly condemn all attacks against and targeting of the Kurdish people. In particular, we condemn the brutal martyrdom of Martyr Sîpan, a member of the Ministry of Defence, by members of the Baggara tribe.




We extend our condolences to his family and friends and demand an independent and transparent investigation into the incident. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable under the law, regardless of their affiliation or identity. To preserve social peace and relations among the different components of society, we also call for individual crimes not to be attributed to entire tribes or groups.”




Learning, teaching and using Kurdish must be guaranteed

author: Unknown
title: The doors of Imralı must be opened to all
content:
The issue that is currently generating the most interest in Turkey is where the Peace and Democratic Society process, which is being negotiated in Imralı, will lead. It seems as though the process has been slowed down. Some say that the pace of the process is tied to the elections. If such an important issue is being handled according to electoral calculations, this would be the greatest disservice that could be done to Turkey. No political force should approach a problem that is a century old and that will determine Turkey’s future through the calculations of an election.




Government spokespeople say that the process is proceeding as planned. But the actions on the ground do not appear to reflect this. An important party to this process is the Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. However, the fact that this leader, who is expected to play a role in advancing the process, has not been given conditions in which he can work freely raises questions about the government’s approach to the process. The rhetoric and the practice are not aligned. The Kurdish people and pro-democracy forces want this leadership to be able to operate freely. It is expected that he should be able to meet with journalists, politicians, and intellectuals and present his views openly to the public. But none of this is happening. title: Kurdish shopkeepers face arrests, shop closures over general strike in Rojhilat
content:
Iranian security agencies have summoned and arrested dozens of Kurdish shopkeepers and market traders for joining a strike across cities in Kurdistan on 16 September, marking the fourth anniversary of Jina Amini’s state killing and the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadi” (Woman, Life, Freedom) uprising.




The agencies involved include the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Ministry of Intelligence.




Authorities have also temporarily sealed businesses under judicial orders and forced some shopkeepers and traders to sign written pledges not to join future strikes.




A shopkeeper in Kamyaran told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) that, on the evening of 16 September, following a widespread strike on Toubrehriz Street, IRGC Intelligence telephoned several shopkeepers and market traders who had closed their businesses that day, summoning them to its local office.




The source said officers ordered them to report within hours or face the closure of their businesses. Several traders went to the office late that night following the threats.




Once there, officers threatened to open judicial cases against them. An elderly shopkeeper who objected was beaten and insulted in front of the others. Those summoned were then made to sign written pledges not to take part in similar strikes in future.

title: KDP and PUK Peshmerga officially placed under joint ministry
content:
The Peshmerga forces previously under the control of the KDP and PUK, two governing parties in southern Kurdistan (northern Iraq), have been brought together under the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI).




The 80th Unit of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the 70th Unit of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) have been placed under the ministry as the First and Second Regions.




Unification process underway since 2022




In 2022, the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs launched a process to unify the armed forces at the urging of the United States. However, a significant part of the Peshmerga structures remained directly under the control of the two dominant parties, the KDP and PUK. Political disputes between the two parties delayed the unification process for years. With the integration of the 70th and 80th units into the structures of the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs, this part of the reform process has now been completed.







Ceremony announces 

the completion of the reorganisation and unification




A ceremony was held on Monday, 21 September 2026, to announce the completion of the reorganisation and unification of the Peshmerga forces.

title: Hatimoğulları visits the vigil of earthquake victims’ families: Their voices must be heard
content:
DEM Party Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları visited the vigil held by families of victims of the February 6 earthquakes outside Turkey’s Ministry of Justice in Ankara. For eleven days, the families have been demanding a meeting with ministry officials and accountability for construction contractors, building inspection authorities, and state institutions.




The vigil is organized by the “Families Seeking Justice” platform. Outside the ministry, relatives commemorate those killed in the earthquakes by displaying their photographs. Signs include messages such as: “Why are those responsible for February 6 still free?” and “Those who construct unsafe buildings, remove columns, and allow this to happen must be punished.”







“Lack of oversight killed”




Hatimoğulları first spoke with the families about their experiences and demands. She then criticized the fact that the relatives had been waiting for days for a meeting with the Ministry of Justice. The scale of the suffering they have endured is almost impossible to put into words, the politician said. According to official figures, more than 53,000 people were killed, she said, although the actual number was far higher. She stressed that the disaster should not be viewed solely as the consequence of a natural event.

author: Unknown
title: 257 people abducted in Syria since the beginning of 2026
content:
The Syrian Committees for the Defense of Democratic Freedoms and Human Rights issued a written statement on August 30, the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances.




The statement said that abductions and cases of enforced detention continue to be reported across Syria. It warned that the loss of contact with detainees and the lack of information about their whereabouts pose a serious threat to their lives.




According to the committees, 257 people have been documented as forcibly abducted since the start of the year. The statement also said that Israeli forces had abducted 52 people.




The committees called on all government-affiliated and non-governmental actors responsible for abductions to disclose the whereabouts and fate of those being held and to end practices that, they said, violate fundamental rights and freedoms.




They also called on the International Committee of the Red Cross and other relevant international organizations to secure access to detention facilities, investigate cases of enforced detention, and establish the fate and whereabouts of detainees and abducted persons.

author: Unknown
title: University student Necme Amini sentenced to death in Iran
content:
23-year-old university student Necme Amini has been sentenced to death in the Iranian city of Mashhad. The student, who was detained during protests in January 2026, announced in a voice message sent from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad that the verdict had been issued on 16 September.




The website “Voice of Iranian Prisoners” published Necme Amini’s voice message on 19 September. The student said that she had been sentenced to death after approximately eight months of uncertainty and called for a fair trial and the right to defend herself.




In her message, Amini appealed to lawyers, legal experts, human rights activists and international organizations, asking them to investigate and follow up on her case.




Previously sentenced to 12 years and 6 months in prison




Branch 1 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court had sentenced Necme Amini to 12 years, 6 months and 1 day in prison on charges of “insulting the Prophet.”




According to reports, the student was detained on 28 February 2026, at Ferdowsi Bazaar in Mashhad and taken to Vakilabad Prison. Sources said that she was denied the right to meet with a lawyer of her own choosing during her detention.




Information regarding Amini's case and the death sentence handed down against her has not yet been confirmed by Iran’s official judicial authorities.

title: Karagöz: Prisoners want the process to move forward
content:
Nearly two years into the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with Abdullah Öcalan’s call, debate continues over steps to implement the framework law and the situation of political prisoners.




Nearly a month has passed since the legislation, adopted by Parliament with the votes of 470 MPs and widely known as the “framework law,” came into force. The Freedom Movement described the law as inadequate but nevertheless regarded it as a step. However, delays in taking concrete steps to implement the law are increasing concerns among prisoners and their families about the process.




Expectations for steps regarding the situation of political prisoners continue, while rights violations, decisions by the Administrative and Observation Boards, and postponements of release also remain on the agenda.




Nurten Karagöz, Co-Chair of the Marmara Association for Solidarity and Assistance with Families of Prisoners and Convicts (MATUHAY-DER), spoke to ANF about developments in prisons over the month since the framework law came into force and the approach of prisoners’ families to the process.




Prolonging the process is causing distrust among prisoners’ families

author: Unknown
title: Defending Kurdistan under fire
content:
The Middle East is passing through a ring of fire in which conflict, political crisis and economic devastation caused by the Third World War are intertwined. At every stage in which the war expands or contracts, basic conditions for survival such as security, shelter and food are turning into areas of severe crisis. The security of existence of the peoples of the region, particularly the Kurds, is coming under increasing threat.




Attacks carried out by states and non-state actors are deepening the security crisis in the Middle East, while the devastation caused by war is driving millions of people into refugee camps, amid ruins or onto migration routes. Conflicts over water, energy and trade routes, along with the disruption of supply chains caused by capitalist plunder and war, are further deepening the economic crisis.




New hegemonic ambitions in the region by the nation-state centres that divided Kurdistan are making this picture even more complex and dangerous. At a time when efforts are underway to reshape the balance of power in the Middle East and Kurdistan has become one of the key arenas of regional power struggles, the long-standing political governance crisis in Southern Kurdistan (Başur) and the failure to form a government are converging with new risks.

title: Two PKK guerrillas, whose remains were relocated from Garzan to Kilyos, identified after nine years
content:
The identities of PKK guerrillas Zehra Kısaoğlu (Raperin) and Süheyla Kaya (Zilan), whose remains were exhumed from Garzan Cemetery in Bitlis and later buried beneath a pavement at Kilyos Cemetery in Istanbul, have been confirmed through DNA matches with samples taken from their families.




The families of Zehra Kısaoğlu and Süheyla Kaya, who died in 1999, were informed on September 17 that the DNA samples had matched. The families then applied to the Zincirlikuyu Cemeteries Directorate in Istanbul before proceeding to Kilyos Cemetery.




According to Zehra Kısaoğlu’s brother, Abdullah Kısaoğlu, his sister left home after completing high school. The family provided DNA samples at various mass grave sites over the years. Kısaoğlu said they learned four days ago that his sister’s remains were in Kilyos.




The remains are expected to be collected from Kilyos Cemetery today and taken to the Karlıova district of Bingöl.




What happened at Garzan Cemetery?




In December 2017, the Turkish state ordered the destruction of the Garzan Cemetery of Martyrs in the province of Bitlis in North Kurdistan. The cemetery is located near the village of Oleka Jor (Upper Ölek), where hundreds of members of the Kurdish guerrilla organisations HPG and YJA-Star and the YPG and YPJ were buried. author: Unknown
title: Akbay: The fundamental task of the youth is to convey the new paradigm to society
content:
ANF spoke with Ibrahim Akbay, a member of the Youth Assembly of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), about the role of youth in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the obstacles encountered during the process, and ideological transformation.




What is the fundamental role assumed by young people in the Peace and Democratic Society Process?




As the constitutive and leading force of society, young people face a historical responsibility in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Today, it is not possible to limit the role of youth merely to carrying out existing party activities or routine youth organizing. In this period, when the construction of a democratic society, democratic nation, and communes is at the center, the practical leading role of youth is intertwined with ideological leadership.




The greatest responsibility for enabling society to understand the values being defended, the struggle being waged, and the life being envisioned falls to the youth, young women, and the women’s movement. Youth continue to occupy the position of being the leading dynamic of society, both specifically in this historical process and independently of the process in every period.

title: 10th Diyarbakır Book Fair to kick off this weekend
content:
The Diyarbakır (Amed) Book Fair will start on Saturday 26 September. Prominent figures from the world of literature and publishing will celebrate the 10th year of the fair. Organized by Tüyap Fairs in cooperation with the Turkish Publishers Association and with the support of the Diyarbakır Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the fair will welcome visitors for nine days at the Mesopotamia International Fair and Congress Centre until 4 October 2026.




Yeni Özgür Politika wrote that the Diyarbakır Book Fair will bring together 125 publishing houses and civil society organizations, and will host a rich cultural programme over nine days. Alongside panels, talks and workshops, the fair will feature activities for children, while hundreds of authors will meet readers at book-signing events. Offering book lovers of different age groups an experience centred on books and literature, the fair will also contribute to the social and cultural life of Diyarbakır and the surrounding region.




73 events




The 10th Diyarbakır Book Fair will host 73 events over nine days, bringing together book lovers with figures from the worlds of literature, culture and art. In addition to talks and panels, the programme will feature theatre performances, music and poetry recitals, and workshops covering literature, history, culture, art, education and social issues. title: Asrın Law Office responds to campaign against Öcalan: “The question of status is important”
content:
The Asrın Law Office has strongly responded to the latest campaigns targeting Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. It said that various circles were attempting to detach the Kurdish question from its historical and political context and reduce the Peace and Democratic Society Process to a sensationalist tabloid debate.




“We are aware that this mentality, which seeks to obscure the historical and political significance of the Kurdish question and reduce the ongoing process to cheap tabloid topics, knows no moral boundaries. These statements reflect an attitude aimed at obstructing society’s pursuit of peace and democracy, as well as discomfort with the prospect of conflict and violence coming to an end.”




According to the Asrın Law Office, which represents Öcalan and his fellow prisoners on the prison island of Imrali, there is currently an opportunity to move the Kurdish question, which has existed for around two centuries, beyond the logic of conflict and violence and address it at the political and legal level. Öcalan, it said, is focusing his efforts on transforming this opportunity into lasting peace and a democratic solution.




“The clearest expression of profiting from blood”

title: Patrichor: We will hold those who damaged the mass graves in Shengal accountable
content:
In Shengal, Iraqi forensic experts have begun work to open a burial site containing the remains of victims of the ISIS genocide. According to Iraqi authorities, the remains of 76 people are believed to be buried in the area.




The remains were recovered from mass graves discovered in the Xanesor (Khanasor) area after Shengal was liberated from the “Islamic State” (ISIS). In 2016, KDP authorities in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq had the remains exhumed and subsequently reburied in the Şerfedîn area, even though the necessary DNA testing had not yet been completed.




Relatives who still had no certainty about the fate of their missing family members subsequently called for the burial site to be reopened. After years of efforts, Iraq’s Directorate for Mass Graves and Missing Persons and the forensic authorities began the exhumation work.




The bones now being recovered will be taken for forensic examination. DNA samples will be collected and compared with those of relatives in order to identify the victims.




Xêrî Elî, head of the Petricor Human Rights Organization, spoke to ANF about the opening of the mass grave in Şerfedîn area.

title: Köker: Strong opposition alliance needed for a democratic republic
content:
Following two years of talks as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the bill known publicly as the “Framework Law”, officially titled the “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration”, was adopted on 10 August with the votes of 467 MPs.




The law, regarded as the first official agreement between the Turkish state and the Kurdish Freedom Movement, has been criticised by intellectuals in Turkey as well as by Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Concerns have repeatedly been raised that the law is problematic in several respects and that making its implementation dependent on the National Security Council is misguided.




Academic Prof. Dr Levent Köker spoke to ANF about the criticisms of the Framework Law and how the process should proceed from this point onwards.




Let me begin with the question currently on Turkey’s agenda: What is the Framework Law, and what do its provisions entail?




The legislation commonly referred to as the ‘Framework Law’, whose full title is the ‘Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration’, essentially regulates the legal status of members of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), which announced some time ago that it had dissolved itself and ended its armed struggle. title: Demo against Solar Power Plant project in Lice: “We will defend our living spaces”
content:
The Derqam Solidarity Platform made a statement in Dêrqam neighborhood in Amed’s Lice district against a Solar Power Plant (SPP) project planned by İskenderun Iron and Steel Company on 800 acres of land.




The Platform drew attention to the project’s potential impact on agricultural land, pastures, forests, livestock farming, and wildlife.




Speaking at the event, platform representative Şeyhmus Dağhan said that they were not opposed to renewable energy but objected to solar energy investments carried out at the expense of fertile agricultural land and natural habitats.




Dağhan called for the project’s impact on agricultural production, livestock farming, and the ecosystem in the region to be examined scientifically and independently.




Ahmet İnan, a lawyer and chair of the Diyarbakır Bar Association’s Environmental and Urban Law Commission, said that approximately 93,000 solar panels were planned to be installed across an area of 800 acres, adding that the project threatened the livelihoods of local villagers.




İnan criticized the decision to issue a positive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) despite local opposition to the project and announced that the Diyarbakır Bar Association and the Ecology Association, together with the villagers, had initiated legal proceedings.

title: "From Jina to Today: Jin Jiyan Azadî" event held in London
content:
Organized by the Jiyan Women’s Assembly under the slogan "From Jina to Today: Jin Jiyan Azadî," a memorial took place at the London Kurdish Community Centre. The gathering paid tribute to Jina Amini and all women who lost their lives, and discussed the historical legacy of the Jin, Jiyan, Azadî struggle as well as the current state of the women’s freedom struggle.




YPJ spokesperson Rûksen Mihemed participated in the event online, while KJAR activist Zeyneb Bayazîdî and Civil and Women’s Rights Activist Sadiye Wekîlî spoke at the venue.




Many years of women's struggle have gone by




Rûksen Mihemed emphasized that the women’s freedom struggle cannot be viewed as a four-year process that began after Jina Amini. “This is not a struggle that has lasted only four years; women’s struggle goes back many years,” Rûksen Mihemed said, noting that through years of organizing and struggle, women have increasingly asserted their own identities and agency.




Mihemed stressed the importance of women existing through their own words, will and identities, and added: “Our language, our thoughts, our spirit, our bodies and our emotions belong to us.” She stated that the gains achieved must be protected and called for stronger solidarity and collective struggle among women.

title: Guerrilla commander Dîlan Şirnex laid to rest in Qandil
content:
Earlier today, the Party of Free Women of Kurdistan (PAJK) announced the death of guerrilla commander Dîlan Şirnex. According to the statement, Şirnex died on September 17 while undergoing cancer treatment. She joined the PKK in 1994 and, according to PAJK, was one of the leading commanders involved in building the autonomous women’s organization.




Masses bid farewell to the female commander at the Mehmet Karasungur Martyrs’ Cemetery in Binarê Qandil. Local residents and many patriots attended the ceremony.




















Addressing the crowd on behalf of PJAK, Sozdar Dilsoz said that Dîlan Şirnex became acquainted with the struggle and joined the Freedom Movement as a guerrilla fighter at a young age.




Dilsoz said that Şirnex joined the struggle without hesitation and with great enthusiasm, adding: “Martyr Dîlan served both as a commander of the women’s forces and as a representative of the women’s movement, struggling in all parts of Kurdistan and across every inch of the country. That is why she fought with great passion until her last breath.”




Stating that the martyrs raised awareness among the people, educated them, and organized them through their struggle, Dilsoz added: “She fought continuously until the day she fell as a martyr. To defend the Rojava Revolution, she fought in Tabqa and Raqqa until the end of the war in Rojava.”

author: Unknown
title: 34 years ago, the killing of Musa Anter
content:
Musa Anter, affectionately known as “Apê Musa” (Uncle Musa), was a prominent Kurdish writer who contributed columns to the daily Özgür Gündem and the weekly Yeni Ülke. He was shot and killed in Diyarbakır on 20 September 1992.




Lured from his hotel by a telephone caller who asked him to help settle a property dispute, Anter and a friend set off in a taxi with an unknown man, described as between 25 and 30 years old. When they began to suspect that a trap was being set, they demanded to get out of the taxi. The man accompanying them also got out and, having walked in front of them, began shooting at them with a gun.




Anter was struck by four bullets and died soon afterward. The friend, hit by two bullets, was seriously injured. Amnesty International reported that a 14-shot 9 mm gun was used in the attack, which the group says occurred on the outskirts of the city near a police station and a manned traffic control point.




Anter, who did not live in Diyarbakır, was visiting the city to sign books during a cultural festival. A previously unknown group, Boz-Ok, claimed responsibility for the killing, but editors at Yeni Ülke and Özgür Gündem discounted the claim, blaming the state and counter-guerrillas.

title: Eva Maria Michelmann: Solidarity freed me, and we will free Ahmet too
content:
German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann spoke in Zurich about her abduction in Raqqa and her subsequent five-month detention in prisons run by the Syrian transitional government. At an event held at the Autonomous School, she also described the final days she spent with her colleague and partner Ahmet Polad and their forcible separation. Polad, whose legal name is Mehmet Nizam Aslan, was transferred to Turkey on September 9 after nearly eight months of detention in Syria. author: Unknown
title: Musa Anter commemorated on the 34th anniversary of his murder in Amed
content:
Kurdish writer and journalist Musa Anter was commemorated in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Sunday. The commemoration took place at the site in the Seyrantepe district where the intellectual, known as Apê (Uncle) Musa, was shot dead on September 20, 1992. The memorial event, organized by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG), was attended by Anter’s relatives, media workers, and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.




Anter’s murder is among the most widely known political crimes of the 1990s. The Susurluk Report, later prepared on behalf of the Turkish prime minister, contained extensive information about the activities of state-backed structures and linked Anter’s murder to Mahmut Yıldırım, alias “Yeşil,” and the military intelligence organization JITEM. A full judicial reckoning with the case has yet to take place.




“For peace, the political murders must be solved”




DFG member Fexredin Kılıç stated that even 34 years after Anter’s death, the structures behind the murder have still not been fully exposed. Referring to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, he called for the political murders of the 1990s to be investigated. “In these days when we are talking about peace, we say it once again at the place where Apê Musa was murdered: For there to be peace, the unresolved political murders must be solved.”

author: Unknown
title: Iraq begins trial of six French ISIS members
content:
The trial of six French nationals accused of membership in the “Islamic State” (ISIS) began on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad. The defendants were transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraq earlier this year. Under tight security, armored military vehicles transported the six men to the Karkh Court of Appeal building. Vehicles carrying French diplomats arrived there later. Journalists were barred from attending the proceedings.




The identities of the six defendants have not yet been made public. They are part of a group of 47 French nationals transferred to Iraq from prisons run by the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria. The group also includes Adrien Guihal, who claimed responsibility on behalf of ISIS for the July 14, 2016 attack in Nice, in which 86 people were killed.




Proceedings against thousands of ISIS members




The trials of the French ISIS members are part of a much larger series of legal proceedings. By mid-February, more than 5,700 suspected ISIS members had been transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraq. According to Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, they represent 67 different nationalities, including 474 Iraqis and 3,497 Syrians. In early September, the Iraqi judiciary announced that the interrogations and investigations involving all 5,704 defendants had been completed. author: Unknown
title: European Kurdish filmmakers meet at workshop
content:
Kurdish filmmakers living in Europe gathered at a workshop in Charleroi, Belgium, to discuss the challenges Kurdish cinema faces in various areas, from production and distribution to festivals and education, and to develop common solutions.




The three-day gathering, attended by around 50 filmmakers, includes directors, screenwriters, producers, actors, cinematographers, editors, and festival organizers.




Explaining the purpose of the workshop, the organizers said: “We want to make films, write screenplays, organize festivals, and distribute films. We face different problems in each area of work. We are holding this workshop to solve these problems.”




Kurdish filmmakers came together at the Çanda Med Cultural Center on September 18. At the reception held on the first day of the gathering, the filmmakers introduced themselves and their work. Filmmakers working in different countries and in different areas thus had the opportunity to get to know one another and share their experiences.




Joint discussion in four areas 




Following the introductions, the filmmakers divided into four working groups. The groups were organized around the themes of distribution and festivals, production and financing, education and development, and international solidarity. Each filmmaker joined one of the groups according to their area of work and interest.

title: Doğan: Roma Alevis’ demands span interconnected areas
content:
Alevis in Turkey have faced repression, massacres and various forms of discrimination for many years. Roma Alevis face these forms of discrimination as well as the additional problem of not being fully accepted within the Alevi community itself.




Ozan Doğan, author of the book Roma Alevis, spoke to ANF about the problems facing Roma Alevis. He said: “The term ‘Roma Alevis’ refers to a diverse range of communities distinguished by their ties to Alevi ocaks and their different social experiences.”




Roma Alevis have different relationships with the Alevi ocak system




Doğan said Roma Alevis have distinct relationships with the Alevi ocak system and continued:




“The term ‘Roma Alevis’ refers to a heterogeneous population with different ethno-cultural characteristics and social experiences. In Turkey, these communities are generally described by outsiders as Roma or Gypsies. However, these groups do not use the term ‘Gypsy’ because of its pejorative connotations. ‘Roma’, meanwhile, is generally used as an umbrella term encompassing different groups such as Rom, Dom and Lom.




An important distinction needs to be made here. Many groups of nomadic origin are regarded as Gypsy or Roma because of factors such as their livelihood strategies, physical appearance, social status or settlement patterns.
