author: Unknown
title: Bedreddin, Dersim and the Alevi pursuit of justice and equality
content:
The social movements that emerged at different points in Alevi history cannot be regarded as identical. One of the threads running through this history, however, is resistance to injustice. Dersim remains one of the deepest wounds in Alevi memory and continues to hold an important place in discussions about peace today.




Alevi history cannot be confined to the 16th and 20th centuries alone. Social movements that emerged in Anatolia at different periods have found different places in Alevi memory through their pursuit of justice and equality and their opposition to oppression. The movements led by Baba Ilyas and Baba Ishak were among the significant challenges to the social and political inequalities of their time. The movement that developed around Sheikh Bedreddin, meanwhile, has been interpreted in different ways for centuries in debates over sharing, equality and social justice.




“Everything should be shared except the beloved’s cheek” has remained in collective memory as one of the most powerful expressions of the egalitarian interpretation of Bedreddin’s legacy. It may not be historically accurate to define all these movements as modern Alevi movements in today’s sense. Yet it is not difficult to understand why they found a place in Alevi memory. author: Unknown
title: Şimşek: No solution without an active society and local democracy
content:
The failure to develop local democracy and the exclusion of society from decision-making processes lie at the heart of the ongoing crises in Turkey and the Middle East. Ali Şimşek, a politician with many years of experience in legal democratic politics, spoke to ANF in Lausanne about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, democratic integration and models of local government.




Şimşek compared Switzerland’s experience of direct democracy, based on its 26 cantons, with the power-centred political mentality prevailing in the Middle East, stressing that society must play a direct role in resolving its own problems. Şimşek said, “Submitting to the system and dissolving within it is not integration; it is assimilation,” and arguing that a lasting solution requires democratic integration in which different communities participate while preserving their distinct identities.







 







As you know, the Peace and Democratic Society Process has been under way in Turkey for nearly two years. Democratic integration has also become a subject of debate following Abdullah Öcalan’s call. You were involved in legal democratic politics for many years. For democratic integration to take place, how should local democracy be developed first? What needs to be done to strengthen local democracy?

author: Unknown
title: Zekiye Dêrazor: I found my courage in the mountains of Kurdistan
content:
The mountains of Kurdistan carry a unique meaning not only because of their grandeur, but also because of the countless stories of lives and struggles they have witnessed. Having witnessed the lives, suffering, joys, and victories of guerrillas, the mountains have become, for those waging a struggle for freedom, not merely a place of struggle but also a place for getting to know oneself and discovering one’s own strength.




One of those who turned toward the mountains of Kurdistan in search of freedom is Zekiye Dêrazor, a YJA Star guerrilla from the Arab people. Raised in a patriotic family, Dêrazor deepened her search for freedom after being influenced by the experiences of martyrdom and struggle within her family.




Dêrazor first came to know the YPJ (Women’s Protection Units) and was influenced by the stance and determination of women in the struggle. Encountering the power of women to change and rebuild life within the ranks of the YPJ, Dêrazor spent some time engaged in the struggle within the YPJ in Rojava.




After joining the YPJ, Dêrazor became acquainted with Abdullah Öcalan’s concept of the democratic nation. She later turned toward the mountains of Kurdistan and decided to join the guerrilla ranks.

author: Unknown
title: Nurettin Demirtaş: The commune is the spirit of collective life and freedom
content:
Nurettin Demirtaş, a member of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, spoke to ANF about the concept of the commune as a model of communal life, freedom, and organization.




Demirtaş said that, drawing on the historical experiences of the struggle, they take organization on the basis of communes as their starting point. Defining the commune as a structure representing society’s side in the historical contradiction between society and the state, Demirtaş added that communal life, solidarity, women’s freedom, and social freedom form the basis of communal life.




Emphasizing that communal life does not arise spontaneously, Demirtaş noted that it requires consciousness, organization, and labor. Demirtaş said: “We will resist through communality, and we will become free through communality.”







 







Nurettin Demirtaş made the following assessment: “Based on the immense experiences of our struggle, today we take organization on the basis of communes as our starting point. Throughout history, there have been the state and powers on one side and society on the other. They have always been in contradiction.




The commune represents society’s side in this contradiction. Önder Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] opened up the dichotomy between the state and the commune in the manifesto and, from a historical perspective, illuminated what we need to do today as well. The commune is a spirit.

author: Unknown
title: 11 people killed in explosion in Deir ez-Zor
content:
An explosion occurred on Friday in the town of Ayash, west of Deir ez-Zor. The relevant authorities said the explosion took place at an ammunition depot belonging to the Ministry of Defense.




According to the latest information, 11 people were killed and 10 were injured in the explosion. Search and rescue efforts are continuing in the area.

author: Unknown
title: Kürkçü: The direction of the new era will be determined by the Kurdish Movement’s struggle
content:
Assessing the stage reached in the Democratic Society and Peace Process and the steps expected to be taken from here, HDP Honorary Chair Ertuğrul Kürkçü spoke to ANF about Abdullah Öcalan’s role in the process, the position of state institutions, the new period facing Kurdish politics, and the implications of developments in Syria for Turkey.




The direction of Kurdish politics will be decisive in the new era




Assessing where the main sticking point lies in the next stage of the “Democratic Society and Peace Process,” Kürkçü said: “Abdullah Öcalan and his organization have done what they could do. What comes next is the question of how the Kurds will participate, as equal citizens with equal rights, in the reconstruction of this society within this new space and this new political arena that has now opened up, and what kind of political line they will pursue. From the very beginning, the state viewed this process as a means of bringing the conflict to an end. Its objective was to reach some kind of mutual agreement with Öcalan in particular, and through him with the PKK, on ending the conflict. We see that they have left everything after that to the future. They have undertaken no commitments. They have made no binding promises.

author: Unknown
title: Paris City Hall hosts commemoration honoring Jina Amini and women’s resistance
content:
The 7th Commission of the Paris City Council held a commemorative evening marking the fourth anniversary of the killing of Jina Amini, highlighting Iranian women’s struggle for freedom spanning more than a century.




Held in the evening at the Hôtel de Ville, the event drew a large audience and was hosted by Commission President Geneviève Garrigos. It was organized in partnership with Neda d’Iran, Damavand, and Comité contre la répression, organizations working with Iranian and exiled communities. The collaboration highlighted the Paris City Council’s institutional support for the women’s movement in Iran and for the universal demand for freedom embodied in the slogan “Femme, Vie, Liberté / Jin, Jiyan, Azadî.”




Representatives of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in France (Tevgera Jinên Kurd li Fransa – TJK-F) were also among the invited guests at the commemoration, which began in the historic setting of the Hôtel de Ville. Human rights defenders, feminist organizations, Iranian activists in exile, and representatives of diaspora communities in France attended the evening. Speeches, testimonies, and performances addressing women’s freedom, state violence, repressive regimes, civil disobedience, and global solidarity created a powerful political and emotional atmosphere. author: Unknown
title: ISIS attack disrupts power supply in Baiji and Haditha
content:
Following an attack by the terrorist organization “Islamic State” (ISIS), the power supply in Baiji, in Salahaddin province, and Haditha, in al-Anbar, was disrupted. According to Saad Ghazi, chairman of the Security and Defense Committee of the Anbar Provincial Council, ISIS members blew up an electricity pylon on the high-voltage transmission line between the two cities on Friday evening.




Security forces were deployed to the area following the attack. According to a security source, they prevented another transmission line from being blown up. After a subsequent armed clash with ISIS members, the area was brought under control.




Technical teams began assessing the damage and repairing the power line.

title: Femicides in Batman and Osmaniye: Two women and three children killed
content:
Two women and three children have been killed in two cases of patriarchal violence in Batman and Osmaniye. In Batman, a 29-year-old man is suspected of stabbing his wife and their two young children to death before taking his own life. In Osmaniye, Didar Filiz, who was six months pregnant, was killed.




The first femicide occurred on Friday afternoon in the district of Kozluk in Batman. Following an emergency call, medical teams and police were dispatched to an apartment in a five-story building. Emergency responders found 29-year-old A.G. dead by hanging. His 27-year-old wife, S.G., and their two children, E.G. and M.P.G., had sustained stab wounds. The children were two and one year old, respectively. All four were pronounced dead at the scene.




According to the governor’s office, based on the evidence gathered so far, investigators believe that A.G. killed his wife and their two children before taking his own life. The bodies were taken for autopsy. Authorities are investigating a possible connection to an earlier dispute involving gold. A.G.’s brother-in-law had reportedly filed a complaint in May, stating that he had entrusted A.G. with around 2.5 kilograms of pure gold for safekeeping and was later unable to reach him. The governor’s office said it is investigating whether the dispute was connected to the killings.

title: Protest in Zurich against deportations: “Human dignity cannot be deported”
content:
In Zurich, numerous people protested against Switzerland’s deportation policy and the increasing number of forced returns. Kurdish organizations, revolutionary groups from Turkey, as well as feminist and anarchist initiatives called for an end to deportations that expose people to persecution, imprisonment, or mistreatment.




The demonstration began at Bürkliplatz on the shore of Lake Zurich. Participants included the Democratic Kurdish Community Center (Dem-Kurd), the Federation of Migrant Workers in Switzerland (IGIF), the Swiss Federation of Democratic Rights (IDHF), the Federation of Workers from Turkey in Switzerland (ITIF), the Pangea Collective and Kulturfabrik, as well as feminist and anarchist groups from Switzerland.




Deportations kill




Before the demonstration began, activists boarded a sightseeing boat docked at Bürkliplatz harbor. There, they unfurled banners reading “Deportation Kills” and “No to Deportations” and chanted slogans. They then joined the demonstration in the square.




















From there, the protest march proceeded through central Zurich, with slogans chanted in Kurdish, Turkish, and German. Participants chanted, among other things, “No to Deportation” and “Long Live the Solidarity of the Peoples.”

author: Unknown
title: FEDA in Geneva: Alevi demands must be part of the peace process
content:
In Geneva, the Democratic Alevi Federation (FEDA) has launched a two-day vigil in support of the process for peace and a democratic society. The organization is combining its support for the process with concrete demands for equality, constitutional recognition, and accountability for Turkish state policies targeting Alevis.




Alongside Alevi organizations, revolutionary, democratic, and civil society groups are also taking part in the action. A tent set up on Friday is hosting discussions on the peace process and meetings with various institutions. The action is scheduled to conclude today with a joint rally in front of the United Nations headquarters.




The Geneva vigil is part of a series of activities held in September in cities including Zurich, Strasbourg, St. Gallen, Leverkusen, Dortmund, and Paris. As part of these activities, the participating organizations held talks and visited various institutions.






















“No free and equal society without peace”




Songül Aslan, co-spokesperson of FEDA Switzerland, described the process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan as a historic opportunity to end the decades-long conflict in Turkey and establish lasting peace. “As Reya Heq Alevis, we support this process and embrace it as our own. Without peace, an equal and free life and a democratic society are not possible,” Aslan said.

title: Şebnem Korur Fincancı: The course of the process depends on the conditions on Imrali
content:
What does it take to turn the end of armed conflict into lasting peace? For human rights defender and forensic medicine expert Prof. Dr. Şebnem Korur Fincancı, the answer lies not merely in the silencing of weapons. Democratization, guarantees of fundamental rights, truth and justice, and the active participation of society are indispensable.




In an interview with ANF, Fincancı discusses the conditions necessary for effective negotiations, Abdullah Öcalan’s conditions on Imrali, and the consequences of decades of conflict for public health. She argues that negotiations do not mean the end of the struggle for rights; rather, they must create the space for democratic politics and social participation to replace violence.




From a human rights perspective, what specific criteria must a “genuine and dignified peace” be based on?




First of all, we must not define peace solely as the silencing of weapons. It is, of course, extraordinarily important that people are no longer dying and that the conflict comes to an end. But that is the beginning of peace, not peace itself.




The foundation of genuine and dignified peace is human dignity, equal citizenship, the protection of rights, and people’s ability to have a say in decisions affecting their own lives. author: Unknown
title: Murat Çakır: Germany is openly playing a dangerous game
content:
Should Germany’s state elections and the rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) be seen merely as a temporary shift in voting patterns? Or are they a direct consequence of the political establishment, Germany’s militarist turn and the deepening crisis of capitalism? Murat Çakır, a researcher at the Rosa Luxemburg Foundation, said mainstream parties are legitimising fascist rhetoric by resorting to anti-refugee demagoguery, while the reformist left has deepened this political vacuum by moving away from genuine class politics. Caught between economic decline, deindustrialisation and growing hostility towards Russia, Germany is putting increasing pressure on workers at home while pursuing a dangerous course of militarism abroad that could open the door to nuclear catastrophe.




Writer and researcher Murat Çakır said the only way to confront the growing threats of fascism and war in Germany in particular and Europe more broadly is for migrants and workers to strengthen a common social struggle along anti-capitalist and anti-militarist lines.




I would like to ask about the elections in Germany, the possible scenarios and their potential short-, medium- and long-term implications. title: Outcry over statute of limitations ruling in Rıdvan Karakoç case
content:
Rıdvan Karakoç disappeared after being taken into custody on 15 February 1995. His body was found around three months later at the Altınşehir Cemetery for the Unclaimed and was identified by his family.




A statement was issued outside the Istanbul Anatolian Courthouse, calling for the investigation to continue and for those responsible to be brought to justice.




Oya Ersoy, Co-Chair of the Human Rights Association (IHD), said the autopsy report indicated that Karakoç’s death bore signs of violence and torture.




Ersoy said that although Karakoç’s clothes had been registered as evidence in the case, they were never examined or subjected to DNA analysis. She added that witnesses identified by the family had provided important information concerning Karakoç’s enforced disappearance in custody.




The IHD said enforced disappearance is a continuing offence and that statutes of limitations cannot apply to crimes against humanity, announcing that it would appeal the decision. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the association said it would take the case to the Constitutional Court and the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).

title: Amed march calls for status and education rights for Kurdish
content:
A march calling for education in the mother tongue was organised in Amed under the leadership of the Mesopotamia Language and Culture Research Association (MED-DER). Representatives of political parties and civil society organisations, along with many residents, joined the march from NCity shopping centre to Koşuyolu Park.




Participants carried a banner in Kirmanckî and Kurmancî reading “Status for Kurdish, education in Kurdish” (“Statuya Kurdî, perwerdehiya bi Kurdî”), as well as placards bearing the message “Education in the mother tongue is a fundamental right” (“Perwerdehiya bi zimanê dayikê mafekî bingehîn e”). The crowd marched to Kurdish songs and chanted slogans including “There is no life without language” (“Bê ziman jiyan nabe”), “Our language is our existence” (“Zimanê me hebûna me ye”), “Bê Serok Apo” and “Woman, Life, Freedom, freedom for Öcalan” (“Jin, jiyan, azadî, azad bike Rêbertî”).




Demand for status for Kurdish and the right to education




A statement was issued in front of the Human Rights Monument at Koşuyolu Park at the end of the march. MED-DER executive Şükran Yakut said that although the new academic year had begun, Kurdish children continued to be denied the right to education in their mother tongue.

author: Unknown
title: What does Alevi history tell us?
content:
A debate sparked by a declaration signed by 53 Alevi intellectuals and writers has once again raised the question of how Alevi history should be understood. Rather than carrying the hostilities of the past into the present, there is a need to reconsider the Alevi understanding of truth, justice, consent and humanity.




The debate sparked by the declaration signed by 53 Alevi intellectuals and writers has once again brought the question of how Alevi history should be approached in Turkey to the forefront. On one side are references to the historical memory of Alevis through Sultan Selim I and Idris-i Bitlisi; on the other is a broader reading of Alevi history extending from Shah Ismail Hatayi and Pir Sultan Abdal to Bedreddin and Seyit Rıza.




Reducing the issue to a debate over “Sultan Selim or Shah Ismail?” overlooks the much broader social and spiritual heritage of Alevi history. Alevi history is not merely a history of sultans, wars and struggles for power. Alevi spiritual lineages, cem (Alevi communal worship ceremony), deyiş (Alevi devotional song), women, exiles, massacres and resistance are also part of this history. Running through all of them is a powerful search for truth that has been passed down from generation to generation.

title: Merve Asya Özgür: If Kurdish artists are free, Turkish artists also gain - Part Two
content:
Actress Merve Asya Özgür, one of the lead actresses in Pelin Esmer’s latest film And the Rest Will Follow, in which she plays the character Aliye, spoke to ANF about the relationship between art and peace.




Part one of this interview can be read 

here

You seem to be saying that artists need freedom in order to find the courage to speak. Wouldn’t positive progress in this process help create that freedom?




We were quite critical of the artistic community earlier, but there are also people who genuinely have something to say and cannot express it because of the pressure they face. There is, first of all, a major problem of censorship. These conditions inevitably create their own artistic language. People often say, ‘Art somehow finds a way and creates a new form.’ There is some truth in that, of course. But repression and the inability to speak under that pressure eventually turn into a collective silence, beginning with the self-censorship of those who would otherwise speak out. Then a new generation emerges within that collective silence. They enter the creative process, quietly settle into a corner and fall into line with that silence. The spiral of silence expands to include the new generation, while subdued forms of artistic expression remain trapped within the same vicious cycle.

title: Kurt: Families of different faiths united in mourning
content:
The Kurdish Freedom Movement has announced the names of guerrillas whose martyrdoms could not be made public in previous years because of wartime conditions. Following the announcements, collective condolences and commemorations were held in many cities across Kurdistan and Turkey.




Ilhami Kurt, Co-Chair of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER), has been informing families in Istanbul of the martyrdoms and helping organise condolences and commemorations. Kurt spoke to ANF about the process of contacting the families and what lies ahead.




More than 100 martyrs have been announced in Istanbul




Kurt said that the number of martyrs announced in Istanbul has exceeded 100: “I offer my condolences to all our people, to the families of our martyred comrades and to their mothers. Announcements were first made for Istanbul’s first and third districts, followed by the second district. More than 100 martyrs were announced. Together with all our institutions, we visited the families and established contact with them. As the process was also being covered in the press, we stood by our families.”

author: Unknown
title: Sarıtaş: Process must advance towards a democratic republic
content:
Political scientist Mehmet Zahir Sarıtaş said the Democratic Society and Peace Process, which has been under way for nearly two years, has created an important platform for discussion on resolving the Kurdish question. He said a lasting solution depends on establishing a new political and social framework based on freedom, human rights, justice and equality. Sarıtaş noted that the abandonment of the strategy of armed struggle has placed democratic politics at the centre, stressing that the state must respond by changing and transforming its own approach.




Sarıtaş said discussions on resolving the Kurdish question cannot be confined to ending the conflict. He noted that both the debates that have emerged over the course of the Kurdish struggle during the past 50 years and the universal values developed around democracy and democratic society across the world provide an important framework for a solution. He said the fundamental question is whether these values will be taken as the basis of the current process.




Sarıtaş stressed that universal values must be embraced in order to build democratic governance and a democratic society. He said the emergence of the Kurdish question itself is linked to the failure to adequately uphold these values in relations between the state and society. Freedom, justice and equality, he added, are fundamental conditions for societies to live

title: People in Cizre rally for education in mother tongue and official status for Kurdish
content:
In the district of Cizre in Şırnak province, numerous people demonstrated for the right to education in the Kurdish language. The protest, held under the demand “Official Status for Kurdish and Education in Kurdish,” was organized by the Platform of Democratic Institutions and Language Organizations.




The demonstrators gathered in front of the Birca Belek Language and Culture Association and marched to the historic Birca Belek Fortress, chanting slogans in Kurdish. Alongside a banner reading “Official Status for Kurdish, Education in Kurdish,” participants carried placards calling for education in their mother tongue.







In front of the fortress, Cahit Akıl, a board member of the Birca Belek Language and Culture Association, read out a joint statement by the participating organizations.




‘Education in Kurdish is a human right’




Adnan Şenbayram, co-chair of the Eğitim Sen education union in Şırnak, said afterward that millions of children had begun the new school year without being educated in their mother tongue. “Eğitim Sen has been campaigning for the right to mother-tongue education for many years. Every child has the right to be educated in their own language,” Şenbayram said. He also stressed that offering Kurdish as an elective subject in schools does not fulfill this demand. author: Unknown
title: “Right to Hope”: Council of Europe to put Turkey on agenda in December
content:
The Council of Europe’s Committee of Ministers will once again address Turkey’s implementation of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) judgments concerning the so-called “right to hope” in December. The Gurban group of cases has been placed on the provisional list of cases to be examined at the Committee’s next human rights meeting. The 1577th meeting of the Committee of Ministers on the supervision of the implementation of ECtHR judgments will take place in Strasbourg from December 1 to 3.




Under the Gurban group of cases, the Committee of Ministers is monitoring ECtHR judgments concerning life imprisonment without a realistic possibility of review and release. The issue also concerns Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, whose prison conditions were the subject of the ECtHR judgment “Öcalan No. 2.” In 2014, the Court found that a life sentence without the prospect of review violates the prohibition of inhuman or degrading treatment.




Implementation pending for years




The Committee of Ministers last addressed the Gurban group of cases in September 2025. At the time, it once again called on Turkey to take the necessary legislative and other measures to implement the ECtHR judgments. Ankara was asked to report to the Committee on relevant progress by the end of June 2026. The group of cases was therefore expected to be considered again at the human rights meeting in Sep

title: Demirtaş: We want to turn dialogue and negotiation into a culture of life
content:
Nurettin Demirtaş, a member of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, said that dialogue and negotiation, which have come to the forefront in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, should not merely be a method used to resolve political issues but rather a culture extended to all areas of social life.




“Living and enabling others to live will replace dying and killing,” Demirtaş said, adding that the process led by Abdullah Öcalan as chief negotiator should be strengthened through dialogue and negotiation among different segments of society.




















Speaking to ANF, Nurettin Demirtaş stated the following:




“The method that has come to the forefront in the Peace and Democratic Society Process is dialogue and negotiation. Dialogue defines the relationship between people. Social life takes shape around it. Without dialogue, there can be no social cohesion. It becomes impossible to understand one another.




When it comes to politics, however, it can be said to have a somewhat deeper meaning. Because it defines the relationship between groups with different political goals and objectives, and this relationship goes beyond everyday dialogue. Discussions are held over aims and objectives, and efforts are made to find common ground.




‘We want to turn negotiation into a culture’

title: Justice Minister Akın Gürlek calls on AKP to back Erdoğan’s re-election in 2028
content:
Turkish Justice Minister Akın Gürlek has called on AKP organizations to work toward the re-election of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in 2028. Speaking at a meeting with the AKP’s provincial organization in Adana on Friday, Gürlek said that party structures would have a crucial role to play. “An election will be held in 2028 to re-elect our president,” Gürlek said. He added that party members bore a “very important responsibility” and needed to maintain a presence on the ground and engage with the public.




Uçum suggests April 16, 2028




Gürlek further stated that the political program described by the AKP as the “Century of Turkey” must continue under Erdoğan’s leadership. His remarks came one day after statements by Mehmet Uçum, Erdoğan’s chief adviser and deputy chair of the Presidential Legal Policies Board. Uçum said that Erdoğan should run once more in the next presidential election and that, in his view, it would be Erdoğan’s final candidacy.




Uçum suggested April 16, 2028, the anniversary of the 2017 constitutional referendum that introduced the presidential system, as a possible election date. He explicitly presented this as his own proposal rather than a fixed election date. He linked this scenario to a parliamentary decision to renew the elections. According to his legal interpretation, such a decision would pave the way for Erdoğan to run again. Gürlek himsel

title: DEM Party calls for special parliamentary session on economic crisis
content:
The co-chairs of the DEM Party, Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan, have called for an extraordinary session of the Turkish parliament in response to the ongoing economic crisis. The National Assembly should not wait until the new parliamentary year officially begins on October 1, the co-chairs said. “We are facing an interconnected crisis that affects millions of citizens and the entire economy,” they said in a joint written statement.




Hatimoğulları and Bakırhan pointed to persistently high inflation, rising bankruptcies and debt, increasing fuel prices and geopolitical risks. They said these problems had been compounded by the recent turmoil on the Istanbul stock exchange. “The Turkish economy is no longer showing warning signs; the alarm bells are ringing,” the co-chairs said. They called on the government to take concrete steps rather than stand by as millions of people, tradespeople, farmers and producers struggle with difficult economic conditions.




Stock market turmoil deepens the crisis




The statement was prompted in particular by recent developments on the Istanbul stock exchange. After several investment funds ran into payment difficulties and further reports concerning companies involved put additional pressure on the markets, the benchmark BIST 100 index fell by more than six percent at one point. An automatic market-wide trading halt was triggered. B

author: Unknown
title: Three members of Internal Security Forces killed in Daraa
content:
Internal Security Forces raided a house in the city of Al-Sanamayn in Daraa Governorate. During the ensuing clashes, Internal Security Forces members Mistefa Seed El Din, Selum El Misalma and Nail El Sefdi were killed, while several others were injured.

Tensions remain high in Al-Sanamayn following the incident, and security forces have imposed a curfew.

The Daraa Governorate Internal Security Forces Command stated that it is closely monitoring the incidents that took place in Al-Sanamayn this morning.

title: Bayık: As long as Öcalan is not physically freed, the state’s law will not be implemented
content:
In an extensive interview with NÛÇE TV’s Hevpeyvîn program, Cemil Bayik, co-chair of the KCK (Kurdistan Communities Union) Executive Council, answered a wide variety of questions regarding the progress of the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey, as well as developments in the region. Bayik particularly emphasized the crucial role played by the situation of the Kurdish people’s leader, Abdullah Öcalan, and offered insights into various aspects of the struggle.






















What stage is the Peace and Democratic Society Process at?




The law passed by the Turkish Parliament does not meet our demands. The Turkish state enacted this law not in accordance with our demands, but rather in line with its own interests. The primary purpose of this law is the disarmament and disbandment of the guerrillas. Some articles have been included in the law that are not very important from our perspective. This is their law; we have our own laws as well. Neither their laws nor our laws are being enforced. There is a struggle between us and the Turkish state over this law.




What is important to us is ensuring that the necessary conditions and circumstances are in place for Rêber Apo [Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan] to carry out this process and bring it to a successful conclusion. This newly enacted law contains no principles regarding the resolution of the Kurdish

author: Unknown
title: Mızraklı: Society must shape its own future
content:
Selçuk Mızraklı, former Co-Mayor of Amed (Diyarbakır) Metropolitan Municipality, who was imprisoned after a government-appointed trustee took over the municipality in August 2019 and was released after completing his sentence, assessed the ongoing peace and democratisation process in Turkey.




Mızraklı said there is cautious hope within society alongside uncertainty about what lies ahead, stressing that lasting peace cannot be achieved simply by the parties shaking hands. He described the rule of law as the “first milestone” of the process and democratisation as the second.




In your first statement after your release, you emphasised “democracy, peace and a solution” and said the process needed to be transparent. How do you assess the process today? What do you observe in society’s approach to it?




Making observations about society genuinely requires a great deal of time and energy. It requires communicating and building relationships with different sections of society and creating spaces where more candid conversations and exchanges can take place. If you look at a city from a bus passing through it, you make judgements based on the buildings, the people walking along the streets, how they are dressed or what they are carrying. Yet none of these things may represent even one ten-thousandth or one hundred-thousandth of everything that city has produced and contains.

author: Unknown
title: KESK Women’s Conference releases final declaration
content:
The final declaration of the 3rd Women’s Conference, organized by the Confederation of Public Employees’ Trade Unions (KESK) under the slogan “Our legacy is resistance, our word is struggle,” was released.




The declaration stated that the struggle against inequalities and forms of domination over women’s labor, bodies, identities, cultures, nature, and right to life would continue. It called for childcare, eldercare, care for the sick, and care for people with disabilities to be removed from the specific responsibility of women and families and organized as a free and high-quality public service.




Women's participation in trade unions will be strenghtened




KESK stated that women’s councils and commissions should be strengthened so that women can have a voice and decision-making power in workplaces and trade unions. It said that meetings and events should be planned in a way that ensures women’s care responsibilities and time poverty do not prevent them from participating in trade union activities.




The declaration also emphasized that education should be organized on the basis of equality, free of charge, secular, democratic, scientific, in people’s mother tongues, and with an approach that upholds gender equality.




Call for action against violence

author: Unknown
title: Iran Human Rights publishes names of over 4,200 people killed in January protests
content:
Iran Human Rights (IHRNGO) has published the names of more than 4,200 people killed during the January 2026 protests in Iran, following months of collecting information, comparing sources, and verifying the identities of victims.




Rojhelat Info

 translated the main findings into English and said that according to the report, at least 420 women and 281 children under the age of 18 are among those identified. Twenty-five of the children were under 14, and the youngest recorded victim was only four and a half months old.




The organization says a large part of the killings took place on January 8 and 9. At least 3,356 people, or 91 percent of the cases where the exact date of death is known, were killed during those two days.




Deaths were documented in cities across 30 of Iran’s 31 provinces. The report also documents repeated patterns of deadly force, including direct fire at protesters, shots aimed at vital parts of the body, shooting people from behind or while they were fleeing, and the use of snipers.




The Iranian authorities have officially announced a death toll of 3,117 people, but Iran Human Rights says the government’s own lists are incomplete. The organization stressed that the figure of more than 4,200 represents only the minimum number of verified deaths and should not be considered the final toll.

title: Family of Mazlum Rizgar Diyar: We will keep our martyrs’ legacy alive
content:
Mazlum Rizgar Diyar (Abdullah Karaviş), a guerrilla of the People’s Defence Forces (HPG) from Şırnak (Şirnex), whose martyrdom was recently announced, was martyred in İdil (Hezex) in 2015 during the struggle for the freedom of the Kurdish people and a democratic life. Diyar joined the guerrilla ranks at a young age and dedicated his life to the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom. Following in the footsteps of family members who had been martyred before him, he took on responsibilities in different areas of the freedom struggle until his martyrdom.




His elder brother, Hakim Karaviş, spoke to ANF about his family’s history of struggle and the legacy left by the martyrs.




We are indebted to the martyrs until our last breath




Hakim Karaviş began by paying tribute to all the martyrs of the freedom struggle. He said the losses his family had suffered represented not only profound grief but also a responsibility to uphold the legacy of struggle left behind by the martyrs.




Karaviş said his family had been involved in the Kurdish people’s freedom struggle for many years and would continue to honour the martyrs and their struggle throughout their lives.




Karaviş also said: “We bow with respect before all our martyrs who lost their lives in the struggle for the freedom of our country. Until our last breath, we remain indebted to their efforts and their struggle. With gr

author: Unknown
title: Merve Asya Özgür: If Kurdish artists are free, Turkish artists also gain - Part One
content:
Actress Merve Asya Özgür, one of the lead actresses in Pelin Esmer’s latest film And the Rest Will Follow, in which she plays the character Aliye, spoke to ANF about the relationship between art and peace.




Özgür said war creates “new distances and new forms of polarisation” between communities, stressing that the Peace and Democratic Society Process is important not only for Kurdish artists but also for Turkish artists, women and workers. She said the process could help bring social groups that have been driven apart closer together again.




Özgür also reflected on the way artists approach the Kurdish question and said: “Artists in the west of the country who have acted as though an issue that has been visible in this region for years simply did not exist may now turn and look at it.”




Özgür stressed that artists need to be more political and courageous, adding that art can play an important role in building broader social support for peace.




What can the relationship between art, prejudice and confrontation teach us when it comes to the issues facing this country?




If we look back at human history, we see that ‘everything’, what we call history itself, is in fact a collection of stories. Long before today’s sanitised spaces of art, the halls, stages and exhibitions, even before language existed, we were beings who somehow managed to tell one another our stories

title: Osman: Kurds should pursue their struggle politically and diplomatically in the new period
content:
At a time when political balances are being reshaped in the Middle East, significant developments are also taking place in the regions where Kurds live. In Iraq, discussions are underway about the future of armed groups and the state’s role in security, while the region’s political and security balances are being reassessed. In Rojava, meanwhile, the future of the gains achieved by Kurds through years of struggle, education and language policies, and the integration process with the administration in Damascus have come to the fore. The political process underway in Turkey regarding a solution to the Kurdish issue is also bringing discussions about a new period, alongside regional developments.




Former Iraqi parliamentarian and Kurdish politician Muhsin Osman assessed the developments facing Kurds in the new period and the methods of struggle they should pursue. Addressing a range of issues, from the future of Sinjar and the gains in Rojava to the relationships Kurds have established with different states in the past and the importance of political and diplomatic struggle, Osman stressed that Kurds need to develop their own political strategy in the new period and protect the gains achieved in different areas.




Persistence on education in Kurdish in Rojava is necessary




Osman said that an important struggle has been waged for years in Rojava in the fields of education a

author: Unknown
title: Berwari: Kurds must develop a common will and strategy
content:
The Middle East is going through a new struggle over power and influence, placing Kurds at a critical juncture. A new wave of attacks is targeting the gains Kurds have achieved across different parts of Kurdistan, while regional balances of power are being reshaped.




Dr Kamuran Berwari spoke to ANF about developments in the region and said Kurds must build their own national policy, defence capacity and common political will rather than seeking a place within balances shaped by other powers.




There can be no disarmament without guarantees




Berwari said discussions over laying down arms and the future of the armed struggle in the process with Turkey should not be reduced solely to the question of “disarmament”. He stressed that the debate must also address how the national and political gains achieved through decades of struggle will be protected, what guarantees will safeguard them and how Kurds will defend themselves in the period ahead.




Berwari underlined the need to establish a constitutional and legal framework before any formal agreement is reached with Turkey, stressing that Kurdish interests must be guaranteed within such a framework. He said the necessary laws and regulations must be introduced, political mechanisms put into operation and a diplomatic dimension incorporated into the process, emphasising that the question of disarmament cannot be considered

author: Unknown
title: Death toll from Kobanê prison fire rises to 10
content:
Mesud Hemo Reşo, a prisoner injured during the fire at the Kobanê prison, lost his life late at night at a hospital in Aleppo where he was being treated.




Nine prisoners had lost their lives and 17 people were injured as a result of the fire that broke out in the prison on 12 September.




The nine people who lost their lives were laid to rest during a mass ceremony held in Kobanê on Saturday (14 September). The investigation launched following the fire is ongoing.

title: Sînemok: A village where history and nature meet at the foot of Qandil Mountain
content:
Located at the foot of Qandil Mountain, the village of Sînemok stands out not only for its natural beauty but also for its historical structures. Situated next to the village of Suredê on the slopes of Qandil Mountain, the village is home to vineyards and gardens filled with numerous fruit trees surrounding both old and new buildings.




















Resembling a forest surrounded by fruit trees, Sînemok draws particular attention for its old structures. Villagers are committed to preserving these buildings, which bear traces of their history and culture. For the village elders, these structures also hold important memories of the past.




Although the exact date when the village was founded is unknown, according to accounts from elderly villagers, Sînemok’s history dates back at least a hundred years.




















Mam, one of the oldest residents of the village, describes its history and life as follows: “I was born in this village. My father and grandfather were also born here. It is an old and ancient village. Sînemok’s history goes back many years. I am not old enough to remember when the village was founded.”




Mam also recounts a story he heard from his elders about the origin of the village’s name, although he says he does not know whether it is true:

author: Unknown
title: Uçum says commission in which Öcalan will take part has been determined
content:
Presidential Chief Adviser and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Legal Policies Board Mehmet Uçum met with journalists at the Turkish Press Federation and made statements regarding the peace and democratization process.




Uçum stated that four subcommittees had been established under the Monitoring and Evaluation Board, which was formed within the scope of the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion.




One of these bodies is the Subcommittee on Disarmament and Strategic Coordination, Uçum said, adding that Abdullah Öcalan would also take part in this subcommittee.




Uçum said that this should not be interpreted differently. He noted that the working space established on İmralı had also been arranged to enable the Kurdish leader to fulfill his role in the process.




October and November could be critical in the next stage of the process, Uçum said, adding that if developments on the ground show progress, the National Security Council (MGK) decision on the process could be finalized by November.




The "Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” known as the “Framework Law,” was passed by parliament with a record number of votes on the night of August 10. title: YRK and HPJ salute the general strike in Rojhilat
content:
The commands of the East Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK) and the East Kurdistan Women’s Defense Forces (HPJ) saluted participation in the general strike on Wednesday on the fourth anniversary of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadi’ (Woman, Life, Freedom) uprising in Rojhilat (East Kurdistan).




The a joint statement on Thursday said:




“We respectfully salute the families of the martyrs of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ revolution and all the patriotic people of Rojhilat Kurdistan. The stance and unity demonstrated by our people at a time when the Iranian regime is exerting intense pressure on the population with all its power are highly valuable and meaningful. Participation in the general strike led by the Kurdish people in Rojhilat Kurdistan on the anniversary of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ revolution has once again demonstrated the determination to defend the gains of the revolution.




As the YRK and HPJ, through this message we would like to express our gratitude to our people for their stance and determination, and once again reaffirm our support for them.”

title: Kurdish child ‘tortured for murder confession’ after IRGC Intelligence arrest
content:
Arzhin Jondi, a 16-year-old Kurdish child from the village of Kuper in Piranshahr, has been arrested by the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and is being tortured and pressured into making a forced confession to involvement in the killing of an IRGC member, an informed source in Piranshahr told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN).




The source said: “After his father died, the 16-year-old lived with his uncle’s family in the village of Kuper. On the evening of 11 September, an IRGC member named Eslam Kak-Darvishi was killed in the village when unidentified armed individuals opened fire on him.”




According to the source, following the killing, Kak-Darvishi’s family destroyed the home of Jondi’s uncle and claimed that the child had been involved in his killing. However, a group called Khori Hiwa had claimed responsibility for the attack.




The source said Jondi had travelled to another village to visit his mother when he was summoned to the local office of the IRGC Intelligence Organisation in Piranshahr on 12 September. He reported to the office accompanied by a family member and was subsequently arrested.




Around the time of his arrest, Iranian state media reported that IRGC Intelligence Organisation forces had arrested the “killer” of the IRGC member, but did not identify the arrested individual.

author: Unknown
title: Uçum points to 16 April for the 2028 elections: Erdoğan to run again
content:
Mehmet Uçum, Chief Advisor to the President and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Council for Legal Policies, discussed the 2028 elections during a meeting with journalists at the Turkish Press Federation.




Uçum said he expects the elections to be held on 16 April 2028, stating: “This date is the anniversary of the referendum through which we transitioned to the presidential system. It has symbolic significance.” Uçum also said that Recep Tayyip Erdoğan would run for the final time.




According to Uçum’s statement, holding the elections on April 16 would mean bringing the existing electoral timetable forward by approximately three weeks. While the regular date for the next general elections is calculated as 7 May 2028, Uçum had previously said that this should not be considered an “early election,” but rather a change of date resulting from the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye (TBMM) deciding to renew the elections.




For the elections to be held on 16 April, the TBMM would need to decide to renew the elections with the votes of 360 members of parliament. Uçum said such a decision could be made in February 2028.

author: Unknown
title: Saint-Martin: I want direct contact with Abdullah Öcalan
content:
The Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began following Abdullah Öcalan’s call on 27 February 2025, is being closely followed in European politics as well as in Turkey and Kurdistan. As debate over the process continues, a notable initiative has emerged from France.




Arnaud Saint-Martin, a sociologist and member of the French National Assembly for La France Insoumise (LFI), has formally applied to meet Abdullah Öcalan on Imrali ahead of his visit to Turkey from 17 to 19 September 2026. Saint-Martin described Öcalan as “one of the indispensable interlocutors” on the Kurdish question and the ongoing process in Turkey, stressing that he should be able to communicate with the outside world and receive visitors. Saint-Martin is currently an LFI member of the French National Assembly.







 







In his formal application to the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which was also sent to the Ministry of Justice and the General Directorate of Prisons and Detention Houses, Saint-Martin said he wanted to hear Öcalan’s views directly on current political developments in Turkey, prospects for peace and democratic dialogue, and a peaceful and democratic solution to the Kurdish question.

author: Unknown
title: HPG warns against those soliciting financial aid in the name of the guerrillas
content:
In a written statement on Thursday, the Press Liaison Center of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG-BİM) said: “Recently, we have received information that in various locations across Turkey and Northern Kurdistan, some persons have been soliciting aid from our patriotic people, businesspeople and various segments of society in the name of the Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas.”




The statement continued: “We have investigated the information received from numerous locations. We have concluded that, at present, no requests for assistance have been made to anyone, either in areas where our guerrillas are present or elsewhere. Therefore, wherever they may be, those making such requests for assistance have no connection with the guerrillas or our movement. On the contrary, we have obtained findings indicating that criminal groups have deliberately been brought into play in this matter and that such misconduct is being carried out by these groups.”




“We call on our patriotic people, our friends and all sections of society not to trust individuals who approach them through notes or other means under any circumstances, and to remain vigilant against anyone requesting financial assistance in the name of the Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas,” the statement concluded.

title: Demirtaş: Developments must be viewed from a historical perspective
content:
Nurettin Demirtaş, a member of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, shared his assessment of the concepts set out in Abdullah Öcalan’s Manifesto for Peace and Democratic Society.




Demirtaş said that rather than taking a snapshot of events as they unfold and interpreting them in isolation, the process should be understood from a historical perspective.




Nurettin Demirtaş said the following:




“Everyone is debating how to understand what is happening today. A significant part of these discussions is genuinely aimed at reaching a proper understanding. Some, however, go beyond the boundaries of criticism and are almost aimed at undermining the process itself. What I would recommend to everyone who is sincerely trying to understand the process is to look at it from a historical perspective rather than simply taking a snapshot of what is happening today, at this particular moment, and interpreting it in isolation. Such a perspective brings us closer to the truth. Why? Because everything happening today has a history.




More accurate conclusions can be reached if events are considered in connection with their past. This is particularly important when we are dealing with a people or a society, because sociological analyses can never be accurate without a historical perspective. author: Unknown
title: Yıldız: AKP is imposing Nazi law in prisons
content:
Hasan Basri Yıldız, a member of the Solidarity Association with the Families of Prisoners (TAYAD) who is 98 percent visually impaired, was arrested in connection with a case dating from 2024. Yıldız was taken to Marmara No. 6 L-Type Prison in Silivri, where he objected to the prison wards being monitored by cameras around the clock. He was subsequently held in an eight-square-metre cell under conditions of isolation and denied access to an exercise yard. Yıldız and his fellow prisoners launched an indefinite hunger strike in protest against these conditions. He was released on 3 September, the 109th day of the hunger strike, and spoke to ANF.




I lost 14 kilos during the 109-day hunger strike, dropping from 62 to 48 kilos




Yıldız, who appeared visibly thinner, said he had lost 14 kilos during the indefinite hunger strike, with his weight falling from 62 to 48 kilos. He said he was detained in January 2026 in connection with an operation targeting TAYAD families in 2024. Yıldız said: “In 2024, they raided the homes of elderly people, some of them 80 years old, and detained them. I was in the village at the time. When I learned that they had come to detain me as well, I returned to Istanbul. Even though I continued living my normal life in Istanbul, a full year and a half after the operation the police put me under surveillance on the grounds that I was ‘wanted’ and detained

author: Unknown
title: Iraqi Ministry of Migration: More than 30,000 people have returned to Shengal
content:
Ali Abbas, spokesperson for Iraq’s Ministry of Migration and Displacement, spoke to Iraqi media about IDP camps in the Kurdistan Region and the number of IDPs who have returned to Shengal.




Ali Abbas said that around 19,000 families, the majority of them Yazidi citizens, are still living in a total of 16 camps in Hewlêr and Duhok.




The spokesperson said that the United Nations has established coordination with the Office of the Iraqi Prime Minister to create the necessary conditions for families to return to Shengal, address the financial crisis, secure the required funding, and increase international efforts in this regard.




Accordingly, field assessments are being carried out in cooperation with local authorities and international organizations to rebuild homes for displaced families in Shengal’s border villages, provide essential services such as water, roads and electricity, and meet the families’ daily needs.




Ali Abbas said that returns to Shengal have increased compared with previous years. He noted that more than 30,000 displaced people have returned to Shengal, Qahtaniya and Sinûnê as a result of improved security and the provision of basic services in these areas.




Ali Abbas added: “Efforts to facilitate returns and close the camps are continuing within the framework of annual plans and the government program. Returning is a decision that citizens can m

author: Unknown
title: Damascus Interim Government releases 49 SDF members
content:
The 49 SDF fighters detained by the Damascus Interim Government have been released.




The most recent releases were SDF fighters Diyar Hisên Mehmûd and Hesen Newaf, who were released on 26 June.




According to information obtained, the interim government is still holding a large number of detained fighters.

author: Unknown
title: Temelli: We need a new vision of socialism and the economy
content:
The Kurdish Political Movement has recently been discussing communes and the communal economy in the context of the municipalities it has won and the economic programme it has developed. A series of conferences have been organised under the slogan “Municipalities are communes, communes are municipalities”, most recently the “Democratic Economy and Economic Organisation Workshop”, organised by the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) in Amed (Diyarbakır).




Work led by the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the DBP has focused on how the commune system and communal economy can be put into practice, as well as the role of local governments and economic organisation within this model.




Sezai Temelli, DEM Party MP for Muş (Mûş), spoke to ANF about the work on communes and the communal economy and their broader significance.




Real socialism failed to transform capitalist modernity’s production model




Temelli said real socialism had failed to transform the production model of capitalist modernity, arguing that merely changing the ownership of capital was not enough.




Temelli said: “At the heart of capitalist modernity’s approach to production lies the accumulation of capital. Capital can only increase in value through surplus value, and an ever-expanding model of production makes greater exploitation and colonialism necessary in the pursuit of ever greater

author: Unknown
title: Alliance of Iranian Kurdistan political parties thanks people for successful general strike
content:
The Alliance of Political Parties of Iranian Kurdistan has issued a statement thanking the people of Kurdistan for their widespread participation in the general strike on Wednesday, 16 September.




The Alliance described the strike as successful despite security pressure and restrictions. The statement said the strike was held on the fourth anniversary of the death of Jina Amini and in remembrance of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” uprising.




The Alliance also thanked dozens of political parties and groups, women’s organizations, civil society groups, political and academic figures, as well as political prisoners who supported the strike, including some who joined through hunger strikes.




The Alliance also expressed appreciation for the support shown by Baluch, Turk, Persian, Turkmen and Arab political groups and figures, saying this solidarity reflected broader support for the action beyond Kurdistan.




The Alliance said it would continue to represent and raise the legitimate demands of the people of Kurdistan and stressed the importance of unity and cooperation in future political and civil activities.

author: Unknown
title: “Jin Jiyan Azadî” win Best Documentary award at 6th Sulaymaniyah International Film Festival
content:
The film “Jin Jiyan Azadî” won the Best Documentary award at the 6th Sulaymaniyah International Film Festival. Directed by Soran Ibrahimi, the film features real-life individuals as its subjects.




Filmed over the course of a few days, the story captures the daily lives of female guerrillas. It also highlights their political and military struggles, their camaraderie, their communal life, and their solidarity. A significant aspect of this story is that it offers the audience an opportunity to gain an intimate understanding of these female guerrillas and their way of life.




The film also aims to showcase the struggle and lives of Kurdish women in the mountains of Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilatê Kurdistan). This struggle is part of a long history of women's resistance and can be viewed as a continuation and complement to the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” movement.




Among these guerrillas are women who have participated in political and military struggles for decades; some have actively taken part in the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” Revolution in Eastern Kurdistan.




The film’s release holds special significance as it coincides with the anniversary of the killing of Jina Amini and the start of the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” Revolution; it directly presents the stories of women whose struggles and resistance are integral to the history of the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” movement.

author: Unknown
title: Mazloum Abdi discusses Kobanê’s security with Aleppo Internal Security Forces Commander
content:
Syrian Presidential Advisor Mazloum Abdi met with Mihemed Ebdulxenî, the Commander of the Aleppo Governorate Internal Security Forces, in Kobanê to discuss security, stability, and the mechanisms for successfully implementing the integration process within the security forces.




During the meeting, which addressed mechanisms for strengthening security and stability, protecting the public, and successfully carrying out the integration process within the Internal Security Forces, issues regarding the enhancement of security operations and the functioning of institutions in the city were discussed.




The meeting stressed the importance of joint coordination and efforts driven by a sense of responsibility in order to safeguard the security and stability of Kobanê and its villages.

author: Unknown
title: General strike in Rojhilat on the fourth anniversary of Jina Mahsa Amini’s death
content:
Numerous cities across Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) are taking part in a general strike on the fourth anniversary of Jina Mahsa Amini’s death. In Sine (Sanandaj), Saqqez, Bane, Piranshar and Mahabad, shops and bazaars remained closed on Wednesday morning. Participation in the strike has also been reported in Mariwan, Shino, Pawe, Diwandareh and Kermanshah.




















The Alliance of Political Forces of Iranian Kurdistan had called for the general strike. The action commemorates Jina Mahsa Amini and the demonstrators killed during the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” revolution, while also protesting the Iranian regime’s ongoing repression. The call urged people to keep shops and markets closed and stay away from work.

Regime forces deployed in cities




Ahead of the anniversary, the Iranian regime responded with arrests and an increased presence of police, Basij militia and Revolutionary Guards. Security and military units were reported on the streets of Sine and Saqqez on Wednesday morning. Riot police and military vehicles were also reportedly deployed in Sine.

content:
On the anniversary of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ revolution, Jina Amini’s mother, Mujgan Eftehari, shared a message on her Instagram account.




Mujgan Eftehari wrote:




“My immortal Jina, my Jina who illuminated the world, the light of my eyes, I was your mother for 21 years. For four years, your memories have brought me comfort like a warm embrace and a mother’s devotion.




I gave birth to you once, and amid the endless pain of your absence, I was born again. Through your life and your existence, you created meaning, and through your departure, you left behind thousands of meanings. I even love the longing I feel for you, because this longing is something you left to me.




My hero,




I believe that one day justice will prevail, and every mother’s heart will be illuminated by the light of truth. Until that day, keep shining through all our nights.”

title: HPJ guerrillas commemorate the martyrs of the ‘Jin Jiyan Azadî’ revolution
content:
On the occasion of the fourth anniversary of the “Jin Jiyan Azadî’ (Woman, Life, Freedom) revolution in Iran and Rojhilat (East Kurdistan), HPJ (Women’s Defense Forces) guerrillas commemorated the martyrs of the revolution.




In memory of Jina Amini, who was killed at the age of 22 by the Guidance Patrol, commonly known as the “morality police,” 22 candles were lit in front of her poster.




The guerrillas then used torches to spell out the slogan “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” and chanted it together.




HPJ Commander: Women must organize to safeguard their gains




Speaking at the commemoration, HPJ Commander Rojîn Fesîh said the following:




“On the anniversary of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ revolution, we commemorate with gratitude all the martyrs of freedom in the person of Jina Amini. Many young people lost their lives during this revolution. We send our greetings to the prisoners who led the revolution from Iranian prisons, represented by Warisha Moradi and Pakshan Azizi.




The ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ revolution is not an ordinary event to be commemorated on just one day each year. ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ is not merely a slogan; it is a philosophy. title: AI: Iran committed crimes against humanity during the suppression of 'Jin, Jiyan, Azadi' uprising
content:
In a landmark new report marking the fourth anniversary of the start of the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadi’ (Woman, Life, Freedom) uprising, Amnesty International warns that those responsible for crimes against humanity committed to brutally crush nationwide protests in 2022 continue to control Iran’s deadly state machinery of repression today.  




The report, 

Architects of Atrocities: State Machinery Orchestrating Crimes Against Humanity in Iran’s 2022 Woman Life Freedom Uprising

 –more than 1,000 pages long – details how Iranian authorities committed the crimes against humanity of murder, torture, enforced disappearance, imprisonment, rape and persecution on political, gender, ethnic and religious grounds in order to crush the uprising. It also documents deadly protest repression operations and command structures, identifying 87 officials who should be criminally investigated for crimes against humanity.  




Amnesty International is calling for an international criminal justice mechanism to be established urgently by the UN General Assembly to ensure Iranian authorities responsible for crimes against humanity are held to account and to deter further atrocities such as the large-scale protest massacres committed on 8-9 January 2026.

title: Released prisoners: We were tortured in the Syrian Interim Government’s prisons
content:
The prisoners released today spoke about the conditions of their detention and their transfers between various prisons, stating that they had been subjected to torture.




Şahîn Osman said he had been held in the Al-Rai and Al-Hasiya prisons after he was arrested by Turkish intelligence agents in Jarablus in November 2024 while traveling to Manbij.




Osman stated that more than 250 prisoners from Hesekê, Afrin, Raqqa, Amûdê, Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî were held in Al-Hasiya prison.




Mistefa Yûnis, from Kobanê, said he was arrested on January 12, 2026, and had been held in various prisons. He was transferred from Homs to Damascus, then to Al-Hasiya prison, and later to Deir ez-Zor and Hesekê.




Ehmed Elî El Casim, from Raqqa, said he was arrested in Latakia on August 10, 2025. He was transferred from Al-Hasiya prison to the Al-Rai military prison, then to a prison in Deir ez-Zor, and finally to Manbij Prison.




El Casim said that prisoners were treated poorly and subjected to torture in the prisons.




Şaban Mihemed, from Afrin, said he was captured by armed groups in 2024 and later handed over to the General Security. He was held in Al-Hasiya prison, where prisoners were subjected to torture.




Şaban Mihemed added that his family in the Mabata district of Afrin did not know where he was being held during his detention.

title: Yazidi Youth Party opens center in Shengal
content:
The Yazidi Youth Party (Partiya Ciwanên Êzidî) has opened a new center in Shengal. The party, which held its founding congress in April, has established its own premises for the first time in the Rojhilat neighborhood.




The opening was attended by party chairman Elî Elyas Osman, members of the Political Bureau, Azad Hisên, co-chair of the Shengal People’s Council, members of the Yazidi women’s movement TAJÊ, and representatives of various institutions.




In his opening speech, Osman said that the party pursues a political and social strategy. “The Yazidi Youth Party is a party for all Yazidis and aims to unite the Yazidi community,” he said, thanking those present for attending.

title: PJAK, YRK and HPJ commemorate the martyrs of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” uprising
content:
The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), the East Kurdistan Resistance Units (YRK), and the Women’s Defense Forces (HPJ) commemorated those who lost their lives in the uprising and the Kurdish freedom struggle on the fourth anniversary of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” revolution.




YRK and HPJ guerrilla fighters visited the Şehîd Arîn and Şehîd Jîrwan cemeteries on Tuesday evening. During a memorial ceremony, they lit candles at the graves and reaffirmed their commitment to continue the resistance for freedom.




In a statement, the organizations recalled how the uprising began following the death of Jina Mahsa Amini on September 16, 2022. The Kurdish woman, who was born in Saqqez, died after being detained by the so-called morality police in Iran’s capital, Tehran. The uprising that subsequently erupted in Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) spread across Iran within a short period of time.




“Jin, Jiyan, Azadî was not merely an uprising against the killing of Jina. It became the voice of women, young people, and all those who rose up for freedom and a free life. The revolution continued through the resistance of the people and became a symbol of the struggle for freedom," the statement said.




During the memorial ceremony, the YRK and HPJ renewed their pledge to “continue on the path of the martyrs and carry on the struggle for freedom and liberation.”

title: Moradi: Jin, Jiyan, Azadî is a project for a free, democratic society
content:
The Freedom for Warisha Moradi Campaign published an article written by Kurdish political prisoner Warisha Moradi, who is being held in Evin Prison, to mark the fourth anniversary of the Jin, Jiyan, Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom) Revolution.




Moradi said Jin, Jiyan, Azadî is not merely the name of a protest, but represents a desire for life, freedom, dignity and human agency, as well as a determination to break down social relations built on power, violence, discrimination and inequality. She stressed that Jin, Jiyan, Azadî is not a process that has ended, but one that continues.




Moradi said women are themselves a driving force for change and that no democratic transformation can succeed without women’s will. She described the repression of women activists and political prisoners, along with the severe sentences imposed on them, as attempts to contain a movement that challenges the foundations of the existing structures of power and social organisation.




She stressed that the struggle does not end at the prison gates and said resistance in prisons and during court proceedings represents a continuation of the choice to pursue a free life. Rather than being a personal matter, she said, this resistance reflects broader public demands for freedom, justice and equality.

author: Unknown
title: Tribute paid to Jina Amini at her grave
content:
Jina Amini was killed by Iran’s “morality police” in Tehran, a group of activists visited her grave in Saqqiz, four years ago.




Today activists released white balloons bearing Jina Amini’s name and the words “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (“Woman, Life, Freedom”) at her grave.




The activists called on the public to take part in this symbolic act on the anniversary of Amini's death and to keep alive her memory and the memory of those who lost their lives for freedom by releasing white balloons.




Another activist who shared footage of the grave visit said: “Jina’s story continues to be told, and her voice echoes in the hearts of those who believe in freedom, dignity, and justice. Jina will never be forgotten. Her memory will endure forever as a symbol of hope and courage. Jina’s name will live on forever.”

title: A prison is still a prison!
content:

Reports have claimed that a two-storey villa with a large garden has been built for Abdullah Öcalan on Imrali. The timing of this report is also significant. It comes at a time when the Turkish state is expected to take steps but has failed to do so. By putting such a story into circulation, attention is being diverted from the state’s failure to act.




According to information we received from DEM Party circles, a new building has been constructed within the Imrali prison complex. The original building where Abdullah Öcalan was held was demolished and replaced with a slightly larger prison building. title: Preparations are underway in Marseille for 6th Sinan Dersim Kurdish Cultural Festival
content:

As part of the program, stalls serving Kurdish cuisine, art exhibitions, and areas featuring Kurdish-language books will be set up. The day-long event is planned to offer visitors both a cultural and gastronomic experience.







 







The stage program will feature numerous artists and groups. Alongside Koma Amed, Kawa Urmiye, Hozan Azad, and Ibo Qamişlo, the ZarokMa children's group, the Kecên Rojê folklore troupe, and the Soul Brasilian Rhythm group will also perform. In this way, Kurdish music and dance, as well as rhythms from different cultures, will come together on the same stage at the festival.




The Festival Preparatory Committee stated that they have been visiting local shopkeepers and families to publicize the event, putting up posters, and making calls for participation through social media.




In a statement, the committee said: “Our most important goal is for the festival to be embraced by broad sections of the community and to achieve strong participation.”




The festival also includes activities specifically aimed at children and young people, and the participation of the ZarokMa group is expected to increase families’ interest.

content:

title: Mother of three martyrs: I am proud of them
content:
Tributes are being held in many cities across Kurdistan, Turkey, and Europe for the guerrillas whose deaths have recently been announced. Rojgirav Amed (Mürsel Nergiz), who was killed in Metina on 13 March 2020, was commemorated at a condolence gathering held in Amed.

First Ilhan left; after he fell as a martyr, Felat left, and before Felat was killed, Rojgirav left. I was in the village. Before Rojgirav left, he called me to central Amed. He told me that he was going to leave. He had already been imprisoned before and had suffered severe torture for about 40 days. When he got out of prison and told me he was going to leave, I didn’t believe him."




Nergiz added: "We stayed together in Amed for 15 days. He told me, ‘I made a promise. I can’t stay here anymore. I can’t go to prison again; I can’t endure that much torture. I’ve made my decision. content:
The Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan) Political Forces Alliance issued a written statement marking the fourth anniversary of the Jin, Jiyan, Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom) Revolution.

As the Political Forces Alliance of Iranian Kurdistan, we attach great importance to this historic period and approach it from a broad perspective, as it became a turning point in strengthening the struggle in Kurdistan and other parts of Iran against the rule of the Islamic Republic. This revolution is a continuation of decades of struggle for freedom and liberation, while also representing women’s struggle for their rights alongside the Kurdish rights movement."

title: Mazloum Abdi meets with representatives of Kurdish parties in Kobanê
content:
Syrian Presidential Adviser Mazloum Abdi and Kobanê Brigade Commander Mahmoud Berxwedan met with representatives of Kurdish parties in Kobanê.




Abdi reviewed developments regarding administrative and security integration in the Kobanê region and said that the state attaches particular importance to the Kurdish cause and respects the distinct characteristics of Syria’s Kurdish regions.




Referring to the efforts of the integration committees on mother-tongue education, Mazlum Abdi said they were working at a high level with the relevant ministries to resolve the issue of education in the Kurdish region and safeguard the right to mother-tongue education in schools in Kurdish areas.




Abdi continued: “We have seen that President al-Sharaa is open on this issue. Education is in a transitional phase. The future will be built on the decisions that are made.”




Regarding the recent events in Kobanê, Abdi said: “The results of the investigation will be shared transparently with the public. Our work is aimed at ensuring the security and stability of the region. Everyone responsible for these events will be held accountable.”

content:
