title: Iraq repatriates 49 imprisoned Iranian citizens
content:
Iran’s Deputy Minister of Justice for Human Rights and International Affairs, Askar Jalalian, spoke to the media about Iraq’s repatriation of Iranian citizens.




Jalalian said that 49 Iranian citizens held in Iraqi prisons had been repatriated to Iran through the Mehran International Border Crossing.




He stated that after the necessary legal and judicial procedures are completed, along with passport and health checks, the persons in question will be transferred to Ilam Central Prison to serve the remainder of their sentences.




Most of the prisoners were reportedly arrested in Iraq on charges related to possession of drugs and prohibited substances or carrying belongings for other people, and were subsequently sentenced to lengthy prison terms.

title: Demonstration outside the Council of Europe calls for freedom for Abdullah Öcalan
content:
Kurds and their supporters demonstrated outside the headquarters of the Council of Europe in Strasbourg, demanding freedom for Abdullah Öcalan and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question. The demonstration coincided with the September meetings of the Committee of Ministers, which supervises the implementation of judgments by the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).




















The rally was organized by the Congress of Democratic Societies of Kurdistan in Europe (KCDK-E) and the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E) as part of the international campaign “Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan – A Political Solution to the Kurdish Question.” Alongside politicians, representatives of Kurdish organizations and activists, members of the European Parliament Domenico “Mimmo” Lucano, Rudi Kennes and Martin Günther also took part in the demonstration.




















The demonstrators called on the Committee of Ministers to press Turkey to implement the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) case law concerning the so-called “right to hope.” At the same time, speakers highlighted Öcalan’s role in the ongoing process for peace and a democratic society and called for conditions that would allow him to fulfill this role freely.

title: Perpetrator of 2022 Paris attack sentenced to seven years in prison for an earlier act of violence
content:
The perpetrator of the December 2022 attack on the Kurdish community center in Paris has been sentenced to seven years in prison for an earlier act of violence. A Paris court found 73-year-old William Malet guilty of a racially motivated attack on a refugee camp in 2021.




On December 8, 2021, Malet attacked a camp in Paris’s Bercy Park with a saber, injuring two people. In court, the former TGV train driver said that he had wanted to injure and frighten the people living there so that they would leave the camp.




In addition to the seven-year prison sentence, the court imposed a five-year ban on Malet possessing or carrying weapons and stripped him of his eligibility to stand for election for five years. He is already being held in pre-trial detention over the 2022 attack.




Trial over Paris massacre set for February 2027




From February 23 to March 8, 2027, Malet is due to stand trial before the Paris Assize Court over the deadly attack of December 23, 2022. On that day, he opened fire on Rue d’Enghien in Paris’s 10th arrondissement, in the immediate vicinity of the Ahmet Kaya Kurdish Cultural Center.




He killed Kurdish revolutionary Evîn Goyî (Emine Kara), musician Mîr Perwer (Mehmet Şirin Aydın) and activist Abdurrahman Kızıl. Three other people were injured.




Following his arrest, Malet said his actions were motivated by a “pathological hatred” of foreigners.

title: Aydar: The law must be implemented and Öcalan’s path opened
content:
The adoption of the framework law has opened a new phase in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, prompting discussions over how the process will move forward and how the law will be implemented. Zübeyir Aydar, a member of the Executive Council of the Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK), spoke to ANF about the process, saying that despite its shortcomings, the law has opened an important door, while delays in its implementation are a cause for concern.




Aydar stressed that conditions must be created for Abdullah Öcalan to play an active role if the process is to advance, adding that the Kurdish question cannot be resolved through a single law. He said the Kurdish people’s identity, language, culture and rights to organise and engage in politics must be guaranteed, while the democratisation of Turkey must also form a central part of any solution.




Honouring the martyrs means honouring the struggle




Aydar reflected on the process, which has been under way for nearly two years, and commemorated the martyrs of the freedom struggle whose martyrdoms were recently announced, drawing attention to the heavy price paid over decades of conflict. He stressed that this legacy must be upheld in the new period and that the struggle must continue through democratic means.




Aydar said: “The people are honouring their martyrs. This is very important. There has been a great struggle

title: HPG commemorates fallen members and honors memorial events in North Kurdistan
content:

author: Unknown
title: PUK President visits Tehran, meets senior Iranian officials
content:
Bafel Jalal Talabani, President of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), is paying an official visit to the Islamic Republic of Iran, accompanied by a high-level PUK delegation.




The visit comes at the official invitation of the Iranian Foreign Ministry.




Talabani and Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, met in Tehran. During the meeting, which was attended by a high-level PUK delegation, discussions focused on the latest political developments and military changes in the region.




Talabani emphasised that problems require peaceful solutions and ongoing dialogue.




He also reiterated the PUK's continuous efforts to establish peace and de-escalate tensions, stating that the Kurdistan Region respects the security and sovereignty of neighboring countries, and that a shared and ancient history binds us together with the Iranian people.




For his part, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran expressed his appreciation for the role of President Bafel and the PUK in their efforts to protect the stability of the Kurdistan Region, Iraq, and the region as a whole.

content:
The issue of Kurdish international representation remains one of the longest-standing problems in Kurdish political history. In the period following the First World War, when the Middle East was reshaped, the Kurds were excluded from the international system and, over the course of nearly a century, remained in fragmented political and legal positions within the borders of different states.




At a time when balances in the Middle East are once again shifting and international diplomacy and institutions are gaining greater importance in terms of regional developments, the representation of the Kurdish people at the United Nations is once again coming to the fore. With the conference to be held in Brussels on 3 October, the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) aims to develop a common position on the representation of the Kurdish people at the UN, establish cooperation at the national and international levels, and determine the steps to be taken in this direction.




At its 24th General Assembly, held on 6-7 June 2026, the KNK put the issue of Kurdish representation at the UN on its agenda and decided to apply for the Kurdish people to be recognized like other nations and represented as observers in UN-affiliated organizations. The conference in Brussels stands out as an important step following this decision, where the next steps in the process will be discussed and the aim will

title: Iran Freedom Congress supports general strike in Rojhilatê Kurdistan
content:
The Iran Freedom Congress announced its support for the call by the Alliance of Political Forces of Rojhilatê Kurdistan for a general strike in the cities of Kurdistan on September 16, marking the fourth anniversary of the killing of Jina Amini and the Jin Jiyan Azadî Revolution.




In a written statement, it said: “As written on her gravestone, Jina became immortal, and her name became a symbol. At the funeral ceremony held at the Ayçî Cemetery in the city of Saqiz, the slogan ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ echoed and became the main slogan of a nationwide serhildan against discrimination and repression. The experience of previous strikes has shown that calls by Kurdish parties rooted in the people have been welcomed by the masses in different cities across Kurdistan. This form of protest was also repeated during the Jin, Jiyan, Azadî serhildan in other cities of Iran. The Iran Freedom Congress considers the general strike a civil and effective step for expressing the people’s demands and resisting repression.”




The statement said that from the suppression of the Jin Jiyan Azadî uprising and the uprisings that preceded it to the unprecedented massacre of people during the January 2026 uprising, the Islamic Republic has resorted to criminal acts to preserve its rule. content:

“Abdullah Öcalan is one of the indispensable interlocutors on the Kurdish question and the ongoing ‘process’ in Turkey. He must be able to receive visitors and communicate with the outside world. We have submitted an official request to visit him at the prison on Imrali Island,” Saint-Martin said.




The French MP also shared the same message on his X account in Kurdish and Turkish.

title: Aydın: The state seeks to prevent mourning from becoming legitimate
content:
The Kurdish Freedom Movement has begun announcing the names of guerrillas whose martyrdoms could not previously be disclosed because of the conditions of war, prompting condolence gatherings and commemorations across Turkey and Kurdistan.




Attempts have also been made to criminalise these gatherings and commemorations, which have drawn mass participation from the Kurdish people. Anthropologist Derya Aydın said mourning is a natural part of conflict resolution and peace processes, noting that the current process is proceeding more cautiously than the 2013–2015 period.




We publish the second part of our interview with Derya Aydın of the Initiative for Respect for the Dead and Justice (IRDJ).




The process is on a tighter knife-edge than in 2013




Some circles close to the government and fascist parties have made provocative statements about the condolence gatherings. Why is the right to mourn met with such hostility at a time when peace is being discussed?




First, if we look at the neglect and indignities inflicted on the dead over the past decade, as well as the rhetoric used to legitimise these practices, we need to recognise that attempts at criminalisation have diminished today. title: PJAK: Iranian regime abducted and tortured one of our members in Kamyaran
content:
The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) issued a statement regarding its member, who was detained by Iranian regime forces on September 9, 2026, in the city of Kamyaran in Rojhilatê Kurdistan.




The PJAK statement said: “On Wednesday, September 9, 2026, our comrade and party member Sîrwan Hebîbî was abducted in the city of Kamyaran in Rojhilatê Kurdistan as a result of a pre-planned trap by security forces of the Intelligence Ministry of the Islamic Republic of Iran. He was subjected to an attack that was in violation of international law and was extremely brutal and inhumane; he was tortured and subjected to violence.“Immediately after being detained, Hebîbî was taken to an unknown location, and despite the time that has passed, no information has been obtained about his health or where he is being held. When our comrade Sîrwan Hebîbî was detained, he was not carrying any weapons or other equipment; he had only visited the city of Kamyaran to carry out his duties and organizational activities.”




The statement added: “In the face of the serious threats to the well-being of our comrade Sîrwan Hebîbî, we call on the people of Rojhilatê Kurdistan, all pro-freedom civil activists in Iran and around the world, and human rights organizations to urgently, carefully and effectively investigate his fate and take a position against these actions.

title: Kongra Star: Women’s will for freedom cannot be suppressed
content:
The Kongra Star Coordination issued a written statement marking the anniversary of the Jin, Jiyan, Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom) Revolution. The statement commemorated the women who lost their lives in the struggle for freedom, including Jina Amini and Şiler Resul.




The statement described Jin, Jiyan, Azadî as more than a slogan, saying it is a philosophy of life that places women’s freedom at the heart of society’s freedom. It said the struggle has spread from Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) and Iran to different parts of the world.




Kongra Star said the Iranian regime has intensified its policies of repression, arrests and executions against women, drawing attention to the resistance of women held in Evin and Qarchak prisons. It expressed solidarity with Zeynab Jalalian, Pakhshan Azizi, Warisha Moradi, Bita Hemmati and Arghavan Fallahi, as well as other women facing the threat of execution.




The statement said femicide and control over women’s bodies are consequences of the patriarchal system and commemorated women who have been killed, including Niloufar Mojaveri. It described compulsory veiling, the criminalisation of women’s freedom of expression and organisation, political arrests and executions in Iran as different aspects of the same policy of repression.

title: Veysi Aktaş: Ongoing dialogue and talks are at a sensitive stage
content:
Hundreds of people gathered in Cologne on Sunday to discuss the peace and democratic society process. At the event held at the Eurosaal, Veysi Aktaş, a member of the Imrali Secretariat, and Ebru Günay, a member of the DEM Party executive board, spoke about the course of the process so far and its current phase.




The event began with a minute of silence for the recently announced fallen members of the Kurdish freedom struggle. Ebru Günay then addressed the historical development of the process and provided an update on its current status. She discussed the steps taken so far by the Turkish state and the Kurdish freedom movement, as well as the latest developments on the prison island of Imrali.






















Aktaş: Öcalan continues his work without interruption




Veysi Aktaş then spoke about Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan’s assessments of the ongoing process. Despite the severe conditions of isolation on Imrali, Öcalan continues his political and theoretical work without interruption, Aktaş said and explained the significance of Öcalan’s paradigm of democratic society for the current phase.




“The process also aims to protect the Kurdish people from renewed policies of annihilation, which they find themselves confronting once again a century later,” Aktaş said. He added that Öcalan’s historical analyses and proposed solutions serve as a fundamental point of refere

title: 17 demonstrators detained during protests in Kobanê released
content:
A total of 17 people, mainly young men, who were detained during protests in Kobanê and subsequently taken to Aleppo have been released last night. The men had been detained by General Security forces of the Syrian transitional government.




Protests had erupted in Kobanê following the abduction and killing of Sîpan Hiznî, a fighter with the Hesekê Brigade. Government forces used force against the demonstrators, resulting in assaults and numerous arrests.




Those who have now been released are Mihemed Necîb Hemo, Azad Celal Osê, Welat Mehmûd Horan, Organ Şukrî Oso, Aras Elaedîn Mişo, Behaedîn Mihemed Bozo, Omer El Hemîd Ehmed, Salih Mihemed Elî, Berxwedan Mihemed Şêxo, Hisên Şêx Mihemed Nebo, Yûsif Mistefa Berkel, Zekeriya Îsmaîl Şêxo, Emar Mehmûd Baqî, Fadil Hecî Heyder, Serdar Mihemed Îsmalî, Ehmed Mihemed Reşad and Zekeriya Îsmaîl Hemo.

title: Hundreds demonstrate in Vienna against attacks in Rojava
content:
Hundreds of Kurds demonstrated in Vienna on Sunday against the killing of Sîpan Hiznî and the recent events in Kobanê. Protesters demanded an investigation, accountability for those responsible, and recognition of the political, linguistic and social rights of the Kurdish population in Syria.




The demonstration began at Karlsplatz. At the start of the protest, a minute of silence was observed in memory of Sîpan Hiznî, the nine people who lost their lives in the fire at Kobanê Prison, and all those who have fallen in the Kurdish freedom struggle.






















Part of a series of attacks against Kurds




Journalist and politician Binyad Cizîrî recalled that Sîpan Hiznî was abducted and killed in Hesekê province on September 10. On the other hand, he added, nine people were killed and many others injured in the fire that broke out at Kobanê Prison a few days later.




Cizîrî said the events should not be viewed as isolated incidents, but as part of a series of attacks and rights violations targeting the Kurdish population of Rojava. Those responsible must be held accountable, he said.




Cizîrî was particularly critical of the policies of the Syrian transitional government. “The events in Kobanê and the deployment of troops from Aleppo to the region show that the principle of Kurdish self-administration is also being rejected,” Cizîrî said. He added that restriction

title: Gülistan Doku case: New detentions over suspected cover-up
content:
A further detention operation has been launched in connection with the suspected femicide of Gülistan Doku in Dersim (Turkish: Tunceli). Detention orders have been issued for eleven suspects, including current and former police officers, on suspicion of destroying or tampering with evidence and interfering with the investigation. On the orders of the Erzurum Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office, simultaneous detentions, searches and seizures were carried out in seven provinces. This is the sixth detention operation since the investigation into the disappearance of the then 21-year-old university student was reopened.




A total of 32 people are now being held in pre-trial detention, including former and current public officials, police officers, doctors and other healthcare workers. Those arrested include Tuncay Sonel, the governor of Tunceli at the time, his son Mustafa Türkay Sonel and his wife Handan Sonel, as well as Çağdaş Özdemir, who was then the chief physician of the state hospital, and Ali Kahraman, the former deputy commander of the provincial gendarmerie.




Suspected organized system of cover-up




Gülistan Doku has been missing since January 5, 2020. The 21-year-old woman, who was from Amed (Diyarbakır), was in her second year studying Early Childhood Education at Munzur University in Dersim. Her family reported her missing the following day, but the search efforts

author: Unknown
title: Mazloum Abdi discusses prison incident with the Kobanê regional director
content:
Syrian Presidential Advisor Mazloum Abdi met with Kobanê Regional Director Îbrahîm Muslim at the regional directorate’s headquarters.




The meeting addressed details of the fire that occurred two days ago at Kobanê Prison, in which 9 detainees were killed, and 17 others were injured. It was also reported that appropriate measures to prevent similar incidents were discussed.




Îbrahîm Muslîm said that the role of judicial and security institutions should be strengthened and coordination improved in order to protect local residents and stabilize the region.




Mazloum Abdi, meanwhile, stated that an independent and transparent investigation should be launched and that those responsible should be punished.




Abdi also emphasized the need to maintain security in the city, strengthen the role of administrative and judicial institutions, and accelerate the process of integrating security, judicial and administrative institutions.

title: Jina Amini’s father: People’s love has brought thousands more children into our family
content:
Four years after Jina Mahsa Amini was killed while in custody in Tehran, her father, Amjad Amini, shared a message on social media marking the anniversary of his daughter’s death.




Amjad Amini said that their pain has not diminished, as Jina remains, for them, the daughter who brought joy into their lives. He noted that his daughter’s name had transcended the boundaries of their family following her death, saluting the solidarity and affection shown by society.




“We had one daughter, and they took her away from us. But people’s love has brought thousands more children into our family,” Amjad Amini said.




Stating that time has a different meaning for a mother and father who have lost their daughter, Amini said that four years had done nothing to ease their pain.




Jina’s photograph, her memories and even hearing her name bring back what happened, her father said, expressing his hope that the truth would be brought to light.




At the end of his message, Amini said that Jina’s name and memory would remain with them until their last breath, adding: “This land holds many lives within it; no one knows all of its secrets.”

title: Öcalan: We dedicate our efforts to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the struggle
content:
Abdullah Öcalan issued a message for the fallen Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas.




The Kurdish leader’s message reads as follows:




“I commemorate our martyrs with respect.




We dedicate all our efforts toward building a Democratic Republic and a democratic society to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in this struggle.




Upholding their legacy is one of the most fundamental responsibilities on the path we are walking.




Our theoretical and practical efforts for peace, and the great peace initiative, are a requirement of the profound respect and loyalty we owe to their cherished memory.




These efforts are an expression of keeping their memory alive and ensuring that their sacrifices are not left unanswered.




As part of our responsibility to be worthy of the memory of those who fell on this path, we must transform the conditions of war and conflict into an honorable peace as soon as possible.




We respectfully bow before the memory of all martyrs and once again reaffirm our determination to keep their struggle and ideals alive.




While extending my condolences and deepest sorrow to all the families, I reiterate that our efforts will continue tirelessly and with determination so that future generations may live in freedom.




Abdullah Öcalan




September 13, 2026




Imrali”

title: Iranian regime threatens the family of Jina Amini
content:
Iranian regime forces are pressuring the family of Jina Amini and the families of those killed during the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” Revolution in the city of Saqiz in Rojhilatê Kurdistan, and are opposing all of their activities and preparations.




Iranian regime forces are threatening the relatives of those who were killed during the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” protests, warning them not to gather at their graves and preventing them from calling on the public to participate in planned demonstrations.




It was reported that the families of those killed in the protests have refused to accept this. Meanwhile, regime forces have been deployed throughout the streets and avenues of the city of Saqqez.




Jina Amini (22), who was from the city of Saqiz in Rojhilatê Kurdistan, was killed by Iran’s morality police on 16 September 2022, on the grounds that she had not covered her hair. Following her death, protests began throughout Rojhilatê Kurdistan and across Iran.

content:

During the meeting, a number of issues concerning recent developments in Kobanê and the security and administrative situation in the region were discussed.




Speaking about the matter, Ilham Ahmed stated that an investigation committee had been established into the recent incidents in Kobanê, particularly the incidents that broke out in Kobanê Prison.




Ilham Ahmed emphasized that necessary and appropriate measures should be taken to prevent such incidents from happening again.




Offering condolences to the families of the fallen and wishing a speedy recovery to the wounded, Ilham Ahmed called on the people of Kobanê to participate in the farewell ceremony for the fallen with a sense of responsibility.




On 11 September, tensions escalated following a demonstration held to condemn the killing of Sipan Hizni, a fighter with the Syrian Ministry of Defense, and numerous young people were detained. title: Over 100,000 students face violation of the  right to education in Rojava
content:
“I am Kurdish, my language is Kurdish”, “Our language is our identity, culture and dignity”, “It is our right to learn in our own language”, “We want our language”, “There is no life without language” and “The Kurdish language will live forever."




These slogans have echoed through the streets of Hasakah (Hesekê), Kobanê, Dirbêsiyê, Tirbespiyê, Qamishlo, Amûdê, Çilaxayê, Dêrik, Til Temir and many other cities since 27 August. Students and teachers have been marching with banners for days, stressing that education in Kurdish is a fundamental right. Among the most prominent participants in the protests are the children of fighters martyred in the Rojava Revolution. They too stress that Kurdish is not simply another school subject or a language spoken at home, but the language of their identity, culture and future.




The scale of what has been achieved is considerable: over the past 14 years, more than one million students in Rojava have received education in their mother tongue as part of what has been described as a “language revolution”. That achievement, however, is now under threat from the interim government in Damascus.




The Ministry of Education of the Syrian Interim Government issued a decree ending Kurdish-language education in schools run by the Autonomous Administration and replacing it with three hours of elective Kurdish lessons. Students, teachers and parents

title: Molina: The law is a first step, Öcalan’s status must be resolved
content:
The search for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question continues as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began following Abdullah Öcalan’s historic call on 27 February 2025. As part of the process, a framework law recently submitted to and adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM) was subsequently signed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and entered into force after being published in the Official Gazette.




The law is regarded as an important step towards advancing the process, but has also drawn criticism for failing to provide a fundamental and comprehensive solution to the Kurdish question.




Developments in the process are being closely followed internationally as well as in Turkey, Kurdistan and the wider region. Fabian Molina, a member of the Swiss Federal Parliament who has closely followed the Kurdish question for many years, spoke to ANF about the latest developments in the Peace and Democratic Society Process.







 







The law is only a beginning




Molina said he was closely following developments in Turkey and described the law adopted by the TBMM as an important first step on the path towards lasting peace.




Molina added: “It is important that a consensus has been reached on this legislation. This law marks the beginning of a process towards genuine, just and lasting peace. In that sense, I believe the law adop

title: DEM Party calls on Parliament to recognize the right to education in one’s mother tongue
content:
The DEM Party’s Commission on Language, Culture and the Arts said in a written statement: “As the new academic year begins, Turkey's education system is facing multidimensional crises, ranging from child poverty and insufficient funding to the commercialization of education, the transformation of children into workers, and gender-discriminatory policies. One of the most meaningful steps that can be taken to address these crises is to provide millions of children with the opportunity to receive education in their own mother tongue.”




The statement continued: “Today, millions of children, particularly Kurdish children, begin their educational lives without having access to this opportunity. Yet education in one’s mother tongue is a guarantee that a child can develop as a free individual with their own identity, language and culture.




Turkey has been going through an important process for the past two years. The Peace and Democratic Society Process aims for a democratic order in which every individual and community lives together on the basis of equal and dignified citizenship and their inherent rights. A democratic, pluralistic and egalitarian social climate is possible only when the rights of different languages and cultures are guaranteed. title: KJK: Let us build democratic socialism through the 'Jin, Jiyan, Azadî' Revolution
content:

content:

In the period following the adoption of the law, it is of great importance that mutual practical steps be taken within the framework of this responsibility and that the relevant committees begin actively carrying out their work.

author: Unknown
title: Rocket attack targets residences at Komala camp near Sulaymaniyah
content:
Residences housing members of the Komala of the Toilers of Kurdistan (Komeleya Zehmetkêşên Kurdistanê) in the village of Zirguêz near Sulaymaniyah were targeted in a rocket attack overnight. The attack, believed to have been launched from Iran, occurred at around 3:10 a.m. According to initial reports, there were no injuries or fatalities.




A source close to the organization linked the attack to the general strike announced for Wednesday in Rojhilat (East Kurdistan). The source said the attack demonstrated the Iranian regime’s fear of the mobilization planned for September 16.




On the fourth anniversary of the death of Jina Mahsa Amini and the anniversary of the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” revolution, political forces in Rojhilat have called for a general strike on Wednesday. Shops and markets are expected to remain closed, and the public has been urged to take part in the action. Numerous organizations have joined the call.

title: Mourning declared in Kobanê
content:
A fire broke out at Kobanê Prison at around 2:00 a.m. on Saturday, September 12, killing nine people. Today, two days of mourning were declared in the city for the victims.




Since early this morning, shops and businesses across Kobanê, particularly those in the central market, have remained completely closed as a sign of mourning and respect for the deceased.




All business activity across the city has come to a halt, and Kobanê’s streets remain empty.




A funeral ceremony for the nine victims had been scheduled for today, but was postponed due to the mourning period. The ceremony will instead be held on Monday at 5:00 p.m.

title: Aydın: People who suffered so much loss stand firmly for peace
content:
The Freedom Movement has begun announcing the names of those who lost their lives in clashes, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years. The announcements, which have been made over the past month, have been followed by condolence gatherings and commemorations in many cities across Turkey and Kurdistan.




The large turnout at these gatherings has been subject to attempts at criminalisation, particularly by circles opposed to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which have issued statements to this effect.




ANF spoke to anthropologist Derya Aydın from the Initiative for Respect for the Dead and Justice (IRDJ) about the right to mourn and hold condolence gatherings during conflict-resolution processes, examples from around the world, and the significance of the gatherings now being held across Kurdistan and Turkey.




We need to use the term “right” carefully




Let me begin with this: What is the right to mourn, and what does it mean?




At the time it emerged that the remains of members of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) had been transferred from Garzan Cemetery in Bitlis (Bedlîs) to Istanbul, both what had happened there and the neglect and indignities inflicted on politically contested dead bodies were largely discussed within a legal framework. Both the violations and the arguments against them were confined to questions of legislation. That was in 2018, and

author: Unknown
title: Sheybani and Fidan meet in Damascus
content:
Syrian Transitional Government Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met in Damascus.




The meeting addressed strengthening political, economic and security cooperation between the two countries, reactivating joint high-level committees, and increasing trade volume.




Shaibani said that a unified national army should be established and that weapons should be held exclusively by the state, while Fidan said that all armed forces should be integrated under the authority of the state and that Syria’s unity and sovereignty should be preserved.




Israel’s activities in southern Syria were also discussed. Shaibani called on Israeli forces to withdraw to the boundaries that existed before January 8, 2024, and to comply with the 1974 ceasefire agreement.




Condemning Israel’s attacks, Fidan said: “Israeli policies are a major obstacle to stability and positive developments in Syria.”

author: Unknown
title: MSD Co-Chair: We will never give up our language and identity
content:
Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) Co-Chair Leyla Qereman visited the condolence tent set up for Sîpan Hizni, a fighter from Hesekê Brigade who was killed on September 10 after being abducted by an armed group. Leyla Qereman delivered a speech at the condolence gathering and stressed that no one could strip Kurds of their rights or silence their demands for freedom.




The MSD Co-Chair also called for efforts to prevent attempts that seek to sow discord among the peoples of the region and to preserve social peace.




Addressing the issue of integration, Qereman stressed that integration “does not mean the end of the Kurdish existence,” adding: “Language is part of our existence and identity, and we will never give up this demand.”

author: Unknown
title: Call for general strike in Rojhilat on anniversary of Jina Amini’s death in Iranian police custody
content:
22-year-old Kurdish woman Jina Mahsa Amini was arrested by the “morality police” in Tehran on September 13, 2022, for allegedly violating Islamic dress codes. Three days later, on September 16, she died as a result of violence suffered while in custody. Amini’s death sparked a large-scale, unprecedented protest movement that became known under the slogan “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom) which thus transcended the country’s borders and became one of the symbols of a global protest movement.




On the fourth anniversary of the death of Jina Amini, the Alliance of Political Parties of Iranian Kurdistan issued a written statement calling for a general strike across Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) on Wednesday, September 16.




To support the strike, the alliance called on shopkeepers to close their businesses and markets, while urging residents to take part in the action by staying at home. The alliance also called on political parties, civil society organizations and various social groups to support the general strike.




The alliance emphasized that the general strike is not merely a way of commemorating those who lost their lives during the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom] resistance.




The strike, it said, is also “a peaceful act of civil protest reflecting the Kurdish people’s ongoing resistance and their political and national demands.”

title: Sulaymaniyah Asayish: 22 ISIS members were arrested in Halabja
content:
The Sulaymaniyah General Directorate of Asayish Operations announced that two ISIS cells had been dismantled in a series of operations carried out over the past 96 hours by forces from the General Directorate of Asayish Operations and the Halabja Asayish Directorate.




The operations resulted in the arrest of 22 covert ISIS members. A large cache of heavy, medium and light weapons, as well as hand grenades, military binoculars and ammunition reportedly intended for use in terrorist attacks planned for September, was also seized.




The investigation is ongoing, and all information and documents related to the cells are currently in the possession of the General Directorate of Asayish Operations and the investigating judge.




On the other hand, a simultaneous operation targeting a senior ISIS leader was carried out in Xurmal on the night of September 12. A clash broke out during the operation, but the senior ISIS figure was detained without any loss of life.




The statement added that all confessions and documents would soon be made public.

title: Shengal People’s Council: A democratic Syria is possible through recognition of all peoples' will
content:
The Shengal People’s Council issued a written statement on the latest developments in Rojava. The Council extended condolences to the family of Sîpan Hiznî, a Kurdish member of Hesekê Brigade who was killed in Hesekê, and to the families of the nine people who lost their lives in the prison fire in Kobanê.




According to the Council, the developments in Rojava and Kobanê demonstrate that the interim government in Damascus rejects the will of the people and is seeking to obstruct mother-tongue education, which has been in place for 14 years. The Council described the killing of Sîpan Hiznî as a manifestation of hostility toward the Kurdish people.




Criticizing the intervention by Damascus government forces against the protests, the People’s Council said these policies were provocations aimed at pitting communities against one another, adding: “This approach is a continuation of the Baathist mentality and is unacceptable in every respect.”




The statement said that the deployment of forces to Kobanê amounted to a denial of the people’s free will and called on Kurds and supporters of freedom to oppose these policies.




The Shengal People’s Council reiterated its support for the people of Rojava, stressing that education in the mother tongue is a red line for them.

author: Unknown
title: DEM Party delegation meets Öcalan on Imrali
content:
The Imrali delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) met with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on the Turkish prison island of Imrali on Sunday. The visit had originally been announced for Monday, September 14.




The delegation consisted of MPs Pervin Buldan and Mithat Sancar, as well as lawyer Faik Özgür Erol from the Asrin Law Office in Istanbul. They traveled to Imrali on Sunday and returned to Istanbul after meeting with Öcalan. No information has yet been released regarding the duration or content of the meeting. The delegation is expected to issue a statement on the talks.




Buldan, Sancar and Erol last visited Öcalan on Imrali on August 2. At the time, the talks focused particularly on the future course of the peace and democratic society process. Öcalan described the Framework Law, which had yet to be adopted at the time, as an important step and said it would mark the beginning of a democratization process of historic significance.




The Framework Law has since been passed by the Turkish parliament. Öcalan had also emphasized that not all issues would be resolved by the law and that all parties involved would need to assume responsibility for the further development of the process.

author: Unknown
title: School boycott for Kurdish-language education continues in Rojava
content:
Students’ protests against restrictions on Kurdish-language education in Syria are continuing. In Girkê Legê, Rimêlan and the surrounding villages, students have stayed away from school for six days. They are refusing to attend classes under the new directives issued by the Syrian Ministry of Education and are demanding the right to continue their education in their mother tongue.




The protests in Hesekê province began on September 6 and have continued ever since. Students in several towns have taken part in demonstrations and other forms of protest, saying they do not accept the Education Ministry’s decision.




The protests were sparked by new regulations for the school year under which Kurdish is to be limited to three hours of instruction per week in Rojava and other Kurdish regions of Syria. Students, teachers, educational institutions and civil society organizations in Rojava reject the downgrading of Kurdish from a language of instruction to a single school subject.

author: Unknown
title: Thousands bid farewell to Sîpan Hiznî in Hesekê
content:
Thousands of people from the Cizîrê region bid farewell to Sîpan Hiznî (Samî Şêxmûs Hiso), a fighter with the Hesekê Brigade. Hiznî was abducted and killed by an armed group in Hesekê on Thursday. The perpetrators filmed the killing and shared the footage on social media along with anti-Kurdish threats. The killing sparked protests in several cities across Rojava. In Kobanê, General Security forces intervened against demonstrators and detained numerous people.




The burial took place on Saturday at the Şehîd Dijwar Cemetery in the village of Dawudiyê in Hesekê.







“Symbol of humanity and freedom”




The funeral ceremony began with a minute of silence for those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle. Welîda Botî, from the Council of Families of Martyrs, offered condolences to the family and called for the achievements of the Rojava Revolution, won at great sacrifice, to be defended.




Xerîb Hiso, co-chair of the PYD, then described the killing of Sîpan Hiznî as a “barbaric and inhumane act.” He said Hiznî had fought against the “Islamic State” (ISIS) and, in doing so, had defended not only his own people but also people from different ethnic and religious communities.

title: MSD calls for urgent, independent investigation on the “dangerous developments” in Hesekê and Kobanê
content:
The Syrian Democratic Council (MSD or SDC) released a statement expressing “deep concern” over the dangerous developments in the city of Kobanê and several areas of northeastern Syria. These developments follow the killing of the fighter Sipan (Sami Sheikhmous Hisso) and the protests and other troubling events that followed. Several civilians and members of the security forces were injured. A number of prisoners also lost their lives after a protest began inside the prison and a fire was set there. The protest was in response to the forced transfer of prisoners to Aleppo and was followed by further deaths among those held in the prison.




“At the same time, what happened in Kobanê must not be treated as an isolated incident or reduced to a single account of events. The deaths and injuries among detainees and prisoners, along with the harm suffered by civilians and security personnel, require an urgent, independent, and transparent investigation. The investigation must establish what happened, determine responsibility clearly, and ensure that anyone found responsible is held accountable, regardless of their position or affiliation,” the statement said.

title: "1001 signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace" declaration announced
content:
Prepared under the leadership of women, intellectuals, artists, academics, workers, and young people with the aim of contributing to efforts for peace, equal citizenship, and a democratic solution in Turkey, the "1001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace" declaration was presented at the Eyüp Sultan Culture and Arts Center. Numerous academics, politicians, journalists, and representatives of civil society organizations also spoke at the event.




Setting out with the message, "Real fairy tales begin when societies do not give up dreaming of their own future," the signatories stated that in Eastern and Western tales, the number "1001" symbolizes inexhaustible hope and the patient transformation of darkness into light; they called for the defense of social peace against a climate of conflict and division. Journalist Nezahat Doğan read the declaration.




The declaration included the following points:




"- Within the context of the ongoing peace and resolution process in Turkey, we initially support disarmament and the complete removal of all forms of violence from the country's and society's agenda.

title: Karakum: My son's right to medical treatment is being denied
content:
It has emerged that Emir Karakum, who has been held at Marmara No. 2 L-Type Prison for 2.5 months on the pretext of the NATO Summit, is also being denied his right to medical treatment. Speaking to ANF, Emir Karakum’s mother, Birsen Karakum, pointed out that her son, who has a serious spinal condition and needs surgery, has not had his request to be transferred to a hospital granted.




My son has been in jail for 2.5 months on the assumption that he would take part in a protest




Around 150 people, including students and lawyers, who were detained in the witch hunt launched under the pretext of the NATO Summit have been held in prisons for months unjustly and unlawfully. Birsen Karakum, the mother of Emir Karakum, one of those detained, summarized the extent of the “enemy law” being applied against opposition groups by saying: “My son Emir was detained on June 23 and arbitrarily imprisoned on June 26, on the assumption that he would take part in a protest ahead of the NATO Summit. He has been held arbitrarily at Marmara No. 2 L-Type Prison for 2.5 months based on this assumption.”




Pointing out that her son’s right to medical treatment is also being denied in addition to his loss of freedom, Karakum said: “Emir has a serious condition affecting his spinal cord. He normally lives with us in Samsun, but he used to travel to Istanbul frequently for treatment. Most recently,

title: KNK: Tensions in Rojava must stop, independent investigation must be conducted
content:
The Executive Council of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a statement regarding the killing of Sîpan Hiznî, a fighter with the Hesekê Brigade, and the subsequent events in Kobanê, which resulted in the deaths of eight people and injuries to 18 others. The KNK called for an open, independent and impartial investigation to be conducted in order to establish all aspects of what happened.




The statement by the KNK Executive Council said that “the killing of Sîpan Hiznî, a fighter with the Hesekê Brigade, and the sharing on social media of footage showing the brutal manner in which the murder was carried out by the perpetrators have caused great shock and anger among our people.




Popular demonstrations were held in many cities and districts of Rojava Kurdistan. Those taking part in the demonstrations condemned the brutal incident and demanded that justice be served and those responsible be held accountable.”




The KNK added: “As part of these events, what happened in Kobanê — including the pursuit and detention of some demonstrators by forces affiliated with Damascus and Turkey-backed groups and attempts to take them to Aleppo Prison, followed by the incidents at and around Kobanê Prison that resulted in eight deaths and 18 injuries — is an extremely dangerous development, particularly given the condition of the wounded, some of whom are in serious condition.

title: Koma Amara releases new album ‘Hevala Min’
content:
Koma Amara has released its new album Hevala Min, dedicated to the Martyrs of Kurdistan Freedom.




Produced in collaboration between Awazgeha Delîla and Jê Muzik, the eight-song album includes ‘Derwêşo’, ‘Sara û Bîşeng’, ‘Vengê Avzem’, ‘Hevala Min’, ‘Çar Heval’, ‘Roniyê Me’, ‘Roj û Zarok’ and ‘Kezî’.




Xwezan Harun, a member of the Movement for Culture and Art (TEV-ÇAND) who contributed to the production of the album and wrote the song ‘Hevala Min’, spoke to ANF about the project.




We must keep the memories of our martyred comrades alive




Xwezan Harun greeted the people, listeners and his comrades and spoke about the process of preparing the album. 




Harun said: “We had been working on our album Hevala Min for some time, and now we have reached the end of that process. We are sharing the album with our listeners. As is known, the martyrdom of comrades whom we knew personally, fought alongside on the front and worked with has recently been announced. We extend our condolences to all the families of the martyrs and bow with respect before their memory. Most of the songs on our album were prepared for our martyred comrades. We shared many memories together; they were wonderful comrades, but sadly they have left us and reached the truth. We must keep their memories alive. title: Bartın: Society must take ownership of the peace process
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP Öznur Bartın assessed the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying it could not be approached solely through the question of “which rights will be recognised”. She said discussions should also focus on what society can create with the resources available to it, which institutions it can develop and how it can build its own future.




The Peace and Democratic Society Process has also brought greater attention to how the Kurdish question is reflected in people’s everyday lives, beyond legal reforms and political decisions. Discussions are taking place across a wide range of areas, from language and education to science, local government, the economy, employment, and the organisation of women and young people.




Bartın said the debates and initiatives emerging through the process should not focus solely on steps expected from the state. She stressed the need to concentrate equally on what society itself can achieve in everyday life and the areas in which it can develop its own structures.




Bartın said the process should not be confined to high-level politics, negotiations or legislative reforms in Parliament, stressing that lasting peace would be possible only if people had a say in their own communities and strengthened their capacity for social organisation.

content:

The statement said: “The Kobanê Martyrs’ Families Council strongly condemns, with deep anger and sorrow, the actions that took place in our city last night, including arbitrary arrests, the intimidation of civilians, and racist rhetoric that violated the dignity of our people and Kurdish identity.




Last night, a convoy belonging to the Internal Security Forces entered the city of Kobanê from Aleppo. Throughout the night, it drove around the streets, arbitrarily arresting civilians, treating local residents disrespectfully, and using racist rhetoric. These practices constitute an outright attack on the dignity of the city and the safety of its residents and cannot be justified on any security grounds.”




The statement added: “Subsequently, the Internal Security Forces, under the command of Officer Majdeddin al-Sheikh, attempted to forcibly transfer the detainees from the city’s prison to another location. In response to this attempt, a group of detainees inside the prison resisted and started a fire. As a result of the fire, nine detainees were martyred and many others were affected by smoke. title: Condolence ceremony was held for Sîpan Hiznî
content:
Dozens of residents from Hesekê, tribal elders from the region, and a delegation from the interim government attended the condolence ceremony held for Martyr Sîpan Hiznî in the village of Micercei in Hesekê.




Following a minute of silence, Ebdulxenî Oso, a member of the Democratic Union Party (PYD), gave a speech in which he said: “The events taking place in the region, including the killing of Sîpan Hiznî, are being carried out by the Turkish state and individuals affiliated with the interim government. The killing of Sîpan Hiznî has nothing to do with the tribe or society. What happened in Kobanê is connected to this situation.”




Oso said that the issue of the Kurdish language is one of the fundamental demands of the Kurdish people and that it should be officially recognized.




Speaking afterward, Sheikh Ekrem Mehşûş, an adviser to the Al-Jabour tribe, said that the crime committed does not represent the tribes, customs, or traditions of the region. He said the perpetrators should be punished as soon as possible, and warned that the integration process would also be affected if those responsible were not punished.

title: KNK: Kurds should support the resistance of the people of Rojava
content:
The Language, Education, Culture and Arts Committee of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a statement regarding the Transitional Government in Damascus’ restrictions on mother-tongue education in Rojava and the resistance of the people of Rojava.




In its statement, the KNK said that hundreds of thousands of people in Rojava take to the streets every day to demand their rights, and stated that they support these legitimate actions.




Reminding that education in one’s mother tongue is a universal and inalienable right, the KNK called on the Syrian Transitional Government to immediately halt its anti-democratic attacks on mother-tongue education and recognize this natural right.




The statement called on Kurds in the four parts of Kurdistan, Kurds living abroad, and international and humanitarian organizations to support the cause and struggle of the people of Rojava.




The statement also said: “The right to education in one’s mother tongue is an inalienable right, and the people of Rojava will continue their struggle until this demand is crowned with victory.”




At the end of the statement, the KNK called for mother-tongue education to be guaranteed by law.

author: Unknown
title: Fire at Kobane Prison: 9 killed, 16 injured
content:
A fire broke out at a prison in Kobane. According to initial reports, 9 detainees lost their lives and 16 others were injured, some of them seriously.




 




The injured were taken to hospitals in Kobane for treatment.




 




The cause of the fire is not yet known, and the relevant authorities are continuing their investigation. Kobane’s Internal Security Forces are expected to issue a statement regarding the incident.




 




The fire at the Kobane prison broke out following public protests in the city. Protesters were demanding an investigation into the abduction and killing of Defense Ministry member Sami Hiso in Heseke.




 




General Security Forces intervened against the protesters and detained several young people from the city.




 




According to sources in the region, General Security Forces have begun surrounding the city.

author: Unknown
title: Amed’s concrete towers threaten its historic skyline and community life
content:
Amed (Diyarbakır) is rapidly losing a culture of urban life that developed over millennia within its city walls, courtyard houses and narrow streets. A city that has witnessed civilisations, wars, migrations and natural disasters over thousands of years is now overshadowed by concrete blocks rising into the sky and the social fragmentation they bring with them. The rapid spread of high-rise development in Amed in recent years is reshaping the city’s collective memory, social relations and skyline.




Amed historically had a horizontal urban culture. Basalt-stone houses with courtyards and gardens, streets where neighbours’ doors opened onto one another, and neighbourhood solidarity built around shared water sources were among its most distinctive features. The 1965 Development Plan, which allowed apartment construction outside the city walls, followed by regulations that provided a legal basis for multi-storey reinforced-concrete buildings even within the walled city, marked the first major rupture in this horizontal urban memory. Over time, outlying neighbourhoods such as Rêzan (Bağlar), Peyas (Kayapınar) and Bajarê Nû (Yenişehir) filled first with informal housing built by impoverished people migrating from rural areas, and later with rapidly expanding and largely uncontrolled apartment development.

content:
Murat Mıhçı, a member of the Central Executive Board of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), said the framework law proposed as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process should not be viewed solely in terms of peace between Kurds and Turks. Describing the law as a historic opportunity for Turkey’s democratisation, Mıhçı said the first steps should include the release of ill prisoners and the creation of conditions in which political actors can freely engage in politics both inside and outside the country.




Mıhçı said mother-tongue rights, equal citizenship, stronger local government, civil society and the expansion of political space were among the key elements of democratic transformation. He added that abandoning policies of war would also bring significant economic and social benefits. Mıhçı said the process should reach a positive stage within two or three years and stressed that even the next six months would be critical.




The framework law is a historic opportunity for Turkey’s democratisation




Mıhçı said he regarded the framework law as highly significant for the history of the region, adding that the broad political consensus behind it was the result of a long struggle.




He argued that it would be wrong to view the law solely as a means of establishing peace between Kurds and Turks.

title: Amed residents: Let us honour our martyrs and their struggle
content:
The Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER) organised a collective condolence gathering for those martyred in the freedom struggle at the Geterler Wedding and Conference Hall in the Rezan (Bağlar) district of Amed (Diyarbakır). Photographs of the martyrs and Abdullah Öcalan were displayed at the venue, where the gathering will continue for three days.




Thousands of people from different parts of the city visited the condolence gathering and offered their condolences to the families. Residents who spoke to ANF stressed the importance of honouring the memory of the martyrs and called on the public to attend the gathering.







 







It is now our duty to honour the martyrs




Emin Kılıç, who visited the condolence gathering, said the Kurdish people had reached an important stage in their struggle for freedom and that political struggle had now come to the fore. He said the martyrs had played a major role in bringing the struggle to this point and stressed that honouring their memory was a duty for everyone.

author: Unknown
title: The political economy of electoral choices in Kurdistan
content:
Reading the economy in Kurdistan solely through relations of production and consumption means overlooking the heart of the issue. For more than a century, the economic structure has been shaped as an extension of a state policy aimed at breaking the political will of the Kurdish people. Patterns of capital accumulation, the system of land ownership, the distribution of public investment and the organisation of the labour market were never “neutral” technical decisions. They were direct political choices. Discussing the political economy of Kurdistan therefore means examining the tools through which the regime of denial continues to operate today.




The Kurdish Freedom Movement has consistently argued that the conventional discourse of development, “bringing investment” to the region, “incentive packages” and “development agencies”, addresses the consequences rather than the source of the problem. Poverty does not stem from Kurdistan’s “underdevelopment”, but from a deliberate colonial division of labour. Kurdistan has historically been assigned the role of a source of cheap labour and raw materials and an area of low-intensity production. This order has been sustained through the transfer of economic benefits in return for political loyalty.

title: Şahin: Portraying the Freedom Movement as anti-Alevi is propaganda
content:
Writer Mehmet Şahin assessed the Kurdish Freedom Movement’s relationship with the Alevi community and the struggle waged between 1986 and 1993 in and around Maraş (Mereş), Malatya (Meletî), Adıyaman (Semsûr) and Antep (Dîlok).




Şahin’s book Engizek’ten Esintiler (Echoes from Engizek) examines the guerrilla struggle and attempts at liquidation during this period. He said the book was not simply an account of the guerrilla movement but also shed light on the sociological structure of the region.




The book is not simply a guerrilla narrative




Şahin said his memoir-biography Engizek’ten Esintiler sheds light on an important period of social history, focusing on events between 1986 and 1993 in Malatya, Adıyaman, Gurgum (Maraş) and the surrounding areas, a region referred to as Tolhildan Province.




Şahin said: “Engizek’ten Esintiler, a memoir-biography, goes beyond a conventional guerrilla narrative and sheds light on an important period of social history. Although the Freedom Movement has its own account of these historic lands, it is not widely known among the broader public. This work seeks to address that gap.




The book offers a multifaceted analysis of both the difficulties faced and the extraordinary struggle waged by the Kurdistan Freedom guerrillas between 1986 and 1993 in Malatya, Adıyaman, Gurgum (Maraş) and the surrounding areas, which were defined as Tolhil

author: Unknown
title: Mencî Akbaş: We will follow in the footsteps of our martyrs
content:
For the past two weeks, the identities of guerrillas who fell as martyrs on different dates and in different regions were announced.




Condolence gatherings were held for the fallen guerrillas in many places, particularly in the provinces of Kurdistan. Aryen Sozdar (Mizgîn Akbaş), a guerrilla who fell as a martyr in Heftanîn on 27 July 2019, was also commemorated at a condolence gathering held in Amed. Hundreds of citizens, as well as the families of martyrs, attended the gathering.




Mencî Akbaş, the mother of Aryen Sozdar, said she was proud of her daughter and added: “We will follow in the footsteps of our martyrs to the last drop of our blood. We will not cry for them; we have given them our word. I said I had two conditions: either betrayal or martyrdom. I will never accept betrayal. I hold my head high and am proud of her martyrdom. I do not cry for my martyr. Our martyrs are immortal. We will follow in the footsteps of our martyrs to the last drop of our blood. All of us, even the baby in the cradle, will follow in the footsteps of our martyrs. We will not follow traitors or dishonorable people; we will not sell ourselves for three pennies or worldly possessions. Even if they offered us the whole world, we would not sell our honor or dignity."

title: Kurds commemorate their martyrs in Serhat region
content:
Commemorative events continue across the cities in Serhat region for those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle at different times and whose deaths were announced in recent days and weeks.

VAN

title: People of Maxmur commemorate the martyrs of the freedom struggle
content:
A commemoration for those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle was held at the self-administered Şehîd Rûstem Cudî refugee camp in Maxmur, Southern Kurdistan. Numerous residents gathered at the institution representing the families of the martyrs.




After the names and biographies of Avesta Fîraz Herekol, Îsmaîl, Ronahî Bilikî, Botan Çiyayî, Zerîn Şoreş, Têkoşer Mehmed, Rojbîn Asya, Çekdar Cudî, Elî Çîçek, Bêrîtan Rûken, Hacer Hîlal, Çiya Vîetnam Cûdî, Mizgîn Tetwan, Birûsk Amed, Çekdar Melek, Tekîn Hemzo Harûn, Rojhat, Evîn Feraşîn, Aras Piling Goyî, Rojda Fîkret, Qehreman Botan, Zinar Osyan and Andok Cîhan were read out, Bedran Pîranî, Co-Chair of the Maxmur People’s Council, addressed the gathering. He recalled the heavy sacrifices made in the struggle for a free life in Kurdistan.




“In order to live freely on our own land, we have had to pay a heavy price. The price of freedom is very high,” Pîranî said. Those we commemorate here today lost their lives at different times and in different places, but all had left their mark on history. They are all children of this people.”




“No one can deny the Kurdish people anymore”

author: Unknown
title: Repression against women in Iran continues
content:
The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) highlighted the ongoing repression of women by the Iranian state in a report it published.




It was reported that Seba Sedifi, a member of the Baha’i faith who was detained by security forces yesterday outside her home in Tehran, was first taken to the Jenatabad Prosecutor’s Office to begin serving her finalized three-year-and-five-month prison sentence, and was then transferred to Qarchak Prison in Varamin to serve her sentence.




Seba Sedifi was also detained in January 2022. She was taken to Branch 2 of the Evin Prosecutor’s Office and was released approximately one and a half months later on bail of 1.5 billion tomans.




Meanwhile, it was announced that Perîsa Kemali Merdikani, a political prisoner and geography student who suffers from a serious intestinal and digestive illness, had been sentenced to 11 years in prison and two years of exile. Perisa Kemalî Merdikanî was transferred from Yazd Prison to Bandar Abbas Prison without prior notice.




Mutehere Gonabadi, a former member of the Tehran University Council who had previously been sentenced to 21 months in prison on charges of “propaganda against the system,” was also reportedly transferred from Qarchak Prison to Evin Prison.

title: Nebi Yavuz dies after more than 30 years in prison
content:
Former political prisoner Nebi Yavuz has died in Mardin after a serious illness. The Kurdish man from Nusaybin was imprisoned in 1993 and spent more than 30 years in Turkish prisons. He was not released until July 5, 2023.




Following his release, Yavuz underwent medical examinations. He subsequently received treatment after doctors suspected pancreatic cancer. After his health deteriorated significantly around two months ago, he was admitted to the state hospital in Kızıltepe district, where he was diagnosed with stage-four pancreatic cancer.




Yavuz died at the hospital on Friday morning. After the necessary formalities were completed, he was laid to rest in the rural neighborhood of Kûrûka Bûhûrî in Nusaybin. Hundreds of people attended the funeral ceremony, along with representatives of political parties and democratic civil society organizations.




Speaking at the condolence gathering, Nilüfer Elik Yılmaz, Mardin Provincial Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), expressed her condolences to Yavuz’s family and said they would always be grateful to Nebi Yavuz and the comrades with whom he struggled.




Release delayed by several months

title: Ekrem İmamoğlu sentenced to 2 years and 1 month in prison and banned from politics
content:
The imprisoned and ousted Istanbul Metropolitan Mayor, Ekrem İmamoğlu, has been sentenced to two years and one month in prison for alleged insult. The court also imposed a political ban on the former presidential candidate of the Republican People’s Party (CHP).




The history of the case is noteworthy: İmamoğlu had already been acquitted twice on the same charge. The case concerns remarks he made about Şadi Yazıcı, the former mayor of Istanbul’s Tuzla district. The hearing took place on Friday in a courtroom on the grounds of Marmara Prison in Silivri, where İmamoğlu is being held.




İmamoğlu alleges political interference




İmamoğlu rejected the accusation of insult. The case stems in part from his description of Yazıcı as “nezaketsiz” — meaning impolite or disrespectful. He said he had not intended to insult Yazıcı but was responding to the conduct of the AKP politician.




In court, İmamoğlu placed the trial in the context of the numerous criminal proceedings he has faced in recent years. “For the past two years, I have had to deal not only with my political rivals, but with one court case after another. Today, I am a defendant in a total of 13 different cases,” he said.

title: Three-day commemoration for the martyrs begins in Şırnak
content:
Three-day commemorative events honoring those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle have begun in the province of Şırnak and several of its districts. On Friday, relatives of the martyrs, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and many other people gathered in the city center as well as in Silopi, Idil, Uludere and Beytüşşebap.




The events are organized by MEBYA-DER, an association representing families of the martyrs. Photographs of the martyrs are displayed at the commemoration sites, along with banners reading “Şehîdên me rûmeta me ne” (Our martyrs are our honor) and “Şehîd ronahiya rêya me ne” (The martyrs are the light of our path).




Hundreds attend commemoration in Şırnak

Participants commemorated those who lost their lives during different phases of the freedom struggle with the slogan “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal).

title: The state-sect alliance: Political engineering of religion in Kurdistan
content:
Since the founding of the Republic of Turkey, the state apparatus, officially associated with the principle of “secularism”, has in practice maintained an uninterrupted relationship with networks of religious orders and communities. In Kurdistan in particular, this relationship went beyond the question of religion and the state, becoming a direct instrument of assimilation, control and low-intensity warfare.




In the tradition of the Kurdish Freedom Movement, religious orders have been regarded as a second front operating alongside the state’s direct instruments of coercion, including the army, gendarmerie and village guard system. Their role has been to manufacture consent, sanctify obedience and reshape collective memory.




The historical roots of religious orders, the role they have assumed in Kurdistan, their organic integration with the state under the Justice and Development Party (AKP), and their efforts to reshape the social order are increasingly coming to light.




The Republic’s hidden partner




Official historiography maintains that the Republic completely dismantled religious orders through legislation enacted in 1925. Yet the founding cadres of the state never abandoned pragmatic alliances with religious sheikhs and aghas, particularly as a means of maintaining control in Kurdistan.

title: A Kurdish fighter of Hesekê Brigade brutally killed after abduction
content:
26-year-old Sîpan Hiznî was killed by an armed group after being abducted in the Hesekê area. The perpetrators filmed the killing of the young Kurdish man and subsequently circulated the footage on social media. The videos show Hiznî having his throat cut. Additional footage shows his body and contains threats against Kurds. Members of the Arab Al-Baggara tribe have been named in connection with the killing.




Hiznî, whose full name is reported as Samî Şêxmûs Hiso, lived in the Muftî neighborhood of Hesekê. He was a member of the Hesekê Brigade and had previously fought with the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). As part of the integration process, his unit was incorporated into the Syrian army as a brigade.




Hemo: Several suspects arrested




Sîpan Hemo, Syria’s Deputy Defense Minister for the Eastern Region and a former YPG commander, condemned Hiznî’s killing as a “brutal and treacherous crime” and extended his condolences to the family. “Sîpan was a fighter with the Hesekê Brigade and served for years to protect the security of the region and its people,” Hemo said.




According to Hemo, the relevant security forces have arrested several people involved in the killing. The search will continue until all those responsible have been apprehended and brought to justice, he added.

title: Mother searching Garzan for her loved ones leaves final wish
content:
Families are continuing their struggle to recover the remains of their relatives from Garzan Cemetery in the village of Oleka Jor, in central Bitlis (Bedlîs), after the cemetery was bombed and destroyed in 2017 and the remains of 267 people buried there were exhumed and taken to Istanbul. Lütfiye Oruç spent years searching for the remains of her children. Her final wish was: “Whatever happens, bring them back, even if all that remains are their bones.”




Garzan Cemetery was bombed from the air by the military in 2017 and subsequently destroyed with excavators. The remains of 267 guerrillas buried in the cemetery were exhumed and taken to Istanbul. It later emerged that the remains had been buried at a site in Kilyos, prompting families to embark on a years-long struggle to recover their loved ones.




Hundreds of families have still been unable to recover the remains of their relatives despite providing DNA samples.







 







Lütfiye Oruç was among the mothers who spent their lives struggling to recover the remains of their children. Years after finding the remains of her children, she laid them to rest in Garzan Cemetery, only to lose them for a second time when the cemetery was bombed.




Her son Serhat Oruç said his mother continued searching for her children’s remains until her final breath. He said, “My mother’s final wish became a gravestone for us.”

title: 59 people executed in Iran and Rojhilatê Kurdistan in six months
content:
Human Rights Watch issued a statement concerning executions in Rojhilatê Kurdistan and Iran.




The statement said that at least 59 political prisoners had been executed in Rojhilatê Kurdistan and Iran over the past six months. Of these, 29 were people who had recently taken part in protest demonstrations, while three had been detained during the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” Revolution protests.




The organization stated that some of those executed were under the age of 18.




It was also reported that five people were executed in public in an effort to instill fear among the population.




The organization also drew attention to another issue, stating that 29 of the cases had no connection to the recent events and that the individuals had been sentenced to death under the pretext of “war.” It said that their statements had been obtained under pressure and torture and that they had subsequently been sentenced to death.

title: IHD’s Erdoğan: New-type prisons deepen isolation
content:
Policies governing the imprisonment of political prisoners in Turkey have gone far beyond the deprivation of liberty, developing into a systematic regime of isolation and rights violations. The growing number of complaints in recent years, reports documenting rights violations and testimonies from prisoners indicate that isolation, barriers to healthcare, restrictions on communication and the arbitrary extension of prison terms are being implemented as deliberate state policy. Seriously ill prisoners in particular remain caught between the Forensic Medicine Institute and the police authorities, with some denied release despite medical reports stating that they are unfit to remain in prison, posing a direct threat to their right to life.




Lawyer Yusuf Erdoğan, Co-Spokesperson of the Central Prison Commission of the Human Rights Association (IHD), spoke to ANF about the deepening regime of isolation in prisons, the architecture of new-type prisons, the unlawful practices of Administration and Observation Boards and the situation of ill prisoners.




Erdoğan said political prisoners were labelled as “dangerous” and as “people who must be kept away from society” from the moment they were detained and arrested.




Political prisoners are subjected to isolation from the outset
